signals.title: [Fix] response_cost_calculator ignores custom_pricing for providers with response cost
signals.text: ## Relevant issues When custom per-token pricing is configured via `litellm_params` (e.g., `input_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_token`), providers like OpenRouter that include `usage.cost` in their response body silently override the custom pricing. The `custom_pricing` parameter on `response_cost_calculator()` is never checked before the provider cost early return. ## Summary ### Failure Path (Before Fix) `response_cost_calculator()` extracts the provider-reported cost from `_hidden_params["additional_headers"]["llm_provider-x-litellm-response-cost"]` and returns it immediately — before checking whether `custom_pricing=True`. This means any provider that reports cost in the response (currently OpenRouter chat and image generation) will bypass custom pricing, discount, and margin logic in `completion_cost()`. ```python # cost_calculator.py – response_cost_calculator() if hasattr(response_object, "_hidden_params"): response_object._hidden_params["optional_params"] = optional_params provider_response_cost = get_response_cost_from_hidden_params(...) if provider_response_cost is not None: return provider_response_cost # ← returns before checking custom_pricing ``` **Concrete example:** Setting `input_cost_per_token=0.00015` / `output_cost_per_token=0.0006` (KRW) on an OpenRouter model — spend is recorded as OpenRouter's USD `usage.cost` instead of the configured custom price. ### Fix Add `if not custom_pricing:` guard around the provider response cost block. When `custom_pricing=True`, the function falls through to `completion_cost()` which already handles custom pricing, discount, and margin correctly. ```python if hasattr(response_object, "_hidden_params"): response_object._hidden_params["optional_params"] = optional_params if not custom_pricing: provider_response_cost = get_response_cost_from_hidden_params(...) if provider_response_cost is not None: return provider_response_cost ``` - `custom_pricing=None` (default) and `custom_pricing=False` → existing behavior preserved - `custom_pricing=True` → skips provider cost, uses `completion_cost()` path ## Testing 3 new unit tests added to `tests/test_litellm/test_cost_calculator.py`: | Test | Scenario | Expected | |------|----------|----------| | `test_custom_pricing_skips_provider_response_cost` | `custom_pricing=True` + provider cost exists | Custom pricing used, provider cost ignored | | `test_provider_response_cost_used_when_no_custom_pricing` | `custom_pricing=False` + provider cost exists | Provider cost returned (existing behavior) | | `test_custom_pricing_without_provider_response_cost` | `custom_pricing=True` + no provider cost | Custom pricing via `completion_cost()` (existing behavior) | Full `test_cost_calculator.py` suite: **38/38 passed**, no regressions. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test

signals.title: fix(auth): apply temp_budget_increase on cache-hit path
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #25760 — `temp_budget_increase` was applied only on the DB-fetch path, so cache hits enforced the stale base `max_budget`. On multi-replica deployments backed by Redis, replicas that didn't run the original DB fetch would intermittently see e.g. `Max budget: 2.0` instead of `102.0`. ## Root cause In \`litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py\`, \`_update_key_budget_with_temp_budget_increase\` was called inside the DB-fetch block only. The cache-only check (\`get_key_object(check_cache_only=True)\`) returned a token without ever applying the increase. A second, latent issue: the helper mutated \`valid_token.max_budget\` in place. The in-memory cache stores object references, so simply moving the call onto the cache-hit path would compound the increase across requests. ## Changes - \`_update_key_budget_with_temp_budget_increase\` now returns a \`model_copy\` and never mutates its input. Returns the same instance unchanged when there's nothing to add (no temp increase, expired, or \`max_budget is None\`). - The call moves to the convergence point right before the budget-enforcement checks, so both cache-hit and DB-fetch paths apply it. ## Test plan New test file: \`tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_temp_budget_increase_caching.py\` - [x] Helper does not mutate input - [x] Repeated calls do not compound (3x calls all return base + temp, input untouched) - [x] Returns same instance when no temp increase - [x] Returns same instance when expiry has passed - [x] No-op when \`max_budget is None\` - [x] \`_user_api_key_auth_builder\` cache-hit path applies the increase (the original bug) and leaves the cached token reference at its base value - [x] Existing tests in \`test_user_api_key_auth.py\` and \`test_proxy_utils.py\` still pass
signals.author: kiyeonjeon21

signals.title: feat(mcp): opt-in short-ID tool prefix to keep MCP tool names under the 60-char limit
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Internal: customers with long MCP server names (e.g. `customer_internal_jira_onprem`) were hitting the 60-character upper bound that some model APIs enforce on tool names, because every MCP tool emitted by LiteLLM is prefixed with the server name (`-`). ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2127 ## Summary Add a new opt-in environment variable `LITELLM_USE_SHORT_MCP_TOOL_PREFIX` that switches the MCP tool prefix from the (potentially long) human-readable server name / alias to a deterministic three-character base62 ID derived from the server's `server_id`. ``` default mode: github_onprem-get_repo short mode: Xy7-get_repo ``` We keep the prefix concept (so semantic filtering and other features that need to distinguish "this tool came from an MCP server" still work) — the only thing that changes is the *length* of the prefix. ## Why three base62 chars? - `62**3 = 238_328` distinct IDs — the chance of a real local tool name happening to start with the exact prefix LiteLLM assigned to a given MCP server is negligible in practice. - The IDs are short enough that prefixed tool names stay well under 60 characters even for long upstream tool names. - Derivation is **deterministic** (`SHA-256(server_id)` → first three base62 chars), so the prefix is stable across processes / workers / restarts without any persistence layer. ## Collision resolution (commit 2) Two distinct `server_id` values can natural-hash to the same three-char prefix. With 62³ ≈ 238k slots the birthday bound is ~488 servers for 50% collision probability, so a proxy hosting >100 MCP servers has a non-trivial chance of seeing one in practice — and a collision means tool names from two different servers share a routing key. Mitigation: - `compute_short_server_prefix(server_id, attempt=N)` folds an attempt counter into the SHA-256 seed so rehashes are deterministic. - New `MCPServer.short_prefix` field caches the resolved (post-dedup) prefix on the model so it stays stable across the process lifetime. - `MCPServerManager._assign_unique_short_prefix` walks attempts `0..N` until it finds an unused prefix in the combined registry. Logs an INFO breadcrumb on rehash. - Wired into every registration site (`load_servers_from_config`, `add_server`, `update_server`, `reload_servers_from_database`). Reload carries the previously-resolved prefix forward so the prefix doesn't churn on a no-op reload. - `get_server_prefix` and `iter_known_server_prefixes` both prefer the cached value. No-op when the env var is disabled. ## Backwards compatibility - Default is **off**. When the flag is unset behaviour is byte-for-byte identical to today. - The lookup map (`tool_name_to_mcp_server_name_mapping`) registers **every known prefix form** for each tool — alias, server_name, server_id, and the short ID — so old clients holding cached long-prefixed tool names continue to route correctly even after the flag is enabled. - `_get_mcp_server_from_tool_name` accepts any of those forms. - The path-based router (`/mcp/{server_name}` and the `//mcp` alias) accepts the short ID via `iter_known_server_prefixes`. - The OpenAPI tool-listing path now filters by `get_server_prefix(server)` instead of `server.name` so spec-backed servers benefit too. The plan is to flip the default in a future release and remove the gate after a deprecation window — customers will be notified ahead of time. ## Files changed - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/utils.py` — new `compute_short_server_prefix` (with `attempt` parameter), `is_short_mcp_tool_prefix_enabled`, `iter_known_server_prefixes`. `get_server_prefix` honours the flag and prefers the cached `short_prefix`. - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py` — `_create_prefixed_tools` registers all known prefix forms; `_get_mcp_server_from_tool_name` resolves any of them; OpenAPI listing filters by the active prefix; new `_assign_unique_short_prefix` resolves collisions and is called from every registration site. - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py` — URL-scoped server matching uses `iter_known_server_prefixes`; permission check resolves the canonical server name from the tool name first. - `litellm/types/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py` — new `MCPServer.short_prefix` field caching the dedup-resolved prefix. - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_short_mcp_tool_prefix.py` — 29 new tests covering helpers, env-flag parsing, manager-level emission, reverse-lookup tolerance, the 60-char length guarantee, and collision rehashing. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added testing in `tests/test_litellm/`. - [x] All MCP unit tests pass locally (588 passed; the single failure is the unrelated optional `semantic_router` dep being missing in this environment). - [x] My PR's scope is isolated to the prefix mechanism. - [ ] Greptile review. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes - New env var `LITELLM_USE_SHORT_MCP_TOOL_PREFIX` (truthy values: `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`). - Deterministic three-character base62 prefix per MCP server when enabled, with collision-safe rehashing and per-server caching. - Routing layer is tolerant of every prefix form for forward / backward compatibility. [Slack Thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/D0AUCPA0MLN/p1777420784703239?thread_ts=1777420784.703239&cid=D0AUCPA0MLN)

signals.title: feat(spend-logs): opt-in suppression of stack traces in spend-tracking error logs
signals.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2704 ## Summary Spend-tracking error paths log full multi-line stack traces on every 4xx/5xx and transient DB error. Customers running the proxy at log level `INFO` are seeing these tracebacks dominate downstream log volume even though they have no actionable signal — Sentry already receives the exceptions via `proxy_logging_obj.failure_handler`. This PR adds a new opt-in env var, `LITELLM_SUPPRESS_SPEND_LOG_TRACEBACKS`. When it is truthy and the proxy logger is at `INFO` (or higher), spend-tracking error paths emit a single concise `ERROR` line and drop the traceback. At `DEBUG`, the full traceback is still preserved so operators can troubleshoot without unsetting the env var. Sentry / `failure_handler` flow is unchanged. ## Implementation New helper `litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.spend_log_error_logger.spend_log_error(message, *args, exc=None)`: - Reads the env var fresh each call (so dynamic flips work). - Suppresses traceback only when env var is true **and** logger is not at DEBUG. - Otherwise behaves like `verbose_proxy_logger.exception` (active exception's traceback attached). Wired through the spend write hot path: - `litellm/proxy/db/db_spend_update_writer.py` — `update_database`, `_update_key_db`, `_update_user_db`, `_update_team_db`, `_update_org_db`, `_update_agent_db`, `_update_tag_db`, `_update_daily_spend` batch upsert, both `_commit_spend_updates_to_db_with_redis` and `_commit_daily_tag_spend_to_db_with_redis` redis-fallback paths. - `litellm/proxy/hooks/proxy_track_cost_callback.py` — `_PROXY_track_cost_callback` outer except. - `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py` — `get_logging_payload` outer except. - `litellm/proxy/utils.py` — `update_daily_tag_spend` and the spend-logs queue monitor. The pre-existing `verbose_proxy_logger.debug(..., traceback.format_exc())` call sites in `_batch_database_updates` are left as-is — they only emit at `DEBUG`, so `INFO` users were never seeing them. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit` (relevant suites: `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/`, `tests/test_litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/`, `tests/test_litellm/proxy/hooks/test_proxy_track_cost_callback.py`, `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py` — 294 passed) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes - New module `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_log_error_logger.py` exposing `spend_log_error()` and `should_suppress_spend_log_tracebacks()`. - Replaced 14 stack-trace-emitting log sites in the spend-tracking write path with `spend_log_error()`. - New unit test file `tests/test_litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/test_spend_log_error_logger.py` (15 tests) covering env-var gating, log-level interaction, default-on traceback behavior, and `exc=` vs. active-exception attachment. - Updated `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_db_spend_update_writer.py::test_update_daily_spend_logs_detailed_error_on_batch_upsert_failure` to assert against the new ERROR-level emission. ## Configuration ```bash # Opt in (default: off, fully backwards compatible) export LITELLM_SUPPRESS_SPEND_LOG_TRACEBACKS=true ``` When unset or set to `false`, behavior is identical to `main`. Linear Issue: [LIT-2704](https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-2704/suppress-spend-log-stack-traces-when-log-level-is-info)

signals.title: feat(proxy): proactive model deprecation alerts and `/model/deprecations` endpoint
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Provider sunset dates ship in the registry but stay invisible - Operators find out a model died when calls fail - No lead time to test and migrate replacements How it solves it: - New `GET /model/deprecations` buckets configured models by urgency - Daily Slack alert lists deprecated and imminent models, behind a 24h pod lock so a multi replica fleet sends it once - Per deployment `model_info.deprecation_date` overrides the registry ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin running a fleet of deployments has no way to see which of them a provider is about to sunset 1. They hit GET http://localhost:4000/model/info with the master key and read back pricing, context windows, and modes 2. The payload carries no provider sunset dates, only whatever they typed into `model_info` themselves, so they keep routing traffic to a dying model 3. The provider retires it and their app starts getting hard failures on POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with no prior warning After: the same admin gets the sunset dates up front, and Slack nags them daily while there is still time to migrate 1. They hit GET http://localhost:4000/model/deprecations with the master key 2. They get back three lists, `deprecated`, `imminent`, and `upcoming`, each entry naming the model as they configured it, the date, days remaining, and the provider 3. They re-bucket without touching config by hitting GET http://localhost:4000/v1/model/deprecations?warn_within_days=90, which pulls anything sunsetting inside 90 days into `imminent` 4. With Slack alerting turned on they also get a daily message titled "Model Deprecation Warning" listing the deprecated and imminent models, at High severity once any date has passed 5. For a model whose sunset date is not in the registry yet, they set `deprecation_date` under `model_info` on that deployment and it shows up in the same lists ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2701 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The user flow above was QA'd before and after on a live proxy, recorded and posted in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0B302ZJU05/p1786400555199479?thread_ts=1786400555.199479&cid=C0B302ZJU05). The before half runs `litellm_internal_staging` at 19c914066b, where `/model/deprecations` 404s and `/model/info` carries no registry sunset dates, and the after half runs 4e7e2f53b9 off the same config. Per step screenshots are in a comment below Captured at 8f1aea5e0a (the endpoint is unchanged since) against a live proxy with five deployments: `claude-opus-4-1` (registry date already passed), `gemini/imagen-4.0-generate-001` (7 days out), `openai/sora-2` (45 days out), an Azure deployment whose `base_model` carries no date, and one deployment with a hand set `model_info.deprecation_date` ```shell $ curl -s -X GET "http://localhost:4000/model/deprecations" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" { "deprecated": [ { "model_name": "opus-4-1", "litellm_model": "claude-opus-4-1", "deprecation_date": "2026-08-05", "days_until_deprecation": -5, "status": "deprecated", "litellm_provider": "anthropic" } ], "imminent": [ { "model_name": "imagen-4", "litellm_model": "gemini/imagen-4.0-generate-001", "deprecation_date": "2026-08-17", "days_until_deprecation": 7, "status": "imminent", "litellm_provider": "gemini" }, { "model_name": "internal-legacy", "litellm_model": "openai/gpt-4o", "deprecation_date": "2026-08-20", "days_until_deprecation": 10, "status": "imminent", "litellm_provider": null } ], "upcoming": [ { "model_name": "sora-2", "litellm_model": "openai/sora-2", "deprecation_date": "2026-09-24", "days_until_deprecation": 45, "status": "upcoming", "litellm_provider": "openai" } ], "warn_within_days": 30, "checked_at": "2026-08-10T23:01:31.944560Z" } ``` `internal-legacy` is the override case: the registry has no date for `openai/gpt-4o`, the date comes from `model_info.deprecation_date` on that deployment. The Azure deployment is correctly absent because neither its `base_model` nor its model string carries a date Widening the window moves `sora-2` from `upcoming` into `imminent`, no restart needed ```shell $ curl -s "http://localhost:4000/v1/model/deprecations?warn_within_days=90" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"deprecated": ["opus-4-1"], "imminent": ["imagen-4", "internal-legacy", "sora-2"], "upcoming": [], "warn_within_days": 90, "checked_at": "2026-08-10T23:01:40.790791Z"} ``` Auth is enforced the same way as the rest of the model management routes ```shell $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" "http://localhost:4000/model/deprecations" 401 ``` Bugbot's startup race concern (the daily loop can start from config load before the router exists, then skip the boot-time alert and silently sleep a full day) was QA'd live with a tiny local HTTP sink standing in for the Slack webhook and a config containing one already-deprecated model. On the before leg at 4e7e2f53b9 the boot-time alert still arrived seconds after startup: on a stock config nothing between the loop starting and the router being assigned truly yields the event loop, so the race needs an unusual config that actually suspends in that window. The fix is still worth having as deterministic hardening, and after it at 2278118493 the loop polls for the router every 30 seconds instead of reading it once, with the boot-time alert reaching the webhook 3 seconds after the proxy reported healthy ```shell $ python3 sink.py 41735 & $ SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=http://127.0.0.1:41735/webhook litellm --config qa_deprecation_config.yaml --port 41733 & $ until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:41733/health/liveliness; do sleep 2; done; date +%H:%M:%S 08:35:00 $ cat sink_head.log 2026-08-12T08:35:03 POST /webhook {"text": "Alert type: `model_deprecation_warnings`
Level: `High`
...
Message: *Model Deprecation Warning*

*Already deprecated:*
• `dead-alias` (provider: unknown, deprecates 2020-01-01, already deprecated 2415d ago)

Plan migrations to a supported model. ..."} ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Coverage is only as good as the registry dates - Slack alert fires daily, enabled by default with alerting on - Deployments sharing a model group and date report once - Alert loop re-reads router and alert types every pass - First alert waits for the router in 30 second polls - One pod alerts per day, via a redis pod lock - Without redis every pod alerts, same as the daily report - Daily timer starts at boot, so restarts re-alert Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/680cda1b74c34159899de6c6ae064ef6 Requested by: @mateo-berri <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 4e7e2f53b98f5737e43a27c5137e9ad6567c71ac. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9ac267a1b87043189b066e7a44373a8e

signals.title: fix(anthropic/chat): place tool `strict` at top level (#27490)
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #27490. Anthropic only enforces tool-call `strict` when it is set as a sibling of `name`/`input_schema` on the tool object; nested inside `input_schema` it is silently ignored. Currently `_map_tool_helper` forwards `strict: true` through the `input_schema` filter (because `AnthropicInputSchema`'s TypedDict listed `strict` as an allowed key), so callers think strict-mode is engaged but Anthropic emits unconstrained tool args. ## Changes - `litellm/types/llms/anthropic.py` - Drop `strict` from `AnthropicInputSchema` (it is not a valid Anthropic input-schema key). - Add `strict: Optional[bool]` to `AnthropicMessagesTool` (the correct location). - `litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py` (`_map_tool_helper`) - Extract `strict` from the canonical OpenAI location (`tool.function.strict`). - As a fallback, accept it from the legacy nested location (`tool.function.parameters.strict`) — preserves the prior behavior of "callers who put it in parameters still get it forwarded" without the silent-drop bug. - Set it on the tool top level (`_tool["strict"]`) only when the caller opted in (no `strict: false`/`null` injected by default). - The `input_schema` filter now strips `strict` from the schema (since it was removed from the allowed keys), so the wire format matches Anthropic's spec. ## Tests Three regression tests added to `tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/test_anthropic_chat_transformation.py`: - `test_map_tool_helper_lifts_strict_from_function_to_tool_top_level` — canonical OpenAI placement (`tool.function.strict`) → lifted to tool top level, absent from `input_schema`. - `test_map_tool_helper_lifts_strict_from_legacy_nested_parameters` — legacy/upstream-nested placement (`tool.function.parameters.strict`) → same outcome. - `test_map_tool_helper_omits_strict_when_caller_did_not_set_it` — when no caller opts in, no `strict` key appears on the tool (no behavior change for non-strict callers). ## Wire-format diff Before (silently ignored by Anthropic): ```jsonc {"tools":[{"name":"...", "input_schema":{"type":"object", "...":"...", "strict":true}}]} ``` After (enforced by Anthropic): ```jsonc {"tools":[{"name":"...", "input_schema":{"type":"object", "..." :"..."}, "strict":true}]} ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: fix(adapter): handle GenericResponseOutputItem in translate_response
signals.text: ## Relevant issues https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/27492 — discovered while using `use_chat_completions_api: true` with DeepSeek and Kimi models through the LiteLLM proxy. Responses API bridge (#19558 follow-ups) added `GenericResponseOutputItem` to the output union but `translate_response` was never updated to handle it. ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [ ] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes ### Root cause When `use_chat_completions_api: true` bridges Anthropic /v1/messages requests to chat completions, the response is converted to a `ResponsesAPIResponse` by `LiteLLMCompletionResponsesConfig.transform_chat_completion_response_to_responses_api_response()`. This calls `_extract_message_output_items()` and `_extract_reasoning_output_items()`, which produce `GenericResponseOutputItem` **Pydantic instances** — not OpenAI SDK native types (`ResponseOutputMessage`, `ResponseReasoningItem`) and not plain dicts. `translate_response()` in `responses_adapters/transformation.py` iterates `response.output` checking: 1. `isinstance(item, ResponseReasoningItem)` — no match (different type) 2. `isinstance(item, ResponseOutputMessage)` — no match 3. `isinstance(item, ResponseFunctionToolCall)` — no match 4. `isinstance(item, dict)` — **no match** (Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` subclasses do not satisfy `isinstance(obj, dict)`) All content is silently dropped. No error, no log — just `content: []` in the returned Anthropic response. ### Fix Add an `isinstance(item, GenericResponseOutputItem)` branch to `translate_response()` that handles both `"message"` (→ text block) and `"reasoning"` (→ thinking block) output types, matching the same shape produced by the chat completions bridge. ### Tests The existing `TestTranslateResponse` tests use `MagicMock` for all output items. `MagicMock` passes `isinstance(mock, AnyType)`, so the type mismatch was invisible. Added 3 tests that construct **real** `GenericResponseOutputItem` Pydantic instances: - `test_generic_output_item_message_pydantic` — message → text block - `test_generic_output_item_reasoning_pydantic` — reasoning → thinking block - `test_generic_output_item_reasoning_plus_message_pydantic` — mixed → both blocks ### Proof of fix Before: ``` % claude --model deepseek-v4-flash -p "say apple" Execution error ``` After: ``` % claude --model deepseek-v4-flash -p "say apple" apple ``` 20/20 `TestTranslateResponse` tests pass (17 existing + 3 new).

signals.title: Add loading state for log filters
signals.text: ## Summary Backend-backed log filters temporarily render an empty result set while the filtered request is still pending. dashboard-only change, targeted and full dashboard tests were run instead). - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem. - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review and received the required confidence score before maintainer review. ## CI (LiteLLM team) - [x] Branch creation CI run Link: PR checks are green for this branch. - [x] CI run for the last commit Link: PR checks are green for the last commit. - [ ] Merge / cherry-pick CI run Links: ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix See Evidence above. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Changes - Added `isFilteringResults` to log filter logic for backend filter requests, including pending debounce and stale-response handling. - Shows `Filtering logs...` and disables/spins the fetch control while filtered results are pending. - Rebuilt the proxy-served dashboard static bundle.

signals.title: fix(ui): don't overwrite guardrails with empty array on model edit
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Reported via Slack (#ui-engineering): user edited litellm params for an Anthropic model in the Admin UI and noticed an empty `"guardrails": []` was persisted into the model's `litellm_params`, even though they hadn't touched the guardrails field. They also hit `prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class` on inference, and recalled "i thought this was fixed somewhere" — referring to the analogous `vector_store_ids` fix from #91d88737b4. ## Root cause In `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/model_info_view.tsx`, the edit-model form initialized `guardrails` to `[]` and then included it in the update payload via: ```ts if (values.guardrails) { updatedLitellmParams.guardrails = values.guardrails; } ``` Empty arrays are truthy in JavaScript, so `if ([])` is `true`. Editing any unrelated field (e.g. `temperature`) on a model without guardrails would inject `guardrails: []` into the model's `litellm_params` via the PATCH-merge backend, polluting the saved config. ## Fix Mirror the `vector_store_ids` pattern directly above: - Initialize the form value to `undefined` when there are no stored guardrails, so the submit handler can distinguish *untouched* from *cleared*. - Only include the field when `length > 0`; if the user explicitly cleared previously-set guardrails, send `[]` to clear on the backend; otherwise `delete` the key from the payload so PATCH leaves the stored value untouched. ```ts if (values.guardrails?.length > 0) { updatedLitellmParams.guardrails = values.guardrails; } else if (values.guardrails !== undefined) { // User explicitly cleared previously-set guardrails — send [] to clear on backend updatedLitellmParams.guardrails = []; } else { delete updatedLitellmParams.guardrails; } ``` ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** — added a regression test in `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/model_info_view.test.tsx` that asserts `guardrails` is not in the update payload when the model has none and the user does not touch the field. The existing `vector_store_ids` regression test lives next to it. - [x] My PR passes all unit tests — `npx vitest run src/components/model_info_view.test.tsx` → 36/36 passing. - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/model_info_view.tsx` - Initialize `guardrails` form value to `undefined` (not `[]`) when the model has no guardrails configured. - Replace the truthy-array check in the submit handler with a length-aware branch that mirrors `vector_store_ids` semantics. - `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/model_info_view.test.tsx` - New regression test: `should not include guardrails in update payload when model has none and user does not touch the field`. [Slack Thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C09JWQ7PZ29/p1778203593355109?thread_ts=1778203593.355109&cid=C09JWQ7PZ29)

signals.title: (deepseek family) Fix reasoning_effort parameter mapping: correctly disable thinking for "none", and map deepseek's high/max reasoning_effort
signals.text: According to DeepDeek's [own documentation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode) of thinking mode, it looks like litellm is unable to correctly transform reasoning_effort. This fixes: - `reasoning_effort: none` now correctly produces the intended no-thinking call. (Note: "none" != `None`). - `reasoning_effort: xhigh` now correctly maps to deepseek's `max` - all other reasoning_effort enum terms collapse to either nothing at all or "high", which is the default mode deepseek-side ("high"). Changes: - litellm/llms/deepseek/chat/transformation.py: reasoning_effort: none now sends thinking: {"type": "disabled"}. All other values are collapsed to DeepSeek's supported "high" or "max" and forwarded as reasoning_effort in the request body. - tests/litellm/llms/deepseek/chat/test_deepseek_chat_transformation.py: Updated existing tests and added coverage for the full mapping (minimal→high, low→high, medium→high, high→high, xhigh→max, none→disabled, direct thinking: disabled passthrough, and precedence rules).
signals.author: neta79

signals.title: fix(exceptions): don't map upstream 400 to RateLimitError on substring match
signals.text: ## Problem OpenAI's `Unknown parameter: ''` / `Unrecognized request arguments supplied: , ` 400s, which echo the rejected field name back in the message, get misclassified as 429 `RateLimitError` whenever the field name contains `rate_limit` (or any `rate[\s_\-]*limit` substring) — e.g. `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors`. Concretely: while reproducing the v3 limiter leak (PR #27001 → PR #27913), OpenAI returned ``` { "error": { "message": "Unknown parameter: '_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors'.", "code": "400" } } ``` and LiteLLM surfaced it to the client as ``` HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests { "error": { "message": "litellm.RateLimitError: OpenAIException - Unknown parameter: '_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors'.", "type": "throttling_error", "code": "429" } } ``` That breaks two contracts: 1. **Retry semantics.** Clients see `429 throttling_error` and assume "back off and retry" — but the upstream rejected the body, retrying won't help. Loops forever on a malformed request. 2. **Debuggability.** It's the misclassification that hid the v3 leak: the 429 made it look like rate-limiting working as intended. The bug only surfaced after end-to-end provider testing. ## Root cause In `litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py`: **Cause 1 — unanchored regex:** `ExceptionCheckers.is_error_str_rate_limit` uses `re.search(r"rate[\s_\-]*limit", _error_str_lower)`. No word boundary, so it matches `rate_limit` as a substring of any identifier. Real OpenAI 400 body fields named with `rate_limit` (or LiteLLM-internal field names like `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors` leaked into the body) all trip the heuristic. **Cause 2 — heuristic runs before status code:** Inside the OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible / Mistral branch of `exception_type`, `is_error_str_rate_limit` is called unconditionally — *before* the status-code branch that handles 400 → `BadRequestError`. So an explicit upstream 400 never gets a chance to map correctly when the string matches. Anthropic's branch was already correct: it routes 400/413 to `BadRequestError` via status code, no string heuristic up front. (Companion observation in PR #16482, which tightened `\b429\b` against `429` substrings — same shape of bug, different token.) ## Fix **Anchor the regex** with a leading word boundary: `\brate[\s_\-]*limit`. Embedded identifiers like `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors` no longer match (the preceding `_` is a word char so `\b` fails). Standalone phrases all still match: `Rate limit exceeded`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `rate-limit-exceeded`, `You hit a rate limit`. **Status-code gate at the mapping site:** when `getattr(original_exception, "status_code", None) == 400`, skip the string heuristic entirely. A 400 is unambiguous per RFC 9110 — the upstream rejected the body, not the rate. Don't second-guess it. Both fixes are independent and complementary: the regex fix protects unknown-status-code paths (some upstream errors don't carry `status_code`), and the gate protects against any future heuristic that could mistake a 400 message for a 429. ## Tests `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py`: - `test_is_error_str_rate_limit_ignores_field_name_substring` — three forms of the OpenAI 400 wire message all return False. - `test_is_error_str_rate_limit_still_matches_standalone_token` — proves the tightening didn't regress legitimate detections. - `TestExceptionTypeStatusCodeGate` — end-to-end mapper tests. Build a real `openai.BadRequestError` with status 400 and the wire messages we saw, run `exception_type`, assert the result is `litellm.BadRequestError` (not `RateLimitError`). - `test_openai_429_still_maps_to_rate_limit` — confirms the genuine 429 path is untouched. ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py -q 43 passed in 0.21s ``` ## Related Companion to #27913 (which fixes the underlying v3 limiter leak that this misclassification was hiding). [Slack Thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/D0AUCPA0MLN/p1778738597799989?thread_ts=1778738597.799989&cid=D0AUCPA0MLN)
signals.author: mateo-berri

signals.title: fix(router): scan all deployments for weight/rpm/tpm in simple-shuffle
signals.text: ## Problem `simple_shuffle` only consults `healthy_deployments[0]` when deciding whether to do a weighted random pick. A config like: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini # ^ no weight/rpm/tpm declared - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini rpm: 1000 - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini rpm: 500 ``` silently falls back to **uniform random across all three** because the first entry has no `rpm`. Users perceive this as "deployment-level `rpm:` (or `tpm:` / `weight:`) is silently ignored under `simple-shuffle`" — the actual behavior is ordering-sensitive: if the first deployment happens to declare the weight field, everything works; if not, the rest are silently disregarded. This was reported as part of a broader audit of v3 rate limit semantics (sibling to #27913, #27914, #27915). It is the only one of those audit findings that's a pre-existing router bug rather than a v3-limiter or exception-mapper issue. ## Fix Extract `_pick_weight_field(healthy_deployments)` which scans **every** deployment for the precedence-ordered weight fields (`weight` > `rpm` > `tpm`) and returns the first one declared by any of them. Deployments that don't declare the chosen field continue to get weight `0` (preserves the existing semantics for in-list-but-unweighted entries). Also: defensive divide-by-zero guard when `total_weight == 0` (every deployment declared the field as 0 — pathological config). Falls through to uniform random instead of crashing. Docstring updated to be explicit that `rpm` and `tpm` here are **static relative weights**, not cap-enforced limits, and to point users at `router_settings.enable_pre_call_checks` (router-level RPM cap filter, gated on `messages is not None`) or the proxy's key-level v3 TPM/RPM limiter for actual cap enforcement under simple-shuffle. ## Scope notes This PR does **not** change the documented semantics of `rpm`/`tpm` under simple-shuffle (still relative weights). Adding actual cap enforcement to simple-shuffle would change load-balancing behavior for every user on that strategy and is out of scope here — leaving it for a follow-up. ## Tests `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_simple_shuffle.py` — 10 new unit tests: `TestPickWeightField`: - `test_returns_none_when_no_deployment_declares_anything` - `test_returns_weight_when_declared_on_first` - `test_returns_weight_when_declared_only_on_later_deployments` — **the headline regression test** - `test_precedence_weight_over_rpm_over_tpm` — covers two precedence pairs - `test_handles_missing_litellm_params` — defensive `TestSimpleShuffle` (statistical assertions over 6,000 picks): - `test_uniform_random_when_no_weights` - `test_rpm_on_later_deployment_is_respected` — end-to-end regression for silent-fallthrough - `test_zero_total_weight_falls_through_to_uniform_random` — divide-by-zero defense - `test_single_deployment_always_picked` - `test_weight_field_wins_over_rpm` — precedence under simple_shuffle (not just helper) ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_simple_shuffle.py -q 10 passed in 0.17s ``` ## Related Companion PRs from the same audit: - #27913 — fix(rate-limit): stop v3 limiter from leaking internal stash to provider body - #27914 — fix(rate-limit): resolve router model_name aliases to real provider (stacked on #27687) - #27915 — fix(exceptions): don't map upstream 400 to RateLimitError on substring match [Slack Thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/D0AUCPA0MLN/p1778738597799989?thread_ts=1778738597.799989&cid=D0AUCPA0MLN)

signals.title: feat: add first-class okta OIDC auth support (CI rerun of #27595)
signals.text: Duplicate of #27595 on a `litellm_`-prefixed branch so CircleCI runs the internal pipeline (forked branches skip it). **All credit to original author @dennishenry.** Original PR: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/27595 Tree based on `dennishenry:add_okta_oidc` @ `bffcc0e`. --- ## Summary (from #27595) Adds first-class Okta OIDC support for both Admin UI login (SSO) and API JWT authentication, instead of wiring Okta through the generic OIDC provider. ### Backend - `LiteLLM_JWTAuth` gains `public_key_url`, `audience`, `issuer` (YAML config beats env vars). - `JWTHandler.get_public_key()` reads `litellm_jwtauth.public_key_url` first; `_build_decode_kwargs()` reads `audience`/`issuer` from the config object. - JWKS URL list accepts a Python `list` in addition to comma-separated string. - New `_OIDC_PROVIDER_OKTA` constant + helpers: `_get_oidc_env_prefix`, `_get_okta_endpoint_from_issuer`, `_is_oidc_pkce_enabled`. - Generic OIDC helpers accept a `provider` param and pick `OKTA_*` vs `GENERIC_*` env prefix. - Okta defaults: PKCE on, Okta claim names (`sub`/`name`/`given_name`/`family_name`/`iss`), `groups` in default scope. - Endpoint auto-derivation from `OKTA_ISSUER` (`/v1/authorize`, `/v1/token`, `/v1/userinfo`). - `OKTA_CLIENT_ID` triggers SSO across `google_login`, `auth_callback`, `debug_sso_login`, `debug_sso_callback`, `sso_readiness`. - `SSOConfig` gains `okta_client_id`, `okta_client_secret`, `okta_issuer`, `okta_authorization_endpoint`, `okta_token_endpoint`, `okta_userinfo_endpoint`. - New example: `litellm/proxy/example_config_yaml/okta_jwt_auth_config.yaml`. ### UI - Dedicated Okta fields (`okta_client_id`, `okta_client_secret`, `okta_issuer`) replace the five generic endpoint fields. - `detectSSOProvider()` extracted; checks `okta_client_id` first, falls back to URL heuristics for backcompat. - Auth0 no longer mis-detected as Okta. - Label: "Okta / Auth0 SSO" → "Okta SSO". ### Tests - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_handle_jwt.py`: 2 new tests for `public_key_url` / `audience` / `issuer` config plumbing. - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_ui_sso.py`: 3 new tests (Okta `should_use_sso_handler`, endpoint derivation, PKCE-by-default). - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/ui_crud_endpoints/test_proxy_setting_endpoints.py`: covers `OKTA_CLIENT_ID`. Diffstat: 25 files, +796 / -287. --- Supersedes #27595 once CI green. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches SSO and JWT validation paths (audience/issuer verification, PKCE handling, secret handling), which can affect login and API authorization if misconfigured; changes are mostly additive with fallbacks to existing env-based behavior. > > **Overview** > Adds **first-class Okta OIDC support** for Admin UI SSO and JWT API auth, introducing `OKTA_*` env/config fields, issuer-based endpoint derivation, and Okta-specific defaults (notably PKCE enabled by default). > > Extends `litellm_jwtauth` to accept `public_key_url` (string/list), `audience`, and `issuer` (config-first, env fallback) and wires these into `JWTHandler` key fetching and `jwt.decode` verification. Also updates SSO settings CRUD to **redact secrets** in responses and preserve stored secrets when clients echo back the redaction sentinel. > > Updates dashboard UI to treat Okta as a distinct provider with dedicated fields, shared provider-detection/payload helpers, and revised tests/docs fixtures (including an Okta example YAML and new backend/unit tests). > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 156c0ecdab46f62068eeb483e24740a0b553aabf. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(dashscope): tiered pricing should be all-or-nothing per official docs
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Re-opens the concern raised in [#16150 comment by @togear](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/16150#issuecomment-2806215418) (cites Alibaba's official tiered-billing rules) which never received a follow-up. Related: #14471 (original — correct — implementation), #15423, #16150 (PR that introduced the regression). ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] CLA signed - [x] Added testing in `tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py` (5 existing tests rewritten + 2 new boundary tests) - [x] `make test-unit` passes for the dashscope dir (12/12) - [x] Black, Ruff, MyPy, circular-imports, import-safety all clean - [x] Scope is isolated — only `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` and its test ## Summary This is **not a single-model issue**. It is a systemic mispricing affecting **every Dashscope (Alibaba Bailian) tiered model** — 14 in `model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` today (qwen-flash, qwen-plus, qwen3-coder-plus, qwen3-coder-flash, qwen3-max, qwen-plus-latest and all their dated snapshots), plus any custom user model declaring `tiered_pricing`. It silently breaks `litellm.completion_cost(...)`, spend logs, budgets, team-level quotas, and alerting on every cross-tier request. ## The bug `_calculate_tiered_cost` in `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` currently splits tokens across tiers using **graduated / income-tax-bracket** math. Dashscope's [official billing documentation](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/billing-for-model-studio) explicitly specifies the opposite — **all-or-nothing**: > 百炼部分模型实行阶梯计费。单价取决于单次请求的输入 Token 总量。**该请求的所有 Token 均按对应阶梯的单价结算。** > > 例如，某模型设有两档计费区间：0 < Token ≤ 32K 和 32K < Token ≤ 128K。若输入 100K Token，因数值落在第二区间（32K < 100K ≤ 128K），**所有 Token 均按第二档单价结算**。 (Translation: *The unit price of a request is determined by its total input tokens. ALL tokens in the request are billed at that single tier's rate.*) This regressed in #16150 (2025-11-04), which removed the all-or-nothing logic from the original #14471 implementation and replaced it with graduated brackets. @togear pointed this out in April 2026 on the merged-PR thread, citing the same official source; the comment did not get a maintainer response. There are two related correctness issues, both fixed here: 1. **Tier selection algorithm.** Graduated brackets should be all-or-nothing. 2. **Tier selection input.** `_calculate_prompt_cost` was passing `text_tokens` and `cached_tokens` separately into the tier selector. Per the docs the tier is decided by the *total* request input (text + cache), and that tier's rates apply to every portion (text, cache, and output). The current code can therefore pick a wrong tier even on flat requests when the cache-hit fraction is large. ## Impact (measured against current code + actual Bailian rates for `qwen-plus`) | Request size | Falls in tier | Bailian charge | LiteLLM today | LiteLLM under-bills | |---|---|---|---|---| | 100K | Tier 1 (≤128K) | 0.015 ¥ | 0.015 ¥ | 0% ✓ | | 140K | Tier 2 (128K–256K) | 0.085 ¥ | 0.025 ¥ | **70%** | | 200K | Tier 2 | 0.121 ¥ | 0.061 ¥ | **49%** | | 500K | Tier 3 (256K–1M) | 0.601 ¥ | 0.384 ¥ | **36%** | The closer a request lands to a tier boundary, the worse the under-bill. For users running long-context Qwen workloads (RAG, document analysis, code understanding), a 30–70% gap between LiteLLM's reported spend and the actual Alibaba invoice is large enough to silently blow past team budgets and alert thresholds. This is also a forward-looking concern: any future provider that adopts the `tiered_pricing` array (Moonshot/Kimi, Volcengine/Doubao, GLM, MiniMax — all of which already publish similar input-length-based tiered prices in their public docs) will inherit the same broken semantics unless `tiered_pricing` is defined as all-or-nothing here. ## The fix 1. Replace `_calculate_tiered_cost` (graduated) with a small pair of helpers: - `_select_tier_for_input(total_input_tokens, tiered_pricing) -> Optional[dict]` - `_tier_rate(tier, cost_key, fallback_cost_key=None) -> float` 2. In `_calculate_prompt_cost` and `_calculate_completion_cost`, compute `total_input = text_tokens + cached_tokens` once, select the tier from it, then bill `text_tokens × tier.input_rate + cached_tokens × tier.cache_rate` and `completion_tokens × tier.output_rate + reasoning_tokens × tier.reasoning_rate` against the same tier. 3. Document the semantics + cite the official Bailian source at the top of the module so the next refactor doesn't repeat the regression. Public surface (`cost_per_token`) and helper signatures (`_calculate_prompt_cost`, `_calculate_completion_cost`) are unchanged. Flat-rate fallback path is unchanged. No call sites outside the module use the removed helper (`grep -rn "_calculate_tiered_cost" litellm/ tests/` is empty after the patch). ### Boundary semantics A tier matches when `range_start < total_input <= range_end`, so a request of exactly `range_end` tokens stays in the lower tier — matching the official phrasing `0 < Token ≤ 32K`. Requests exceeding the highest declared range fall back to the last tier's rate. ## Tests `tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py` — 7 tests: | Test | What it locks down | |---|---| | `test_dashscope_flat_pricing_fallback` | Flat-rate models unaffected (qwen-max) | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_within_first_tier` | All-tier-1 request → tier-1 rate | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_crossing_into_higher_tier` | Cross-tier request → entire request at higher tier (the regression case) | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_with_caching` | Tier selected by total input; cache cost billed at input-tier rate | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_exceeding_highest_tier` | Beyond top tier → last-tier rate | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_boundary_at_range_end` | Exactly `range_end` tokens → lower tier | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_output_uses_input_tier` | Output billed at input-selected tier, not by output volume | ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/ -v ====================== 12 passed, 1 warning in 1.15s ======================= ``` ## Lint / type / format ``` $ uv run black --check litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py 2 files would be left unchanged. $ uv run ruff check litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py All checks passed! $ uv run mypy litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py Success: no issues found in 1 source file $ make check-circular-imports check-import-safety No LiteLLM type hints found. [from litellm import *] OK! no issues! ```

signals.title: fix(proxy): use >= in _team_max_budget_check to match other budget checks
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #28020 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory — added `test_team_budget_check_raises_when_spend_equals_max_budget` in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_auth_checks.py` - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit` (could not run the full suite locally; the new test follows the same pattern as the existing `test_team_budget_check_reads_from_spend_counter` directly above it) - [ ] Greptile review pending ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_team_max_budget_check` used `>` while every other budget enforcement path in the same file uses `>=`: | Check | Line | Operator | |---|---|---| | `_virtual_key_max_budget_check` (key) | 3283 | `>=` | | Budget window (key) | 3316 | `>=` | | `_team_max_budget_check` (team) | **3653** | **`>` ← bug** | | Budget window (team) | 3701 | `>=` | | `_organization_max_budget_check` (org) | 4007 | `>=` | A team whose spend equals exactly `max_budget` was therefore still allowed through, e.g. `10.0 > 10.0` is False. This is inconsistent with key/org/window enforcement and contradicts the natural meaning of "max budget". ### Diff ```diff - if spend > team_object.max_budget: + if spend >= team_object.max_budget: ``` ### Test Added `test_team_budget_check_raises_when_spend_equals_max_budget` that constructs a team with `max_budget=10.0`, mocks `get_current_spend` to return exactly `10.0`, and asserts `BudgetExceededError` is raised with `current_cost == 10.0` and `max_budget == 10.0`. Mirrors the existing `test_team_budget_check_reads_from_spend_counter` test pattern. ### Scope note This PR intentionally does **not** touch the other `>`-using sites (`global_proxy_spend > litellm.max_budget` at line 331, `project_object.spend > max_budget` at line 3815) — those are separate decisions and out of scope for #28020. --- _Disclosure: this PR was prepared with assistance from Claude (Anthropic). The bug location and proposed fix were both pre-specified in the linked issue; I verified the surrounding code matches the issue's description and added the regression test._

signals.title: fix(proxy/ui): detect stale restructured dirs as needing rebuild
signals.text: ## Summary - `_is_ui_pre_restructured` short-circuited to `True` as soon as it found any `<route>/index.html` subdirectory, ignoring whether a fresh `<route>.html` source file was sitting next to it. - That mixed state happens routinely in development: a UI rebuild lands new chunk hashes via `chore: update Next.js build artifacts`, but leftover `<route>/index.html` files from a previous proxy run remain on disk. The detection returns `True`, restructure is skipped, and the proxy serves the stale `<route>/index.html` — which references `/_next/static/chunks/<hash>.js` files that no longer exist. Browser sees `ChunkLoadError` / 404 on UI routes. - Fix walks the tree: only return `True` when at least one restructured subdirectory exists **and** no unrestructured `*.html` source files remain (outside `_next/` and `litellm-asset-prefix/`). Mixed state now correctly triggers a re-restructure, and `os.replace` atomically refreshes the stale `index.html` files. ## Test plan - [x] `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py -v -k "is_ui_pre_restructured or restructure_ui_html or extensionless_route"` — 6 passed (4 new + 2 existing) - [x] `uv run black litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py` - [ ] Local repro: stale `out/<route>/index.html` left over from a prior proxy run + fresh `out/<route>.html` → restart proxy → restructure runs, stale chunk references replaced. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Low risk: this only changes UI static-file restructure detection and adds focused tests, but could affect when the proxy decides to skip or rerun restructuring on startup. > > **Overview** > Fixes `_is_ui_pre_restructured` so it no longer returns `True` just because *some* `<route>/index.html` directories exist; it now walks the UI tree and only treats it as ready when **at least one restructured route exists** and **no unrestructured `*.html` source files remain** (excluding `_next` and `litellm-asset-prefix`). This prevents serving stale restructured HTML after a UI rebuild that leaves mixed `<route>.html` + `<route>/index.html` on disk (which can cause missing-chunk 404s). > > Adds new tests covering marker-file readiness, clean restructured pattern detection, unrestructured trees, and the mixed-state regression case. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 2cc51774018009791761363469bcc8cd231d3774. signals.title: feat(cost): support OpenAI regional/data-residency 10% uplift via service_tier="regional"
signals.text: ## Summary OpenAI now charges a 10% premium when using regional/data-residency processing on the latest GPT models (see [pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)). LiteLLM didn't account for this — cost tracking for requests opting into regional processing was 10% under-reported. This adds a `regional` value to the `ServiceTier` enum and 10%-uplifted `*_regional` pricing keys to every OpenAI model in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` that already has priority-tier pricing (gpt-5 family, gpt-5.1/5.2/5.3/5.4/5.5 families and codex/chat variants, gpt-4.1 family, gpt-4o family, o3, o4-mini). Above-272k-tokens variants on gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.5 also get a regional counterpart. The existing `service_tier` resolution chain (optional_params, response attribute, usage attribute, explicit argument) already covers the customer-facing API surface, so passing `service_tier="regional"` anywhere now produces the correct cost. ## Customer-facing usage ```python import litellm resp = litellm.completion( model="gpt-5", messages=[...], service_tier="regional", # 10% uplift applied ) litellm.completion_cost(completion_response=resp) ``` Or, if `service_tier` is set on the response object by OpenAI itself, no client change is needed — `completion_cost()` picks it up automatically. ## Code changes - `litellm/types/utils.py` — add `ServiceTier.REGIONAL`; add `*_regional` fields to `ModelInfoBase` and `CustomPricingLiteLLMParams`. - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py` — generalize `_get_service_tier_cost_key` to iterate `ServiceTier` (so future tiers slot in without code changes). - `litellm/utils.py` — expose new `*_regional` keys via `get_model_info()`. - `model_prices_and_context_window.json` + `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` — 101 new `*_regional` entries across 30 OpenAI models (10% uplift). - `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py` — extend JSON schema validator with regional keys. ## Test plan - [x] `make test-unit` style runs: `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/test_llm_cost_calc_utils.py` (47 passed) and `tests/test_litellm/test_cost_calculator.py` (41 passed). - [x] `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py::test_aaamodel_prices_and_context_window_json_is_valid` passes (JSON schema). - [x] Six new dedicated regional tests cover: standard regional pricing, case-insensitive tier value, fallback when model has no regional keys, above-272k regional pricing, regional cost-key resolution, enum membership; plus two end-to-end `completion_cost` tests for regional via response attribute and via `optional_params`. - [x] Black formatting clean. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Updates core cost calculation and model pricing data, which can change reported spend for OpenAI models and above-threshold cache/token pricing paths. Scope is bounded and covered by new unit tests, but impacts billing-critical logic. > > **Overview** > Adds a new `ServiceTier.REGIONAL` and propagates `*_regional` pricing keys through `ModelInfo`/`get_model_info()` so cost tracking can apply OpenAI’s regional/data-residency ~10% uplift. > > Cost-key resolution in `llm_cost_calc/utils.py` is generalized to accept any known `ServiceTier` (now including `regional`) and is extended to prefer service-tier-specific *above-threshold* cache pricing keys when present. > > Updates `model_prices_and_context_window*.json` with regional price entries for relevant OpenAI models (including >272k token variants) and adds tests covering regional pricing, fallback behavior, case-insensitivity, and `completion_cost` service-tier extraction. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ebd580aad8dd45054baad5d1b6818dd913ce6882. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(anthropic, bedrock): drop temperature/top_p for Claude Opus 4.7
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #26444. Anthropic's Messages API returns `400 invalid_request_error: temperature is deprecated for this model.` whenever `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` is set to a non-default value on Claude Opus 4.7 ([Opus 4.7 migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/migration-guide#migrating-to-claude-opus-4-7)). LiteLLM's `AnthropicConfig.get_supported_openai_params` still advertised `temperature` / `top_p` for every Anthropic model, so `litellm.drop_params=True` was a no-op on 4.7: litellm had no reason to drop a param it believed was supported, the value was forwarded to the API, and end users took a hard 400. The same shape hits `AmazonConverseConfig` for Bedrock-routed Opus 4.7. This fix uses the maintainers' existing capability-flag pattern (`supports_*` keys on `model_prices_and_context_window.json` read via `_is_explicitly_disabled_factory`) rather than hardcoding model strings in transformation logic — the same approach `OpenAIGPT5Config._is_reasoning_effort_level_explicitly_disabled` already uses for the gpt-5 family. ### Scope Models marked `supports_temperature: false` + `supports_top_p: false`: - `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-7-20260416` (Anthropic) - `anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` + `{global,us,eu,au}.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (Bedrock Converse) - `azure_ai/claude-opus-4-7` - `vertex_ai/claude-opus-4-7`, `vertex_ai/claude-opus-4-7@default` Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.6, 3.7-sonnet, and 3.x models are unchanged — the deprecation is Opus-4.7-only per the migration guide. OpenRouter and Perplexity entries are deliberately left alone — they route through different configs and may handle the param differently. ### Why a static fallback as well `AnthropicConfig._param_explicitly_unsupported` first consults `_is_explicitly_disabled_factory`. When the registry lookup misses — e.g. an unreleased dated 4.7 snapshot not yet in the JSON — it falls back to the existing `_is_claude_4_7_model` family check so future 4.7 variants are covered before anyone updates the JSON. Newer-than-4.7 models, including hypothetical future Opus releases, only need a JSON entry — no code change. ### Defense in depth at the mapping site `map_openai_params` honours the same helper inside the `temperature` / `top_p` branches so direct callers don't leak the params either, even without `drop_params=True`. This addresses Greptile's P2 finding on #26445 (the prior closed PR for this issue). ## Test plan - [x] Parametrized unit asserts `temperature` / `top_p` are filtered out of `AnthropicConfig.get_supported_openai_params` for `claude-opus-4-7`, the dated `claude-opus-4-7-20260416`, and the vendor-prefixed `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` - [x] Family-fallback test covers an unreleased dated snapshot (`claude-opus-4-7-20991231`) not in the registry - [x] Regression suite pins Sonnet 4.6 (dated + alias), Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 3.5, Sonnet 3.7, and Opus 4.6 to still advertise both sampling params - [x] `map_openai_params` unit confirms explicit `temperature=0.3, top_p=0.9` does not reach `optional_params` for Opus 4.7 but does for Opus 4.6 - [x] End-to-end-shape test reproduces the issue: `map_openai_params(drop_params=True)` + `transform_request` no longer leaks `temperature` into the Anthropic request body - [x] Bedrock Converse mirror suite covers all four region variants and pins Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5 / 3.5-sonnet on Bedrock as regressions - [x] Existing Anthropic + Bedrock test suites stay green locally (`pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic tests/test_litellm/llms/bedrock/chat` — 976 passed) ## Reproduction (before this PR, on `main`) ```python import os, importlib os.environ["LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP"] = "True" import litellm params = litellm.get_supported_openai_params( model="claude-opus-4-7", custom_llm_provider="anthropic" ) assert "temperature" not in params # FAILS on main, PASSES with this PR ``` ## Notes for reviewers - The Databricks workspace endpoint surfaces the same upstream Anthropic deprecation (per a follow-up comment on the issue from @Kontinuation). I left that out of this PR to keep the diff focused on the two configs the bug report names; happy to fold it in here or do it as a follow-up — whichever you prefer. - `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` absorbs ~34 lines of upstream drift from earlier unrelated merges so the `ci_cd/check_files_match.py` byte-identity check passes — same constraint that hit #26246. The actual `supports_temperature` / `supports_top_p` additions are 20 lines, mirrored across both files. - I'm aware that #26445 and #26246 were prior attempts at this fix that both got closed. I read both diffs and the review feedback before writing this one — this PR drops the wholesale rewrite of `ProviderSpecificModelInfo` from #26246 (we don't need it — `_is_explicitly_disabled_factory` reads raw `.get(key)`), keeps the scope tighter than #26445 (Opus-4.7-only rather than the whole reasoning family), and adds the defense-in-depth at `map_openai_params` that Greptile flagged on #26445. Fixes #26444 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: fix(databricks): drop unsupported temperature param for Claude Opus 4.7
signals.text: ## Summary Follow-up to #28113. Same root cause — Anthropic's Messages API rejects `temperature` for Claude Opus 4.7, accepting only `top_p` for sampling control — applied to the Databricks adapter. Reported by @Kontinuation in the original issue thread ([#26444](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/26444)), with a detailed reproduction by @dgomez04 in the same thread showing the same 400 surfacing through the Databricks workspace endpoint: ``` litellm.BadRequestError: DatabricksException - {"error_code":"BAD_REQUEST", "message":"BAD_REQUEST: Model us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 does not support the temperature parameter."} ``` This PR mirrors the #28113 pattern in the Databricks code path: - `DatabricksConfig.get_supported_openai_params` filters `temperature` / `top_p` out when the model id matches the `claude-opus-4-7` family - `map_openai_params` adds the same defense-in-depth guard so a raw kwargs leak is caught at the second layer too - A new `databricks/databricks-claude-opus-4-7` entry is added to `model_prices_and_context_window.json` (and the backup file — `ci_cd/check_files_match.py` passes) with `supports_temperature: false` / `supports_top_p: false` The `_param_explicitly_unsupported` helper is kept self-contained on `DatabricksConfig` rather than reaching into the helper #28113 adds on `AnthropicConfig`, so this PR can land independently of #28113 in either order. Happy to deduplicate in a follow-up commit once both land. ## Test plan - [x] new unit test: `temperature` is filtered out for `databricks-claude-opus-4-7`, the dated variant `databricks-claude-opus-4-7-20260416`, and the vendor-prefixed `databricks/databricks-claude-opus-4-7` form - [x] new unit test: unreleased dated Opus 4.7 snapshots not yet in the registry fall back to the `_is_claude_4_7_model` family check - [x] regression test: Databricks Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.1, and 3.7-sonnet still expose `temperature` / `top_p` - [x] defense-in-depth: `map_openai_params(drop_params=False)` strips `temperature` / `top_p` for Opus 4.7 and preserves them for Opus 4.5 - [x] end-to-end shape: top-level `litellm.get_supported_openai_params(model="databricks-claude-opus-4-7", custom_llm_provider="databricks")` no longer reports `temperature` (the exact contract `litellm.drop_params=True` keys off — without the fix this was the no-op @dgomez04 hit) - [x] `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/databricks` — 81 passed, 13 skipped (integration tests requiring credentials) ## Notes - Companion to #28113 — they apply the same fix to different provider adapters and can be merged in either order. - The new `databricks/databricks-claude-opus-4-7` JSON entry is the first 4.7 entry on the Databricks side (there were already 4.5, 4.1, 4, sonnet-4-5/4-1/4, haiku-4-5, and 3-7-sonnet entries). Pricing mirrors `databricks-claude-opus-4-5` (5e-6 input / 25e-6 output, 7.1429e-5 / 3.57143e-4 DBU) as a placeholder pending the Databricks pay-per-token listing for Opus 4.7 — flagged in the entry's `metadata.notes`. Happy to update the prices in a follow-up commit once Databricks publishes them, or before merge if a maintainer has the authoritative numbers.

signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #28126 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/test_litellm/` directory - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Before fix: File "litellm/router.py", line 9523, in update_settings _casted_value = int(kwargs[var]) TypeError: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'NoneType' After fix: update_settings(timeout=None) resets the setting to None without crashing. Regression test passes: test_router_update_settings_none_resets_int_setting ✅ ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Router.update_settings() called int(kwargs[var]) with no None guard. This is a real production path: the proxy server calls update_settings() on every startup with settings merged from config.yaml and a JSON database. JSON null maps to Python None, so clearing a timeout via the admin UI caused a proxy startup crash. Fixed by adding an explicit None check before casting. signals.title: fix(utils): prevent content growth in shorten_message_to_fit_limit when half_length is 0
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #28128 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/test_litellm/` directory - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Before fix: AssertionError: Content grew — shorten_message_to_fit_limit returned content longer than the original when half_length was 0. After fix: Content is always shorter after trimming. Regression test passes: test_shorten_message_never_grows_content ✅ ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes When new_length < 2, half_length becomes 0. Python's -0 == 0 identity means content[-0:] == content[0:] == entire string. The trimmed result was "" + ".." + full_content — two characters longer than the original on every iteration. The loop hit MAX_TOKEN_TRIMMING_ATTEMPTS without ever shrinking content, causing the caller to receive an untrimmed message and then get a context_length_exceeded error from the provider. Fixed by adding a half_length == 0 guard that falls back to simple head-truncation (content[:new_length]) which always produces a strictly shorter result. Added regression test asserting content length is monotonically non-increasing across all trimming iterations.

signals.title: fix(bedrock): forward Anthropic hosted-tools via additionalModelReque…
signals.text: ## Problem After #16115 the Anthropic direct path correctly forwards hosted tools (memory_20250818, web_search_*, web_fetch_*, code_execution_*) and auto-injects the matching beta header. The **Bedrock Converse** path does not — hosted tools fall through to `_bedrock_tools_pt` and are emitted as a generic empty toolSpec named `litellm_unnamed_tool_X`, which Bedrock dutifully returns as a phantom tool_use the model can never satisfy. Reproduction (LiteLLM 1.83.14, real Bedrock call, debug enabled): ```python import litellm litellm._turn_on_debug() litellm.acompletion( model='bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'remember my name is Maze'}], tools=[{'type':'memory_20250818','name':'memory'}], aws_region_name='eu-central-1', max_tokens=200, ) ``` Outgoing payload — note empty `additionalModelRequestFields`, unnamed tool: ```json { "toolConfig": {"tools": [{"toolSpec": { "inputSchema":{"json":{"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[]}}, "name":"litellm_unnamed_tool_0", "description":"litellm_unnamed_tool_0" }}]}, "additionalModelRequestFields": {} } ``` ## Fix Route hosted tools into `additionalModelRequestFields.tools` (raw Anthropic format) and auto-inject the matching beta header into `additionalModelRequestFields.anthropic_beta`. This mirrors the existing computer-use branch and the Anthropic direct path. A defensive guard in `_bedrock_tools_pt` skips hosted tools so they cannot regress into the generic transform later. Beta header mapping: - `memory_*` → `context-management-2025-06-27` - `web_fetch_*` → `web-fetch-2025-09-10` - `web_search_*` → `web-search-2025-03-05` ## After Same input, with the patch applied: ```json { "additionalModelRequestFields": { "tools": [{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}], "anthropic_beta": ["context-management-2025-06-27"] } } ``` End-to-end verified against real Bedrock — Sonnet now invokes `memory.view` followed by `memory.create` on its own initiative. ## Tests - 12 new tests in `tests/test_litellm/llms/bedrock/test_bedrock_hosted_tools.py` covering the predicate, payload routing, beta-header injection, function-tool no-regression and mixed-tool routing. - Existing `test_anthropic_beta_support.py` and `test_converse_transformation.py` suites still green (110 tests). ## Notes - Bash/text_editor remain on the existing computer-use branch — no change. - The patch merges hosted-tools with any tools already placed in `additionalModelRequestFields` by the computer-use branch, so the two features coexist cleanly.

signals.title: fix(ui): trim whitespace from MCP inspector tool call inputs
signals.text: ## Summary - Strip leading/trailing whitespace from form values in the MCP inspector's `ToolTestPanel` before submitting a tool call. - Copy-pasted arguments often carry stray spaces / newlines that the upstream MCP tool then rejects or matches incorrectly. - Whitespace-only inputs now also fall through the existing empty-value guard and are correctly treated as "not provided" instead of being sent as `" "`. The change is a single `normalizedValue = typeof value === "string" ? value.trim() : value` step at the top of the per-field loop in `handleSubmit`, with every `switch` branch routed through it (`string`, `number`/`integer`, `boolean`, `object`/`array`, `default`). Booleans from the antd `<Select>` and already-parsed numbers pass through unchanged because they aren't strings. For `object`/`array` fields, trimming the JSON blob before `JSON.parse` is safe and also fixes a paper cut where a trailing newline from a paste would invalidate the JSON. File touched: `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/mcp_tools/ToolTestPanel.tsx` ## Test plan - [ ] In the MCP inspector, paste a tool argument with leading/trailing spaces (e.g. `" hello "`) and confirm the request body shows the trimmed value. - [ ] Submit a whitespace-only value into an optional string field and confirm it is omitted from the request (not sent as `" "`). - [ ] Submit an object/array field with a trailing newline in the JSON textarea and confirm it parses correctly. - [ ] Boolean and number fields still submit the correct typed values. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: feat(vertex_ai): add Lyria music generation support
signals.text: ## Relevant issues <!-- e.g. "Fixes #000" --> ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] Tests added in `tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_lyria.py` (21 unit tests) - [x] `make test-unit` passes - [x] Scoped to a single problem: Lyria routing and response transformation - [ ] Greptile review pending ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Calling `vertex_ai/lyria-3-clip-preview` or `vertex_ai/lyria-3-pro-preview` returned `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT`. No route matched, so requests fell through to the legacy predict handler, which built a `generateContent`-style URL. Lyria uses a separate endpoint: ``` POST https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/{project}/locations/global/interactions ``` This adds `VertexAIModelRoute.LYRIA` and `LyriaConfig`. The handler: - Calls the v1beta1 Interactions endpoint with GCP Bearer auth - Transforms the prompt into `{"model": "...", "input": [{"type": "text", "text": "..."}]}` - Parses three response outputs: timestamped lyrics, caption, and base64 MP3 - Returns audio in `message.audio` (`data` + `transcript`), `content=None` per OpenAI audio spec - Puts `caption` and `interaction_id` in `provider_specific_fields` - Sets cost in `_hidden_params["response_cost"]`: $0.04 per clip, $0.08 per full song Pricing entries for both models use `mode: audio_generation`. The gemini provider routes to a different host with no Interactions API path, so no `gemini/` entries. **Caller usage:** ```python import base64, litellm response = litellm.completion( model="vertex_ai/lyria-3-pro-preview", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "upbeat disco polo"}], vertex_project="my-project", ) audio_bytes = base64.b64decode(response.choices[0].message.audio.data) lyrics = response.choices[0].message.audio.transcript caption = response.choices[0].message.provider_specific_fields["caption"] with open("song.mp3", "wb") as f: f.write(audio_bytes) ``` ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy log confirming the correct endpoint after this change: ``` POST https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/my-project/locations/global/interactions {"model": "lyria-3-pro-preview", "input": [{"type": "text", "text": "disco polo"}]} Response: {"status": "completed", "outputs": [{"type": "text", ...}, {"type": "audio", "mime_type": "audio/mpeg", "data": "..."}]} ```
