signals.title: fix(streaming): backfill response.completed output from output_item.done events
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #25429. Related to #26179. Supersedes #30934 ## Linear ticket N/A ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) (201 pre-existing failures in prisma/database, vertex AI, and MCP semantic filter tests; none in touched files — 324 tests across `tests/test_litellm/responses/` and `tests/test_litellm/llms/chatgpt/` pass cleanly) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## CI (LiteLLM team) > **CI status guideline:** > > - 50-55 passing tests: main is stable with minor issues. > - 45-49 passing tests: acceptable but needs attention > - <= 40 passing tests: unstable; be careful with your merges and assess the risk. - [ ] **Branch creation CI run** Link: - [ ] **CI run for the last commit** Link: - [ ] **Merge / cherry-pick CI run** Links: ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The `chatgpt/` provider routes through chatgpt.com's Codex backend, which sends `response.completed` with `output: []`. The actual assistant content arrives via preceding `response.output_item.done` SSE events. Without accumulation, the chat-completions bridge receives an empty output list and raises: ``` ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: [] ``` The fix teaches `BaseResponsesAPIStreamingIterator._process_chunk` to accumulate `response.output_item.done` payloads as they stream in and backfill them into the `response.completed` chunk before it is stored as `completed_response`. Items are serialized to plain dicts via `model_dump()` so the downstream `_handle_raw_dict_response_item` callback in the transformation layer can process them. The existing `_recover_output_items_from_raw_sse` fallback in `LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler.transform_response` is preserved as a second layer if the streaming path is ever bypassed. **Before:** ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: hello"}],"stream":false}' {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: []. Received Model Group=gpt-5.4\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` **After:** ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: hello"}],"stream":false}' {"id":"chatcmpl-764df91c-940a-47ea-be8c-d2aff173b8f4","created":1782409329,"model":"gpt-5.4","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"hello","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":5,"prompt_tokens":1635,"total_tokens":1640,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}}} ``` ## Type Bug Fix ## Changes `BaseResponsesAPIStreamingIterator` accumulates `response.output_item.done` items into `_streamed_output_items` during streaming. A secondary `_streamed_text_only_items` dict catches providers that emit `response.output_text.done` without a preceding `response.output_item.done`. At `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`, if `output` is empty and either dict is non-empty, the merged items are sorted by `output_index` and backfilled onto the response object. Items are serialized via `model_dump()` when they are Pydantic instances and passed through unchanged when they are already plain dicts; both the serialization and the assignment sit inside a `try/except` so any failure degrades to a logged warning rather than crashing the stream. `FallbackResponsesStreamWrapper` (router.py) and `MCPEnhancedStreamingIterator` (mcp_streaming_iterator.py) both bypass `super().__init__()` and are updated to mirror the two new instance attributes. Twelve regression tests are added to `tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator_output_recovery.py`, covering: the core backfill, multi-item index ordering, authoritative output preservation, `response.incomplete` backfill, `response.failed` no-backfill, `output_text.done` fallback, `output_item.done` precedence, replace-in-place content slots, gap padding, absent `output_index` sequential fallback, exception swallowing, and the dict-type contract required by the downstream transformation layer. The bulk of the line-count change in `streaming_iterator.py` is ruff reformatting of pre-existing code required to pass `ruff format`; the logical additions are confined to the accumulation block in `_process_chunk` and the two new instance attributes in `__init__`.

signals.title: feat(cost): support time-based off-peak pricing in cost calculation
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Some providers discount per-token rates during a daily window - The cost map only modeled one static rate per model - Logged spend therefore overstates cost inside that window How it solves it: - A model entry can carry an `off_peak_pricing` block - `hours_utc` takes one `"HH:MM-HH:MM"` window or a list - Windows may wrap past midnight; unset rates fall back - An off-peak rate replaces the tier or threshold rate - Timezone-aware timestamps are normalized to UTC before comparing ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin serving a provider that discounts by time of day sees the same spend logged around the clock, so their cost dashboard overstates what the provider actually invoices 1. They add the deployment to their config with a single `input_cost_per_token` and `output_cost_per_token` 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with that model at 18:00 UTC, inside the provider's published discount window 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request billed at the full daytime rate 4. They send the same request again at 12:00 UTC and see an identical spend figure, so the discount never shows up anywhere After: the same two requests bill differently, so logged spend tracks the provider invoice 1. They add `off_peak_pricing` to the deployment, giving `hours_utc` plus the discounted per-token rates 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions at 18:00 UTC 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows that request at the discounted rate 4. They send it again at 12:00 UTC and see the standard rate, so the two windows are visibly different ## Relevant issues Fixes #31606 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The feature is time-gated, so the only thing that changes between two otherwise identical calls is the clock. Captured at 7621e0df4e, asking the cost calculator for the same usage at four different times: ```python from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone import litellm from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.utils import _get_token_base_cost from litellm.types.utils import Usage litellm.register_model( { "offpeak-demo": { "litellm_provider": "openai", "mode": "chat", "input_cost_per_token": 1e-6, "output_cost_per_token": 2e-6, "off_peak_pricing": { "hours_utc": "16:30-00:30", "input_cost_per_token": 5e-7, "output_cost_per_token": 1e-6, }, } } ) info = litellm.get_model_info(model="offpeak-demo") usage = Usage(prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=50, total_tokens=150) for label, when in [ ("18:00 UTC (inside window)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 18, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("12:00 UTC (outside window)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("00:15 UTC (past midnight wrap)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 0, 15, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("02:00 UTC+8 (same instant as 18:00 UTC)", datetime(2026, 1, 2, 2, 0, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=8)))), ]: print(label, _get_token_base_cost(info, usage, current_time=when)[:2]) ``` ``` 18:00 UTC (inside window) (5e-07, 1e-06) 12:00 UTC (outside window) (1e-06, 2e-06) 00:15 UTC (past midnight wrap) (5e-07, 1e-06) 02:00 UTC+8 (same instant as 18:00 UTC) (5e-07, 1e-06) ``` The last row is the timezone case: an aware timestamp in UTC+8 lands on the same instant as 18:00 UTC and gets the discount, rather than being compared as a bare 02:00 wall clock and missing the window To see it end to end, put the same `off_peak_pricing` block on a deployment in your proxy config, set `hours_utc` so it covers the current UTC time, send a real request to /v1/chat/completions, and check the spend on /ui/?page=logs against the same request made outside the window ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Windows are UTC only, no named timezones - Naive timestamps are treated as already being UTC - Not exposed yet on deployment-level custom pricing params - Boundary-crossing requests bill at completion time, not request start - Off-peak replaces tier rates rather than discounting them proportionally ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(ui): show key edit for team members granted /key/update
signals.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reproduction against a local proxy on `localhost:4000` with the dashboard dev server pointed at it. Setup runs as proxy admin; verification runs as a regular team member. 1. Create a team and note its `team_id` ```bash curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/team/new \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_alias": "sa-edit-demo"}' ``` 2. Add a regular member (role `user`) to the team ```bash curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/team/member_add \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_id": "<TEAM_ID>", "member": {"role": "user", "user_id": "<MEMBER_USER_ID>"}}' ``` 3. Grant the team's members the `/key/update` permission ```bash curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/team/permissions_update \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_id": "<TEAM_ID>", "team_member_permissions": ["/key/info", "/key/health", "/key/update"]}' ``` 4. Create a service account key for the team (its `user_id` is null by design) ```bash curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/key/service-account/generate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_id": "<TEAM_ID>", "metadata": {"service_account_id": "sa-edit-demo"}}' ``` 5. Sign in to the dashboard as the team member from step 2, open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-keys, click the service account key, then open the Settings tab Before this change the Settings tab shows no Edit button for that key. After this change the Edit Settings button appears; opening it shows the safe operational fields editable (key alias, models, rate limits, metadata, guardrails, tags, prompts, lifecycle) while a banner at the top explains that budgets, allowed routes, access scope, and organization or team assignment can only be changed by a team or proxy admin. Those sensitive fields are disabled, and even if the form value were present it is stripped from the update payload, so a permission-only member cannot broaden the key. Saving a change to a safe field succeeds. The route case is worth calling out. The backend rejects setting a non-empty `allowed_routes` from a non-admin, but it treats an empty list as "not set" and lets it through, so a permission-only member who could edit that field would be able to clear the restriction and turn a route-restricted key into a full-access one. The form locks that field for non-privileged editors to close the gap. I will attach before/after screenshots of the Settings tab. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes The dashboard hid every key mutation control behind a single check that allowed only proxy admins, team admins, and the key owner. Service account keys have a null `user_id`, so the ownership branch never matched, and the check never looked at team member permissions. A team member holding `/key/update` was therefore unable to edit their team's service account keys from the UI even though the backend authorizes that edit. The Settings tab now shows the Edit Settings button when the caller is a member of the key's team and that team grants `/key/update`, mirroring `can_team_member_execute_key_management_endpoint` on the server. Delete, regenerate, and reset-spend remain gated on admin or owner as before, so a permission-only member gains edit access without inheriting admin-only actions. Exposing the edit form to a permission-only member surfaces fields the backend treats as admin-only, plus controls that would weaken safety or escalate access. The route-restriction case is one sharp edge: the server rejects a non-empty `allowed_routes` from a non-admin but treats an empty list as "not set", so clearing the field is allowed and would let a member turn a route-restricted key into a full-access one. Guardrails are another: a delegated editor changing `guardrails`, toggling `disable_global_guardrails`, or swapping `policies` could bypass policy enforcement on the key. To keep the form aligned with backend authorization and close those gaps, a non-privileged editor gets the sensitive set disabled and stripped from the submit payload: allowed routes, key type, budgets (max budget, reset period, budget windows), passthrough routes, guardrails, policies, vector stores, MCP servers and groups, agents and access groups, and organization or team assignment. Agents and access groups matter here because the backend has no team-scope check on them for team keys, so leaving them editable would be another escalation. What stays editable is the safe operational set: key alias, models (bounded to the team's models server-side), rate limits, metadata, tags, prompts, and lifecycle. Tests cover the new `canTeamMemberUpdateKey` helper, the Edit Settings button appearing for a permitted member on a service account key and staying hidden without the grant, and the edit form disabling and stripping the full sensitive set for a non-privileged editor while leaving it intact for a privileged one.

signals.title: feat(proxy): add filters to exclude health-check logs
signals.text: Health-check probes (/health/readiness, /health/liveliness, /health/liveness) are excluded from the uvicorn access log by default. Users can extend the exclusion list via litellm_settings.log_filters.excluded_uvicorn_access_paths, or set exclude_health_check_paths: false to see the default paths logged again. ## Relevant issues + https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/28325 + https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/18992 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Adds `litellm_settings.log_filters` to the proxy config, giving operators a first-class way to drop noisy paths from the uvicorn access log without writing a custom Python logging filter or passing `--log_config`. By default, health-check probes (`/health/readiness`, `/health/liveliness`, `/health/liveness`) are excluded from the access log, since these are typically polled by Kubernetes at a high frequency and produce most of the noise. `excluded_uvicorn_access_paths` lets users extend that list with their own paths, and `exclude_health_check_paths: false` turns the default exclusion off entirely if someone wants those probes logged again. A path listed explicitly in `excluded_uvicorn_access_paths` is always excluded, even when `exclude_health_check_paths` is false. The filter is attached directly to the `uvicorn.access` logger via `logging.Filter`, after uvicorn's own logging setup runs but during normal proxy config parsing, so it survives config reloads and works the same whether or not JSON logging is enabled. ```yaml litellm_settings: log_filters: # optional: extends the built-in health-check exclusion list, doesn't replace it excluded_uvicorn_access_paths: - /my/custom/noisy/endpoint # optional: defaults to true; set to false to see health-check probes logged again exclude_health_check_paths: false ``` ⚠️ Note on CI: two unrelated test failures appear in this PR's CI run, `test_can_key_call_model_wildcard_access[key_models4-bedrockz/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-False]` and `test_can_team_access_model[bedrockz/anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-team_models5-False]` in `tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_auth_checks.py`. Both are pre-existing on `litellm_oss_daily_2026_07_10` and reproduce in a clean worktree of that branch with none of this PR's changes applied, so they're unrelated to this change. `git diff` between this branch and the base branch touches nothing under `litellm/proxy/auth_checks.py` or `litellm/proxy/auth/`.

signals.title: chore(release): backport 11 staging PRs onto patch-1.92.0rc2 for the 1.92.0 stable cut
signals.text: ## Relevant issues This backports eleven already-merged `litellm_internal_staging` PRs onto `patch-1.92.0rc2` (the branch cut at the `v1.92.0-rc.2` tag) so they ride the pending `1.92.0` stable release. Seven were requested for the release; the other four are prerequisites those seven need to compile and pass their own tests on this older line, without which the requested picks would be dead on arrival. No version bump: the branch's `pyproject.toml` already holds the final `1.92.0`, and `v1.92.0` has not shipped anywhere yet (no DockerHub/GHCR image, no git tag, no `release/v1.92.0` branch), so the picks ride the pending version rather than bumping it. This matches the rc1 -> rc2 backport, which was also bump-less. ## Linear ticket ## What is included (staging merge order) Requested for the release - #32542 fix(guardrails): walk Responses-API text taxonomy in shared content helpers - #32578 fix(bedrock): keep mid-conversation system messages in place for Claude Invoke - #32655 feat(otel): emit the gen_ai.client.operation.exception event on failed LLM calls - #32831 fix(bedrock): gate in-place system role messages on model support for Claude Invoke - #32882 fix(bedrock): flag mapped Claude 4.8+ entries with supports_mid_conversation_system - #32873 refactor(fallback-generalizations): split rules into routing and provider-neutral capability kinds - #32874 fix(anthropic): thread real provider through capability probes instead of pinning anthropic Prerequisites (required for the above to work on this line; each is itself a merged staging PR) - #32389 fix(utils): resolve bedrock regional inference profiles to regional pricing in get_model_info; #32873's cost-ladder test fails without it (regional ids fall back to bare pricing) - #32701 feat: add Meta Model API provider and muse-spark-1.1; #32874 patches a class this PR introduces (JSONProviderAnthropicMessagesConfig) - #32867 fix(anthropic): translate adaptive thinking/effort to pre-4.6 model support; #32874 modifies a method this PR introduces (_translate_adaptive_effort_for_non_adaptive_model) - #32739 test: add /v1/messages to supported_endpoints schema enum; follow-up of #32701 that keeps the model-cost JSON schema canary green once muse-spark advertises /v1/messages Every commit is a `git cherry-pick -x` of the corresponding staging squash/merge; there is no hand-written code and no version-bump, lock, or UI-artifact commit (no production `.tsx` is touched). ## Adaptation notes Four picks diverge from their staging source; the rest are byte-for-byte (patch-id verbatim). - #32701: the new `test_meta_provider.py` shipped without a local-cost-map fixture, so its four muse-spark model-info tests passed only when an earlier test happened to leave the bundled cost map in `litellm.model_cost`; run in isolation they failed because `muse-spark-1.1` is a day-0 model not yet on the remote `main` map. Added the same `local_model_cost_map` fixture that sibling day-0 model tests use, pinning the bundled map for those four tests. signals.title: fix(streaming_chunk_builder): handle empty choices and missing delta role in build_base_response
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes the `IndexError: list index out of range` in `stream_chunk_builder` reported on `v1.93.0-rc.1` when streaming providers emit usage-only chunks with `choices: []`. ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `ChunkProcessor.build_base_response` previously assumed that the first chunk containing a `choices` key also had a non-empty `choices` array with `choices[0].delta.role`. Some streaming providers (for example Anthropic with usage-only events) can send a chunk where `choices` is empty before content chunks arrive. This caused: ``` role = first_chunk_with_choices["choices"][0]["delta"]["role"] IndexError: list index out of range ``` This change makes the role extraction defensive: if the first chunk with choices has an non-empty choices array and the first choice's delta contains a role, use it; otherwise default to `role = "assistant"`. - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`: defensive role lookup with fallback. - `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_chunk_builder_utils_empty_choices.py`: regression tests for empty choices and missing delta role. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ``` $ .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_chunk_builder_utils_empty_choices.py -v ... 2 passed $ .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py -v ... 16 passed ``` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(batches): don't crash logging when a completed batch has no output file
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - All-error batches finish with an error file only, no output file - Retrieving such a batch crashed the gateway's success logging - The completed-batch retrieve never reached the spend logs How it solves it: - Treat a completed batch with no output file as empty - Record zero cost and usage instead of raising ## User Flow Before: the poll that sees the all-error batch complete is missing from the gateway's spend records, and the gateway console prints a file-retrieval error when it runs 1. They upload their batch input with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (purpose=batch, target_model_names=gpt-5.5), every JSONL line asking for an out-of-range temperature, and get back a long gateway file id 2. They create the batch with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches using that input_file_id and get back a batch id with "status": "validating" 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} with their virtual key until the response shows "status": "completed" with "output_file_id": null and a real "error_file_id" 4. They open GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?api_key=<their virtual key> and find a batch-retrieve row for every poll except the final one: the completed poll was never recorded, and the console printed "ValueError: Output file id is None cannot retrieve file content" when it ran After: the completed poll is recorded like every other one, at zero spend, with a clean console 1. They upload their batch input with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (purpose=batch, target_model_names=gpt-5.5), every JSONL line asking for an out-of-range temperature, and get back a long gateway file id 2. They create the batch with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches using that input_file_id and get back a batch id with "status": "validating" 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} with their virtual key until the response shows "status": "completed" with "output_file_id": null and a real "error_file_id" 4. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?api_key=<their virtual key> now lists every poll including the final one, whose row shows "spend": 0.0, and no error appears in the console ## Relevant issues Fixes #33987 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4852 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live e2e QA at the current head is in progress; the author's original regression-test proof is retained below until it lands `tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_batch_no_output_file_is_zero`: with the guard removed the test fails with `ValueError: Output file id is None cannot retrieve file content`, the exact error from the issue; with the fix it passes, returning zero cost, zero usage, and no models while asserting the output-file fetch is never attempted ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix

signals.title: fix(responses): honor caller stream flag when provider forces SSE
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `chatgpt/*` ignores a caller's `stream: false` since v1.90.0 - `/v1/responses` hands back raw SSE instead of JSON - `/v1/chat/completions` fails with `Unknown items in responses API response: []` How it solves it: - Transport streaming and response shape are decided separately - Only the caller's own `stream` value picks the shape - Providers that force SSE are still read as streams ## User Flow Before: a developer calling a ChatGPT subscription model without streaming gets back something they cannot parse 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"stream": false` and a ChatGPT subscription model 2. A 200 comes back, but `content-type` is `text/event-stream` and the body is 12 SSE frames instead of one JSON object 3. Their client breaks on the string; n8n reports `Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'object' in data:` followed by the whole stream 4. They try the same model at POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with no streaming 5. That returns 500 with `Unknown items in responses API response: []`, so neither endpoint serves a plain response After: the same two requests come back in the shape the caller asked for 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"stream": false` 2. A 200 comes back with `content-type: application/json` and a single response object whose `status` is `completed` 3. Their client parses it normally, with no SSE frames in the body 4. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions 5. That returns 200 with an assistant message and a `finish_reason` of `stop` 6. Sending either endpoint with `"stream": true` still streams exactly as before ## Relevant issues Fixes #34094 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a live proxy hitting the real ChatGPT subscription backend, with `chatgpt/gpt-5.4` as the only entry in `model_list` and no api_key (the provider reads the stored subscription token) Response bodies are reported as content type, SSE frame count and body byte count rather than pasted in full, because they carry account-scoped identifiers. Body bytes exclude headers The before run is the current base commit with nothing applied; the after run is this branch. Both were run back to back against the same account and prompt Commands, run once per proxy: ```bash for s in false true; do curl -sS -D - -o body.txt http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\": \"m-gpt54\", \"input\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"say hi in 3 words\"}], \"stream\": $s}" \ | grep -iE "^(HTTP/|content-type)" grep -c '^data: ' body.txt wc -c < body.txt done for s in false true; do curl -sS -D - -o body.txt http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\": \"m-gpt54\", \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"say hi in 3 words\"}], \"stream\": $s}" \ | grep -iE "^(HTTP/|content-type)" grep -c '^data: ' body.txt wc -c < body.txt done ``` ### Before, at `b0fac57fe4` | request | status | content-type | SSE frames | body bytes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `/v1/responses` `stream: false` | 200 | text/event-stream | 12 | 29661 | | `/v1/chat/completions` non-streaming | 500 | application/json | 0 | 240 | | `/v1/responses` `stream: true` | 200 | text/event-stream | 12 | 29658 | The non-streaming Responses call is served as a full SSE stream, and the 500 body is the `Unknown items in responses API response: []` error ### After, at `f9a1e98780` | request | status | content-type | SSE frames | body bytes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `/v1/responses` `stream: false` | 200 | application/json | 0 | 9688 | | `/v1/chat/completions` non-streaming | 200 | application/json | 0 | 443 | | `/v1/responses` `stream: true` | 200 | text/event-stream | 12 | 29661 | | `/v1/chat/completions` `stream: true` | 200 | text/event-stream | 5 | 783 | The Responses body is a single response object with `"status": "completed"` and one output item, the chat body carries an assistant message with `"finish_reason": "stop"`, and both streaming calls still stream, ending in `data: [DONE]` for the chat one `/v1/messages` is not covered because this change only touches the Responses handlers; that endpoint does not reach them ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes The two Responses handlers in `litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py` decided whether to hand the caller a streaming iterator by reading `stream` off the provider payload: ```python stream = bool(stream or data.get("stream")) ... is_stream_request = bool(stream) ``` `data` there is what goes out to the provider, not what the caller sent. `ChatGPTResponsesAPIConfig.transform_responses_api_request` sets `request["stream"] = True` unconditionally because the Codex backend only serves SSE, so `data.get("stream")` is always true for this provider and a caller that sent `stream: false` was silently moved onto the streaming path. Other Responses providers are unaffected; chatgpt is the only one whose transform touches `stream` at all On `/v1/responses` that meant a raw SSE body was returned to a caller expecting one JSON object. On `/v1/chat/completions` the Responses bridge fell into `_collect_response_from_stream`, which keeps only the `response` from the `response.completed` event; when the Codex backend emits that event with an empty `output` the request failed with `Unknown items in responses API response: []`. The recovery path added for that case in `_recover_output_items_from_raw_sse` re-parses the raw SSE from `logging_obj.model_call_details["original_response"]`, and the only place that populates it for this provider is `transform_response_api_response`, which lives on the non-streaming path and was no longer being reached That merge line came from #30189, which set out to stop provider transforms that force `stream: true` from being sent through the non-streaming branch, ChatGPT Codex models included. The transport half of that is right and this PR keeps it. The problem is that a single `stream` variable was carrying two decisions at once: what to pass to httpx, and whether to return an iterator or an aggregated body. Merging the provider payload into it fixed the transport half and silently changed the response shape along with it. A later refactor lifted the merged value into `is_stream_request`, which renamed the variable without splitting the two decisions This keeps transport streaming exactly as it was, so a provider that only serves SSE is still read as a stream, and narrows the response-shape decision to the caller's own `stream` value, captured before the transform runs. When the provider forces SSE for a non-streaming caller the body is read and aggregated through the existing path. The bridge half of #30189, which preserves a top-level `stream=True` into the Responses request, is untouched Tests cover both handlers: a caller sending `stream: false` (and one omitting it) against a provider that forces streaming gets an aggregated `ResponsesAPIResponse`, and a caller that asks for streaming still gets an iterator. The two existing `..._streams_when_provider_transform_adds_stream` tests from #30189 are untouched apart from one fixture line, so the transport-level behaviour they lock in stays covered, and the streaming rows in the after table confirm it end to end ## Caveats (if any) - Proof uses `chatgpt/gpt-5.4`; codex-suffixed models were refused by this account - Rebased onto `b0fac57fe4`; earlier proof commits in this PR's history are stale ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(proxy): serve the Claude Code gateway protocol under /claude_code_gateway
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Claude Code can now use a LiteLLM proxy as a first-class gateway - Anthropic published a gateway protocol; LiteLLM did not speak it How it solves it: - Serve the protocol under `/claude_code_gateway`, off by default - OAuth device sign-in reuses the existing proxy SSO flow - Add managed settings and OTLP telemetry ingestion endpoints ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4698 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a live proxy on `localhost:4000` at commit `575da405f231b43d55eaabd55057140f60f84629`, started with a config that sets `general_settings.enable_claude_code_gateway: true` plus a sample `claude_code_gateway_managed_settings` block ``` $ curl -s $B/claude_code_gateway/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server {"issuer":"http://localhost:4000/claude_code_gateway","device_authorization_endpoint":"http://localhost:4000/claude_code_gateway/oauth/device_authorization","token_endpoint":"http://localhost:4000/claude_code_gateway/oauth/token","grant_types_supported":["urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code","refresh_token"]} $ curl -s -X POST $B/claude_code_gateway/oauth/device_authorization {"device_code":"cli-xAA2Vt_VEdTBlOE3HchbhJ3YzFBtLw7q","user_code":"4F9U-XACB","verification_uri":"http://localhost:4000/sso/key/generate?source=litellm-cli&key=cli-xAA2Vt_VEdTBlOE3HchbhJ3YzFBtLw7q","verification_uri_complete":"http://localhost:4000/sso/key/generate?source=litellm-cli&key=cli-xAA2Vt_VEdTBlOE3HchbhJ3YzFBtLw7q&user_code=4F9U-XACB","expires_in":600,"interval":5} # token poll before the browser SSO leg completes $ curl -s -X POST $B/claude_code_gateway/oauth/token -d 'grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code' -d device_code=$DEVICE_CODE {"error":"authorization_pending"} [HTTP 400] # refresh tokens are intentionally not issued; the client re-signs in $ curl -s -X POST $B/claude_code_gateway/oauth/token -d grant_type=refresh_token -d refresh_token=x {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"This gateway does not issue refresh tokens; sign in again"} [HTTP 401] $ curl -s -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' $B/claude_code_gateway/managed/settings HTTP/1.1 200 OK etag: "657fd7729a2167ee9530d04017905bd00fe711be5991f7cd297dc6d42740cd40" {"env":{"CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY":"1"},"permissions":{"defaultMode":"acceptEdits"}} # conditional GET with the returned ETag $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'If-None-Match: <etag>' $B/claude_code_gateway/managed/settings 304 $ for sig in metrics logs traces; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "/v1/$sig %{http_code}\n" -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' --data-binary @otlp $B/claude_code_gateway/v1/$sig; done /v1/metrics 200 /v1/logs 200 /v1/traces 200 # bearer auth is enforced on the authenticated endpoints $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST $B/claude_code_gateway/v1/metrics 401 ``` The `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` inference legs reuse the proxy's existing Anthropic Messages handlers unchanged, so provider routing, streaming, model access control, and spend tracking all apply as they do today. The browser sign-in leg reuses the shipped proxy SSO device flow, which needs an IdP configured, so it is not exercised in the transcript above ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Anthropic published a protocol for third-party Claude Code gateways (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway). Their reference gateway is deliberately minimal (YAML only, Claude models only, no UI or SCIM). This wires the same protocol into LiteLLM so an existing proxy can act as the gateway while keeping LiteLLM's provider breadth, routing, and governance Everything lives in a new lazy-loaded router at `litellm/proxy/anthropic_endpoints/gateway_endpoints.py`, mounted under `/claude_code_gateway` and gated by `general_settings.enable_claude_code_gateway` (off by default), so nothing changes for existing deployments The surface added, all same-origin under the base so Claude Code's fixed path behavior works: - `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` for RFC 8414 discovery, advertising only the device-code and refresh grants - `POST /oauth/device_authorization` and `POST /oauth/token` for the RFC 8628 device flow. The device code is an opaque 256-bit secret stored hashed, single-use, and rate limited, reusing the proxy's existing `cli_sso_session_cache` and SSO verification page. On success the token endpoint mints the same session JWT the LiteLLM CLI already issues, so the bearer token flows through `user_api_key_auth` and every downstream model and budget check - `POST /v1/messages` and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` delegate to the existing Anthropic handlers behind the enable gate - `GET /managed/settings` serves an operator-provided `claude_code_gateway_managed_settings` block with an ETag and If-None-Match handling, and returns 404 when no policy is set so the distinction between no policy and an empty policy is preserved - `POST /v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs`, `/v1/traces` accept OTLP payloads and return 200 Refresh tokens are not issued; the token endpoint returns `invalid_grant` so the client re-signs in through the device flow. OAuth errors use the protocol's `{"error": ...}` envelope and the authenticated endpoints reuse LiteLLM's existing Anthropic error envelope ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/864913c6147549cbaae682144511c2de Requested by: @mateo-berri

signals.title: fix(anthropic): shallow-copy input_schema to prevent caller mutation
signals.text: ## Description The Anthropic→OpenAI tool translation adapter was directly assigning the caller's `input_schema` dict to the `function_chunk["parameters"]` field. A subsequent loop that merges extra kwargs mutated it in place: ```python for k, v in tool.items(): if k not in mapped_tool_params: function_chunk.setdefault("parameters", {}).update({k: v}) ``` This means the caller's original tool definition dict gets mutated every time the adapter runs, breaking reusability of the tool schema across multiple calls. ## Fix Wrap with `dict()` to create a shallow copy before assigning — the extra kwargs loop now mutates the copy, not the original: ```python function_chunk["parameters"] = dict(tool["input_schema"]) ``` ## Related Issue Closes #34510

signals.title: fix(dashscope): select one pricing tier from request input size
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - DashScope cost tracking applies graduated, income-tax-style slicing to `tiered_pricing`, but Alibaba Model Studio picks one tier from a request's total input tokens and bills every token in that request at that tier's rates. Large Qwen requests are logged well under what the provider actually charges - Each token category was tiered independently from zero, so completion tokens selected their own tier and cached input selected a tier from the cached count alone rather than from the request's input size - The proxy's budget reservation path already uses the request-size model via `select_tier_for_input`, so reservation estimates and post-response spend disagreed with each other on the same request How it solves it: - Resolve the tier once in `dashscope/cost_calculator.py` from `usage.prompt_tokens` using `select_tier_for_input`, the selector budget reservation already uses, and apply that one tier's rates to plain input, cached input, completion and reasoning tokens ## Relevant issues Fixes #34729 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I do not have DashScope credentials, so this is the repro script from the issue rather than a live proxy run. It makes no provider call; the token counts are synthetic and the rates come straight out of `model_prices_and_context_window.json`. ``` python - <<'PY' from litellm.llms.dashscope.cost_calculator import cost_per_token from litellm.types.utils import Usage from litellm.utils import get_model_info from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.tiered_pricing import ( select_tier_for_input, tier_rate, ) model = "qwen-flash" input_tokens = 300_000 output_tokens = 2_000 usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=input_tokens, completion_tokens=output_tokens, total_tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, ) actual_input, actual_output = cost_per_token(model, usage) model_info = get_model_info(model=model, custom_llm_provider="dashscope") tier = select_tier_for_input(model_info["tiered_pricing"], input_tokens) expected_input = input_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "input_cost_per_token") expected_output = output_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "output_cost_per_token") print({ "actual_total": actual_input + actual_output, "request_tier_total": expected_input + expected_output, }) PY ``` Before, on `24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c`: ``` {'actual_total': 0.024599999999999997, 'request_tier_total': 0.079} ``` After: ``` {'actual_total': 0.079, 'request_tier_total': 0.079} ``` `qwen-flash` declares `[0, 256000]` at $0.05/M input and `[256000, 1000000]` at $0.25/M input. A 300,000-token request sits in the second tier, so Model Studio charges all 300,000 input tokens at $0.25/M and the 2,000 completion tokens at that tier's $2/M. The old result charged the first 256,000 input tokens at the cheap rate and put the completion tokens in tier 1 entirely, which is 69% under. Reverting only `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` and keeping the new tests gives the failures below, so the regression coverage is genuinely pinned to this fix: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py -q --tb=line E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0246, 0.079, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:96: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.012800249999999999, (256001 * 2.5e-07), rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:127: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.2488, 0.3, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:281: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0015999999999999999, 0.002, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:259: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0474, 0.07379999999999999, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:172: assert False FAILED ...::test_dashscope_cached_tokens_count_toward_tier_selection FAILED ...::test_dashscope_input_above_first_tier_bills_whole_request_at_that_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_output_tokens_do_not_select_their_own_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tier_boundary_is_inclusive_of_range_end FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_exceeding_highest_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_string_costs_exceeding_highest_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_with_caching 7 failed, 3 passed in 1.39s ``` With the fix restored: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/ tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/ -q 193 passed in 23.14s $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_cost_calculator.py -q 80 passed in 4.55s ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` now resolves the tier once per request instead of running four independent graduated calculations. `_calculate_prompt_cost` and `_calculate_completion_cost` take the selected tier rather than the whole `tiered_pricing` list, and read their rates with `tier_rate`, which keeps the existing fallbacks (cached input falls back to the tier's input rate, reasoning falls back to the tier's output rate) and the existing string-cost coercion for YAML-parsed rates. The flat-pricing path for models with no `tiered_pricing` is untouched, as is `calculate_tiered_cost` itself for any caller that wants graduated behaviour. A follow-up commit converts the three annotations the fix touches to PEP 604 / PEP 585 form (`dict | None`, `list[dict] | None`), which keeps the strict-rule budget from moving; the file drops from 8 strict violations to 2. The existing tests in `test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py` asserted the graduated numbers, so they are updated to the request-size expectations. Five cases were added or reworked to cover what the issue asked for: an above-first-tier request billed wholly at that tier, the tier boundary being inclusive of `range_end` (256,000 stays in tier 1, 256,001 moves up), output tokens not selecting their own tier, cached tokens counting toward tier selection, and input beyond the highest declared range falling back to the last tier. The two string-valued-rate regressions from the earlier YAML coercion fix are kept, with expectations recomputed under the new model. ## QA runbook Point a deployment at a DashScope Qwen model with `tiered_pricing` in the cost map (`qwen-flash` or `qwen3-coder-plus`), send one request whose input is comfortably above the first tier's `range_end` and one below it, then compare `spend` on the two `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` rows against the Model Studio console for the same requests. The large request should now be priced entirely at the higher tier rather than partly at the cheap one, and it should match the budget reservation estimate for that request rather than falling short of it. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(anthropic): populate inference_geo from the request so regional pricing applies
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streamed Anthropic usage loses the region it was served from - Regional traffic then gets billed at global rates How it solves it: - Streaming reassembly carries `inference_geo` through - Requested region is the fallback when the response omits it ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming Anthropic traffic out of a US region sees the gateway log no region at all, so regional pricing never applies to any streamed request 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true` 2. The response streams back fine, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at the global price with no region recorded 3. They repeat it on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages with `"stream": true`, and both log the same way 4. Dropping `"stream": true` on any of the three routes does record `us`, so their spend is only correct for non-streaming traffic After: the same streamed requests record the region, so streamed and non-streamed traffic price the same way 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true` 2. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the request served from `us` 3. The same holds on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages with `"stream": true` 4. A request that asks for no region, or that Anthropic serves globally, still records `global` and prices as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4867 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Screen recording of the before and after run, in one video, is in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1786414063855749?thread_ts=1786408619.329699&cid=C0BE49SAUE6). It captured the before at `1d3b64c66f` (current `litellm_internal_staging`) and the after at `82a64de9a2`, and reproduced the runs below Live proxy against the real Anthropic API, real spend, `claude-opus-4-8`, one request per route with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true`. Region and cost were read off the standard logging payload ```bash H=(-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01') curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions "${H[@]}" -d @chat_geo_stream.json curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d @msg_geo_stream.json curl -sS localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d @pt_geo_stream.json ``` Before, at `1d3b64c66f`, every streamed route drops the region: ``` route=acompletion geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 route=anthropic_messages geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 route=pass_through_endpoint geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 ``` After, at `82a64de9a2`, all three keep it: ``` route=acompletion geo=us cost=0.14788949999999998 route=anthropic_messages geo=us cost=0.14788949999999998 route=pass_through_endpoint geo=us cost=0.14799949999999998 ``` The cost barely moves because the uplift itself is #34850, and the point here is that without the region reaching cost calculation that PR can never fire on streamed traffic. The same three routes without `"stream": true` already recorded `us` before this change, on this branch they still do ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Merged with `litellm_internal_staging`, absorbing the #36447 speed plumbing - Cache tokens still miss the geo uplift until #34850 lands ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/13d7b3dbf5a641f0a24aa0b48893d315 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit d88193eea52b0095df6bb61d83179608497c9350. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: feat(mcp): scope gateway session bearers to the RFC 8707 resource
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Session bearers carried the user's whole MCP entitlement, never one server - The RFC 8707 `resource` param spec clients send was ignored How it solves it: - A per-server `resource` seals that server through flow, code, and session tokens - Admission intersects the sealed scope against resolved grants, fail closed ## User Flow Before: a user connects an MCP client to one gateway server, and the token the client walks away with silently works on every server that user can reach 1. Their MCP client POSTs https://litellm-domain/register and receives a `client_id` 2. The client opens https://litellm-domain/authorize?...&resource=https://litellm-domain/mcp/github in the browser; the user lands on the LiteLLM connect page and approves 3. The client exchanges the code at POST https://litellm-domain/token (sending the same `resource`) and receives a bearer token 4. The client lists tools at POST https://litellm-domain/mcp/github and sees that server's tools 5. The same bearer POSTed to https://litellm-domain/mcp/internal-billing, a server the user can also reach but the client never asked for, lists that server's tools too 6. Anyone holding that one client's token can act on every MCP server in the user's entitlement After: the same connection walk hands the client a token that works only on the server it asked for 1. Their MCP client POSTs https://litellm-domain/register and receives a `client_id` 2. The client opens https://litellm-domain/authorize?...&resource=https://litellm-domain/mcp/github in the browser; the user lands on the LiteLLM connect page and approves 3. The client exchanges the code at POST https://litellm-domain/token (sending the same `resource`) and receives a bearer token 4. The client lists tools at POST https://litellm-domain/mcp/github and sees that server's tools 5. The same bearer POSTed to https://litellm-domain/mcp/internal-billing returns an empty tool list, and redeeming a code for a different `resource` than it was issued for fails with `invalid_target` 6. Anyone holding that client's token can act only on the one server the user connected it to ## Relevant issues - Reads the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter at `/authorize` and `/token`; a value resolving to exactly one gateway-managed oauth2 server scopes the session to it, and the token endpoint rejects a conflicting redemption with `invalid_target` on both grants - The scope is a restriction, never a grant: it intersects the admitted subject's resolved server set after every union (operator-open and the exception fallback included), so a scoped bearer can never reach servers outside its scope and a resolver fault can never widen it - Absent, aggregate, foreign, unknown, or non-gateway-managed resources keep today's flow byte for byte; unscoped tokens are minted without the new claim so they stay byte-compatible with pods that predate it ## Linear ticket Part of LIT-4917 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on `localhost:4917` at commit fcb1a5e16e, real Postgres, real public upstream (`mcp.deepwiki.com`). Servers: `wiki_oauth` (gateway-managed oauth2, `allow_all_keys`, a vaulted per-user token seeded via `POST /v1/mcp/server/{id}/oauth-user-credential`) and `deepwiki` (auth none, `allow_all_keys`), so an unscoped session reaches both and the only narrowing in play is the sealed scope ``` == W1. DCR register (open /register, loopback redirect) == client_id: llm_dcrc_evI4WCg... == W2. scoped authorize (resource=/mcp/wiki_oauth): connect page interlude, no silent code == HTTP/1.1 303 See Other location: http://localhost:4917/ui/connect?connect_flow=mkqfsitmnGejC4ZqMs1y4aSX-dubtw4X&connect_client=... == W3. finish the connect page (POST /authorize/complete): code delivered to the client == 303 -> http://127.0.0.1:8976/callback?code=llm_gcode_9dVUpRisAWg9x3... == W4. token exchange (resource echoed per RFC 8707) == token_type: Bearer | error: None == W5. scoped bearer at ITS OWN server /mcp/wiki_oauth == tools (3): ['wiki_oauth-ask_question', 'wiki_oauth-read_wiki_contents', 'wiki_oauth-read_wiki_structure'] == W6. SAME bearer at /mcp/deepwiki (granted via allow_all_keys, but OUTSIDE the sealed scope) == tools (0): [] == W7. redeem a scoped code for a DIFFERENT resource == {"error":"invalid_target","error_description":"resource does not match the scope this code was issued for"} == W8. unscoped walk (no resource): flow unchanged, bearer reaches deepwiki via allow_all_keys == location: http://localhost:4917/ui/connect?connect_flow=Qhd48usFCKWlRLT47YT9qyJnaKeRtQUq&connect_client=... tools (3): ['deepwiki-ask_question', 'deepwiki-read_wiki_contents', 'deepwiki-read_wiki_structure'] ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Scoped flows still show the connect page; every code mint stays POST-bound - The connect-page skip lands in the follow-up PR behind a real intent step - Rolling deploy: old pods reject new SCOPED bearers with the standard re-auth challenge - Unscoped artifacts (flow cookie, code, bearer) carry no new key on the wire ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit fcb1a5e16e19f19d3d638b46233b7fa2e06f521a. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: feat(voyage): add voyage-4 family + voyage-context-4 and fix contextual list[str] input
signals.text: ## Summary Adds the missing Voyage AI `voyage-4` embedding family and `voyage-context-4` to the model cost/context map, and fixes contextual-embeddings input handling so a plain `list[str]` no longer 400s. ### Models added (both root and backup json) - `voyage/voyage-context-4` — $0.12/M, 120K context (contextualized endpoint) - `voyage/voyage-4`, `voyage/voyage-4-large`, `voyage/voyage-4-lite` — 32K context - `voyage/voyage-4-nano` — $0 (open-weight), 32K context ### Contextual embeddings input normalization Voyage's `/contextualizedembeddings` API rejects a flat `list[str]` unless `input_type="query"` or auto-chunking is enabled. `transform_embedding_request` now normalizes input: a single `str` and non-query flat `list[str]` are sent flat with `enable_auto_chunking`, a query `list[str]` is passed as-is, and `list[list[str]]` is passed through unchanged. ### Tests Adds pricing-registration checks for the voyage-4 family + context-4, `voyage-context-4` model detection, and input-normalization cases (flat, query, document, single, nested) in `tests/llm_translation/test_voyage_ai.py`.

signals.title: fix(vertex_ai): translate /v1/embeddings batch rows to the Gemini embedding shape
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex batch `/v1/embeddings` rows fail: "no such field: 'contents'" - The OpenAI `input` is dropped entirely on those rows - Embedding result rows come back as raw Vertex jsonl How it solves it: - Route each jsonl line by its own `url` - Embeddings lines emit an `EmbedContentRequest` row - Embedding output rows transform into OpenAI embeddings responses ## User Flow Before: a developer running an embeddings batch job through the gateway sees the batch report success while every row inside it failed and the text they asked to embed was never sent 1. They write `batch_embeddings.jsonl` where every line targets the embeddings endpoint, e.g. `{"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": "hello world from litellm batch"}}` 2. They upload it with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (`purpose=batch`, `model=gemini-embedding-001`) and get back a `file-...` id 3. They create the job with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches passing that `input_file_id` and `"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"`, and a batch id comes back 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reports `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null`, which looks like success 5. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and every row is an error, `{"custom_id": "req-1", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": "... EmbedContentRequest ... no such field: 'contents'"}}`, with not one embedding in the file After: the same job returns one OpenAI embeddings response per input line 1. They write the same `batch_embeddings.jsonl` with `"url": "/v1/embeddings"` lines 2. They upload it with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (`purpose=batch`, `model=gemini-embedding-001`) and get back a `file-...` id 3. They create the job with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches passing that `input_file_id` and `"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"`, and a batch id comes back 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reports `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null` 5. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and get one row per input line, e.g. `{"custom_id": "req-1", "response": {"status_code": 200, "body": {"object": "list", "data": [{"embedding": [...], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 7}}}, "error": null}` 6. A line whose `input` was an array of N texts comes back as one row whose `data` holds N embeddings, index-aligned with the input array ## Relevant issues Fixes #35638 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4920 Resolves LIT-5123 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live Vertex AI batch runs against a real project in `us-central1`, staging through a real GCS bucket; no mocks anywhere. Latest re-verification after the staging merge: before on `litellm_internal_staging` at `f03df1bb42`, after at the PR tip `de77711cf9`. The earlier full-coverage runs at `627d2755da` and `bf723fa9c1` are kept below <details open><summary>Re-verification: the same 2-entry batch before at f03df1bb42 and after at de77711cf9</summary> Input file: `req-1` with a single string input, `req-2` with an array of 2 texts, both lines `"url": "/v1/embeddings"`. Identical commands both times: upload `curl -X POST http://localhost:<port>/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -F purpose=batch -F 'model=gemini-embedding-001' -F file=@batch_embeddings.jsonl`, create via `POST /v1/batches` with the returned `input_file_id` and `"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"`, poll `GET /v1/batches/<id>` to `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null` (~4 min), then fetch `GET /v1/files/<output_file_id>/content` Before at `f03df1bb42`, what LiteLLM staged to GCS is chat-shaped with the customer texts replaced by a single space and req-2's 2-text array collapsed into one row ```json {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-1"}}} {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-2"}}} ``` and the content fetch returned 2 rows with zero embeddings ```json {"id": "batch_req_7ec23587-6414-415d-a686-4b4399251fec", "custom_id": "req-2", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": "{\"code\":3,\"space\":\"generic\",\"message\":\"Failed to parse JSON into proto: google.cloud.aiplatform.master.EmbedContentRequest with status: invalid JSON in google.cloud.aiplatform.master.EmbedContentRequest, near 1:13 (offset 12): no such field: 'contents'\"}"}} {"id": "batch_req_2c1a60ce-b35a-40e5-b50a-d5899bf25c34", "custom_id": "req-1", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": "{\"code\":3,\"space\":\"generic\",\"message\":\"Failed to parse JSON into proto: google.cloud.aiplatform.master.EmbedContentRequest with status: invalid JSON in google.cloud.aiplatform.master.EmbedContentRequest, near 1:13 (offset 12): no such field: 'contents'\"}"}} ``` After at `de77711cf9`, the GCS staging is per-element `EmbedContentRequest` rows with the texts intact ```json {"key": "req-1", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "hello world from litellm batch"}]}}} {"key": "req-2#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "first text"}]}}} {"key": "req-2#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "second text"}]}}} ``` and the content fetch returned one OpenAI row per entry, embedding arrays trimmed here ```json {"id": "batch_req_0bf52833-0663-45b3-ac9a-cfda7f4bb030", "custom_id": "req-2", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id": "", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "data": [{"embedding": [-0.029436894, 0.024541076, "...3072 floats"], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}, {"embedding": [0.01739435, 0.002744379, "...3072 floats"], "index": 1, "object": "embedding"}], "object": "list", "usage": {"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 4, "total_tokens": 4}}}, "error": null} {"id": "batch_req_eedcbbb6-19bc-42f9-acd3-7c13522f146e", "custom_id": "req-1", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id": "", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "data": [{"embedding": [-0.020151937, 0.020540899, "...3072 floats"], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}], "object": "list", "usage": {"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 7}}}, "error": null} ``` cosine between a live online `/v1/embeddings` call for `"first text"` and the batch `req-2` `data[0]` vector is 1.000000, against `data[1]` it is 0.806420, so `data[0]` aligns with `input[0]` specifically </details> <details><summary>After: one real batch job over a mixed single / array / nested-combined input</summary> Input file, uploaded with `curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -F purpose=batch -F 'model=gemini-embedding-001' -F file=@batch_embeddings.jsonl` ```json {"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": "hello world from litellm batch"}} period followed the Renaissance in music"], "dimensions": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"custom_id": "req-5", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": ["ONE: submarines navigate using sonar", "TWO: sourdough bread needs a starter culture", "THREE: the Voyager probes left the solar system"]}} {"custom_id": "req-6", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": [["a caption about mountains", "and a second combined part about rivers"]]}} ``` what LiteLLM actually wrote to GCS, 7 Vertex rows for 4 entries ```json {"key": "req-1", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "hello world from litellm batch"}]}}} {"key": "req-4#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "ALPHA: photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"key": "req-4#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "BETA: the Baroque period followed the Renaissance in music"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"key": "req-5#0/3", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "ONE: submarines navigate using sonar"}]}}} {"key": "req-5#1/3", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "TWO: sourdough bread needs a starter culture"}]}}} {"key": "req-5#2/3",
