signal.title: fix(model_prices): add missing OpenAI models and refresh stale limits and deprecation dates
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `chat-latest` and `gpt-5.6-cyber` missing from the cost map - Daybreak aliases missing, so their calls cost $0 - Sonnet 4.6 and DeepSeek V4 output caps too low - Retired OpenAI completion models carry no deprecation date How it solves it: - Adds four OpenAI entries from the official pricing and model pages - Raises Sonnet 4.6 to 128k and DeepSeek V4 to 384k output - Adds `deprecation_date` for the 2026-09-28 OpenAI retirements - Adds Gemini Robotics ER 1.6 shutdown date plus Claude structured-output flags ## User Flow Before: a developer calling the newest OpenAI models through the gateway gets refused or billed nothing, so their spend dashboard is wrong 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "chat-latest"` 2. The call is rejected as an unknown model, and adding it by hand logs the request at $0 spend 3. They ask for `"model": "claude-sonnet-4-6"` with `"max_tokens": 100000` and the gateway reports the model only allows 64000 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows those requests with no cost attached After: the same calls go through and land in the logs with real cost 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "chat-latest"` 2. A 200 comes back with the assistant reply, and the request is billed at $5 per million input and $30 per million output 3. They ask for `"model": "claude-sonnet-4-6"` with `"max_tokens": 100000` and get a normal streamed answer 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows those requests at non-zero spend, and GET https://litellm-domain/model/info reports 128000 max output tokens ## Relevant issues Supports #26900 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) Note on tests: this is a data-only change to the cost map, so it is covered by the existing registry schema and cost-map suites rather than new test files ## What changed, with sources New entries, all priced and sized from OpenAI's own pages - `chat-latest`: $5 / $0.50 cached / $30 per 1M, 400k context, 128k max output, text plus image in, from https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing and https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/chat-latest - `gpt-5.6-cyber`: $12.50 / $1.25 cached / $15.625 cache write / $75 per 1M, 2x input and 1.5x output above 272k, 400k context, 128k max output, reasoning and computer use supported, from https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing and https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-5.6-cyber - `daybreak-red-latest`: documented alias of `gpt-5.6-cyber` with matching pricing, 400k context, from https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/daybreak-red-latest - `daybreak-blue-latest`: documented alias of `gpt-5.6-sol` with matching pricing, 1,050,000 context, from https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/daybreak-blue-latest Stale limits - `claude-sonnet-4-6` max output 64000 -> 128000, per the model comparison table at https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/models/overview - `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` max output 8192 -> 393216 (the documented 384K), per https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing Deprecation dates, in the existing `YYYY-MM-DD` shape - `babbage-002`, `davinci-002`, `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`: 2026-09-28, per the retirement table at https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations - `gemini/gemini-robotics-er-1.6-preview`: 2026-08-31, per https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations Missing capability flags - `supports_pdf_input` on the four new OpenAI entries, which the repo requires for every vision-capable OpenAI model - `supports_native_structured_output` on `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-fable-5`, signal.title: Gemini native custom api_base sends system_instruction instead of canonical systemInstruction
signal.text: ### Description When using the native Gemini provider with a custom `api_base`, a request containing an OpenAI-style `system` message is serialized with the snake_case JSON key `system_instruction`. Some Gemini-compatible proxies parse this as a duplicate protobuf optional/oneof assignment and return HTTP 400: ```text Invalid value at 'request' (oneof), oneof field '_system_instruction' is already set. Cannot set 'system_instruction' ``` The same endpoint accepts the canonical Gemini REST JSON key `systemInstruction`. ### LiteLLM versions Reproduced with: - 1.91.0 - 1.96.2 (latest available from PyPI when tested) Python 3.13.14 on Windows. ### Minimal reproduction ```python import litellm litellm.completion( model="gemini/gemini-3.6-flash", api_base="https://<custom-gemini-base>/v1beta", api_key="<key>", messages=[ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: ok"}, ], max_tokens=512, ) ``` Actual result: HTTP 400 with the protobuf oneof error above. A user-only request succeeds, so the failure is specifically triggered when LiteLLM extracts a system message. ### Request-body comparison Sending this directly to `/v1beta/models/<model>:generateContent` succeeds with HTTP 200: ```json { "systemInstruction": { "parts": [{"text": "You are a concise assistant."}] }, "contents": [ {"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "Reply with exactly: ok"}]} ] } ``` Changing only the key to snake_case reproduces HTTP 400: ```json { "system_instruction": { "parts": [{"text": "You are a concise assistant."}] }, "contents": [ {"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "Reply with exactly: ok"}]} ] } ``` ### Suspected source In `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/transformation.py`, the request transformer currently sets: ```python data["system_instruction"] = system_instructions ``` ### Expected behavior For native Gemini REST requests, serialize the system-instruction field using the canonical JSON name `systemInstruction`. This remains accepted by the Gemini REST endpoint and improves compatibility with custom native Gemini endpoints that do not safely handle the snake_case alias.

signal.title: fix(dashscope): select one pricing tier from request input size
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - DashScope cost tracking applies graduated, income-tax-style slicing to `tiered_pricing`, but Alibaba Model Studio picks one tier from a request's total input tokens and bills every token in that request at that tier's rates. Large Qwen requests are logged well under what the provider actually charges - Each token category was tiered independently from zero, so completion tokens selected their own tier and cached input selected a tier from the cached count alone rather than from the request's input size - The proxy's budget reservation path already uses the request-size model via `select_tier_for_input`, so reservation estimates and post-response spend disagreed with each other on the same request How it solves it: - Resolve the tier once in `dashscope/cost_calculator.py` from `usage.prompt_tokens` using `select_tier_for_input`, the selector budget reservation already uses, and apply that one tier's rates to plain input, cached input, completion and reasoning tokens ## Relevant issues Fixes #34729 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I do not have DashScope credentials, so this is the repro script from the issue rather than a live proxy run. It makes no provider call; the token counts are synthetic and the rates come straight out of `model_prices_and_context_window.json`. ``` python - <<'PY' from litellm.llms.dashscope.cost_calculator import cost_per_token from litellm.types.utils import Usage from litellm.utils import get_model_info from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.tiered_pricing import ( select_tier_for_input, tier_rate, ) model = "qwen-flash" input_tokens = 300_000 output_tokens = 2_000 usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=input_tokens, completion_tokens=output_tokens, total_tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, ) actual_input, actual_output = cost_per_token(model, usage) model_info = get_model_info(model=model, custom_llm_provider="dashscope") tier = select_tier_for_input(model_info["tiered_pricing"], input_tokens) expected_input = input_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "input_cost_per_token") expected_output = output_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "output_cost_per_token") print({ "actual_total": actual_input + actual_output, "request_tier_total": expected_input + expected_output, }) PY ``` Before, on `24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c`: ``` {'actual_total': 0.024599999999999997, 'request_tier_total': 0.079} ``` After: ``` {'actual_total': 0.079, 'request_tier_total': 0.079} ``` `qwen-flash` declares `[0, 256000]` at $0.05/M input and `[256000, 1000000]` at $0.25/M input. A 300,000-token request sits in the second tier, so Model Studio charges all 300,000 input tokens at $0.25/M and the 2,000 completion tokens at that tier's $2/M. The old result charged the first 256,000 input tokens at the cheap rate and put the completion tokens in tier 1 entirely, which is 69% under. Reverting only `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` and keeping the new tests gives the failures below, so the regression coverage is genuinely pinned to this fix: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py -q --tb=line E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0246, 0.079, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:96: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.012800249999999999, (256001 * 2.5e-07), rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:127: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.2488, 0.3, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:281: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0015999999999999999, 0.002, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:259: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0474, 0.07379999999999999, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:172: assert False FAILED ...::test_dashscope_cached_tokens_count_toward_tier_selection FAILED ...::test_dashscope_input_above_first_tier_bills_whole_request_at_that_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_output_tokens_do_not_select_their_own_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tier_boundary_is_inclusive_of_range_end FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_exceeding_highest_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_string_costs_exceeding_highest_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_with_caching 7 failed, 3 passed in 1.39s ``` With the fix restored: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/ tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/ -q 193 passed in 23.14s $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_cost_calculator.py -q 80 passed in 4.55s ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` now resolves the tier once per request instead of running four independent graduated calculations. `_calculate_prompt_cost` and `_calculate_completion_cost` take the selected tier rather than the whole `tiered_pricing` list, and read their rates with `tier_rate`, which keeps the existing fallbacks (cached input falls back to the tier's input rate, reasoning falls back to the tier's output rate) and the existing string-cost coercion for YAML-parsed rates. The flat-pricing path for models with no `tiered_pricing` is untouched, as is `calculate_tiered_cost` itself for any caller that wants graduated behaviour. A follow-up commit converts the three annotations the fix touches to PEP 604 / PEP 585 form (`dict | None`, `list[dict] | None`), which keeps the strict-rule budget from moving; the file drops from 8 strict violations to 2. The existing tests in `test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py` asserted the graduated numbers, so they are updated to the request-size expectations. Five cases were added or reworked to cover what the issue asked for: an above-first-tier request billed wholly at that tier, the tier boundary being inclusive of `range_end` (256,000 stays in tier 1, 256,001 moves up), output tokens not selecting their own tier, cached tokens counting toward tier selection, and input beyond the highest declared range falling back to the last tier. The two string-valued-rate regressions from the earlier YAML coercion fix are kept, with expectations recomputed under the new model. ## QA runbook Point a deployment at a DashScope Qwen model with `tiered_pricing` in the cost map (`qwen-flash` or `qwen3-coder-plus`), send one request whose input is comfortably above the first tier's `range_end` and one below it, then compare `spend` on the two `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` rows against the Model Studio console for the same requests. The large request should now be priced entirely at the higher tier rather than partly at the cheap one, and it should match the budget reservation estimate for that request rather than falling short of it. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): normalize tuple-form JSON Schema items before the Vertex transform
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Tuple-form `items` crashes every `vertex_ai/*` request carrying that tool - Error surfaces as `APIConnectionError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` - OpenAI-compatible clients and several MCP servers emit that shape How it solves it: - Rewrite `"items": [A, B]` as `"items": {"anyOf": [A, B]}` once, before the walkers - Runs after `unpack_defs`, so `$ref`-expanded schemas are covered too - `items: []` drops out and `process_items` synthesizes `{"type": "object"}` ## User Flow Before: a developer whose tool schema declares a fixed-shape array gets a connection error from the gateway on every call, while the same tool works against other providers 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash"` and a tool whose parameters contain `"a": {"type": "array", "items": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "string"}]}` 2. The gateway answers with `litellm.APIConnectionError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`, and no request ever reaches the model 3. They retry the identical body against an OpenAI-compatible provider and get a normal completion, so the tool schema itself is fine 4. Their only way forward is a pre-call shim that rewrites the tool schema before the gateway sees it After: the same request is accepted and the tool reaches the model 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same tuple-form tool 2. The gateway forwards the tool to Vertex with that field typed as an array whose entries may be an integer or a string 3. They get a normal completion back, with a tool call if the model chooses to make one 4. The shim can come out of their stack The array position that carried a fixed order is now an unordered union, which is the closest shape Vertex can express ## Relevant issues Fixes #36848 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I do not have Vertex credentials, so there is no live provider run here. What I can show is that the failure is raised while building the request, before anything is sent, so it reproduces without a project or a key. Both runs below use the exact tool schema from the issue. Before, at `423b791e` (the parent of this branch): ``` $ python -c " from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.common_utils import _build_vertex_schema print(_build_vertex_schema({'type':'object','properties':{'a':{'type':'array','items':[{'type':'integer'},{'type':'string'}]}}}))" AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' ``` After, at `f99823bf`: ``` $ python -c " from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.common_utils import _build_vertex_schema print(_build_vertex_schema({'type':'object','properties':{'a':{'type':'array','items':[{'type':'integer'},{'type':'string'}]}}}))" {'type': 'object', 'properties': {'a': {'type': 'array', 'items': {'anyOf': [{'type': 'integer'}, {'type': 'string'}]}}}} ``` A maintainer with Vertex access can confirm the end to end path with the curl in the issue body, which is the same tool schema against a live `vertex_ai/*` deployment. Happy to add that run here if someone can share a sandbox project. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Positional constraints are lost; Vertex cannot express tuple arrays - `additionalItems` is dropped, same as every other unsupported keyword - Boolean sub-schemas (`items: [false]`) still crash, unchanged from today - `prefixItems`, the 2020-12 spelling, is untouched and still ignored - `_build_json_schema` still passes tuple `items` through unchanged ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: Admin UI session cookie is a non-HttpOnly JWT carrying the caller's proxy key
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? The Admin UI login sets a `token` cookie holding a JWT whose `key` claim is the caller's real proxy key, and the cookie is not marked `HttpOnly`. For a proxy admin signing in with `UI_USERNAME` / `UI_PASSWORD` or through SSO, that means a full-privilege `sk-...` key sits in `document.cookie`, readable by any script running on `/ui`, for the whole 8h cookie lifetime. Two things make it worse than a normal session cookie: The key keeps working outside the browser. Anything that can read the cookie can paste the decoded key into `curl` and mint new keys, read spend, or call models, with no session involved. Logout does not revoke it. The dashboard clears cookies client-side, so a key that was copied before logout stays valid until its own expiry. I would expect the browser to hold an opaque session identifier that the proxy resolves server-side, in an `HttpOnly` cookie, with a logout route that drops the session on the server. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run the proxy with any config that sets a master key, for example ```yaml model_list: [] general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` 2. Log in the way the Admin UI does, and look at the cookie it sets ``` $ curl -si -X POST http://localhost:4000/login -d 'username=admin&password=sk-1234' | grep -i '^set-cookie' set-cookie: token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoiZGVmYXVsdF91c2VyX2lkIiwia2V5Ijoic2steHh4eHh4...<truncated>; Path=/; SameSite=lax ``` No `HttpOnly` flag, so `document.cookie` in the devtools console on http://localhost:4000/ui/ returns the same string. 3. Decode the middle segment ``` $ echo "$TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d | python -m json.tool { "user_id": "default_user_id", "key": "sk-<the admin's real proxy key>", "user_role": "proxy_admin", "login_method": "username_password", "auth_header_name": "Authorization", "server_root_path": "", "exp": 1786805817 } ``` 4. Use that key from outside the browser ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_FROM_COOKIE" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"minted-outside-the-browser"}' { "key": "sk-...", "key_alias": "minted-outside-the-browser", "expires": null } ``` 5. Log out in the UI, then repeat step 4 with the same key; it still mints keys ### Relevant log output ```shell POST /login HTTP/1.1" 303 See Other POST /key/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 OK # using the key decoded out of the login cookie ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? UI Dashboard ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.98.0 (reproduced on `litellm_internal_staging` at 423b791ee0) ### Possible direction I have a working change locally that swaps the JWT for an opaque `sso_<hex>` handle stored in the cache the `login_code` exchange already uses, delivered in an `HttpOnly` `SameSite=Lax` cookie, plus `/sso/session/me` for identity and `/sso/session/logout` for server-side revocation, with a credential-free `litellm_ui_session=1` marker so the dashboard can still tell a session exists. Happy to open a PR if that direction sounds right to you.

signal.title: fix(proxy/ui): detect stale restructured dirs as needing rebuild
signal.text: ## Summary - `_is_ui_pre_restructured` short-circuited to `True` as soon as it found any `<route>/index.html` subdirectory, ignoring whether a fresh `<route>.html` source file was sitting next to it. - That mixed state happens routinely in development: a UI rebuild lands new chunk hashes via `chore: update Next.js build artifacts`, but leftover `<route>/index.html` files from a previous proxy run remain on disk. The detection returns `True`, restructure is skipped, and the proxy serves the stale `<route>/index.html` — which references `/_next/static/chunks/<hash>.js` files that no longer exist. Browser sees `ChunkLoadError` / 404 on UI routes. - Fix walks the tree: only return `True` when at least one restructured subdirectory exists **and** no unrestructured `*.html` source files remain (outside `_next/` and `litellm-asset-prefix/`). Mixed state now correctly triggers a re-restructure, and `os.replace` atomically refreshes the stale `index.html` files. ## Test plan - [x] `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py -v -k "is_ui_pre_restructured or restructure_ui_html or extensionless_route"` — 6 passed (4 new + 2 existing) - [x] `uv run black litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py` - [ ] Local repro: stale `out/<route>/index.html` left over from a prior proxy run + fresh `out/<route>.html` → restart proxy → restructure runs, stale chunk references replaced. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Low risk: this only changes UI static-file restructure detection and adds focused tests, but could affect when the proxy decides to skip or rerun restructuring on startup. > > **Overview** > Fixes `_is_ui_pre_restructured` so it no longer returns `True` just because *some* `<route>/index.html` directories exist; it now walks the UI tree and only treats it as ready when **at least one restructured route exists** and **no unrestructured `*.html` source files remain** (excluding `_next` and `litellm-asset-prefix`). This prevents serving stale restructured HTML after a UI rebuild that leaves mixed `<route>.html` + `<route>/index.html` on disk (which can cause missing-chunk 404s). > > Adds new tests covering marker-file readiness, clean restructured pattern detection, unrestructured trees, and the mixed-state regression case. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 2cc51774018009791761363469bcc8cd231d3774. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(responses): honor caller stream flag when provider forces SSE
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `chatgpt/*` ignores a caller's `stream: false` since v1.90.0 - `/v1/responses` hands back raw SSE instead of JSON - `/v1/chat/completions` fails with `Unknown items in responses API response: []` How it solves it: - Transport streaming and response shape are decided separately - Only the caller's own `stream` value picks the shape - Providers that force SSE are still read as streams ## User Flow Before: a developer calling a ChatGPT subscription model without streaming gets back something they cannot parse 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"stream": false` and a ChatGPT subscription model 2. A 200 comes back, but `content-type` is `text/event-stream` and the body is 12 SSE frames instead of one JSON object 3. Their client breaks on the string; n8n reports `Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'object' in data:` followed by the whole stream 4. They try the same model at POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with no streaming 5. That returns 500 with `Unknown items in responses API response: []`, so neither endpoint serves a plain response After: the same two requests come back in the shape the caller asked for 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"stream": false` 2. A 200 comes back with `content-type: application/json` and a single response object whose `status` is `completed` 3. Their client parses it normally, with no SSE frames in the body 4. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions 5. That returns 200 with an assistant message and a `finish_reason` of `stop` 6. Sending either endpoint with `"stream": true` still streams exactly as before ## Relevant issues Fixes #34094 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a live proxy hitting the real ChatGPT subscription backend, with `chatgpt/gpt-5.4` as the only entry in `model_list` and no api_key (the provider reads the stored subscription token) Response bodies are reported as content type, SSE frame count and body byte count rather than pasted in full, because they carry account-scoped identifiers. Body bytes exclude headers The before run is the current base commit with nothing applied; the after run is this branch. Both were run back to back against the same account and prompt Commands, run once per proxy: ```bash for s in false true; do curl -sS -D - -o body.txt http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\": \"m-gpt54\", \"input\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"say hi in 3 words\"}], \"stream\": $s}" \ | grep -iE "^(HTTP/|content-type)" grep -c '^data: ' body.txt wc -c < body.txt done for s in false true; do curl -sS -D - -o body.txt http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\": \"m-gpt54\", \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"say hi in 3 words\"}], \"stream\": $s}" \ | grep -iE "^(HTTP/|content-type)" grep -c '^data: ' body.txt wc -c < body.txt done ``` ### Before, at `b0fac57fe4` | request | status | content-type | SSE frames | body bytes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `/v1/responses` `stream: false` | 200 | text/event-stream | 12 | 29661 | | `/v1/chat/completions` non-streaming | 500 | application/json | 0 | 240 | | `/v1/responses` `stream: true` | 200 | text/event-stream | 12 | 29658 | The non-streaming Responses call is served as a full SSE stream, and the 500 body is the `Unknown items in responses API response: []` error ### After, at `f9a1e98780` | request | status | content-type | SSE frames | body bytes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `/v1/responses` `stream: false` | 200 | application/json | 0 | 9688 | | `/v1/chat/completions` non-streaming | 200 | application/json | 0 | 443 | | `/v1/responses` `stream: true` | 200 | text/event-stream | 12 | 29661 | | `/v1/chat/completions` `stream: true` | 200 | text/event-stream | 5 | 783 | The Responses body is a single response object with `"status": "completed"` and one output item, the chat body carries an assistant message with `"finish_reason": "stop"`, and both streaming calls still stream, ending in `data: [DONE]` for the chat one `/v1/messages` is not covered because this change only touches the Responses handlers; that endpoint does not reach them ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes The two Responses handlers in `litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py` decided whether to hand the caller a streaming iterator by reading `stream` off the provider payload: ```python stream = bool(stream or data.get("stream")) ... is_stream_request = bool(stream) ``` `data` there is what goes out to the provider, not what the caller sent. `ChatGPTResponsesAPIConfig.transform_responses_api_request` sets `request["stream"] = True` unconditionally because the Codex backend only serves SSE, so `data.get("stream")` is always true for this provider and a caller that sent `stream: false` was silently moved onto the streaming path. Other Responses providers are unaffected; chatgpt is the only one whose transform touches `stream` at all On `/v1/responses` that meant a raw SSE body was returned to a caller expecting one JSON object. On `/v1/chat/completions` the Responses bridge fell into `_collect_response_from_stream`, which keeps only the `response` from the `response.completed` event; when the Codex backend emits that event with an empty `output` the request failed with `Unknown items in responses API response: []`. The recovery path added for that case in `_recover_output_items_from_raw_sse` re-parses the raw SSE from `logging_obj.model_call_details["original_response"]`, and the only place that populates it for this provider is `transform_response_api_response`, which lives on the non-streaming path and was no longer being reached That merge line came from #30189, which set out to stop provider transforms that force `stream: true` from being sent through the non-streaming branch, ChatGPT Codex models included. The transport half of that is right and this PR keeps it. The problem is that a single `stream` variable was carrying two decisions at once: what to pass to httpx, and whether to return an iterator or an aggregated body. Merging the provider payload into it fixed the transport half and silently changed the response shape along with it. A later refactor lifted the merged value into `is_stream_request`, which renamed the variable without splitting the two decisions This keeps transport streaming exactly as it was, so a provider that only serves SSE is still read as a stream, and narrows the response-shape decision to the caller's own `stream` value, captured before the transform runs. When the provider forces SSE for a non-streaming caller the body is read and aggregated through the existing path. The bridge half of #30189, which preserves a top-level `stream=True` into the Responses request, is untouched Tests cover both handlers: a caller sending `stream: false` (and one omitting it) against a provider that forces streaming gets an aggregated `ResponsesAPIResponse`, and a caller that asks for streaming still gets an iterator. The two existing `..._streams_when_provider_transform_adds_stream` tests from #30189 are untouched apart from one fixture line, so the transport-level behaviour they lock in stays covered, and the streaming rows in the after table confirm it end to end ## Caveats (if any) - Proof uses `chatgpt/gpt-5.4`; codex-suffixed models were refused by this account - Rebased onto `b0fac57fe4`; earlier proof commits in this PR's history are stale ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(mcp): return configured alias in serverInfo.name for /mcp/{alias} endpoints
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - MCP Gateway endpoints at `/mcp/{alias}` returned the hardcoded `serverInfo.name = "litellm-mcp-server"` instead of the specific server alias. How it solves it: - Dynamically populates `serverInfo.name` with the scoped server alias/name on per-alias endpoints, falling back cleanly to the default name for aggregate endpoints or empty aliases. ## Relevant issues Fixes #29800 ## Description - **What was broken**: Connecting to per-alias MCP gateway endpoints (`/mcp/{alias}`) returned a hardcoded `serverInfo.name = "litellm-mcp-server"` in the `InitializeResult`, causing all gateway-backed servers to appear with identical names in MCP clients (#29800). - **Root cause**: `_gateway_create_initialization_options` and `_gateway_initialize_instructions_request_scope` in `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py` needed strict non-empty validation and path alias fallback so the scoped endpoint's alias is reliably propagated into `InitializeResult.serverInfo.name`. - **What changed**: - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py`: Validated `scoped_server_name` is non-empty before updating initialization options, and added fallback to path alias when server name properties are unset. - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_mcp_server.py`: Added parameterized regression tests for multiple distinct aliases (`grafana`, `playwright`, `home_assistant`) and aggregate/whitespace fallback tests. - **How it was tested**: - `TestGatewayCreateInitializationOptions::test_streamable_http_handler_scopes_server_name_for_distinct_aliases` - `TestGatewayCreateInitializationOptions::test_streamable_http_handler_fallback_on_aggregate_endpoint` - `TestGatewayCreateInitializationOptions::test_scoped_request_empty_or_whitespace_alias_falls_back_to_default` - `TestGatewayCreateInitializationOptions::test_scoped_request_uses_configured_server_alias` - `TestGatewayCreateInitializationOptions::test_sse_handler_scopes_server_name_from_single_server_path` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix

signal.title: [Bug]: interactions.create() silently drops response_format when routed via litellm_proxy (Gemini)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When `USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true` (or `litellm.use_litellm_proxy=True`) is set process-wide, `litellm.interactions.create()` for a Gemini model silently loses its `response_format` (JSON schema / mime type constraint) with no error or warning, and the model falls back to free-text output. Root cause, traced through the source: 1. `get_llm_provider()` (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/get_llm_provider_logic.py`) checks `LiteLLMProxyChatConfig._should_use_litellm_proxy_by_default()` **first, unconditionally**, before looking at any explicitly-passed `custom_llm_provider`. With `USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true` set, this forces `custom_llm_provider="litellm_proxy"` for *every* litellm call in the process, including `interactions.create()`. 2. `get_provider_interactions_api_config()` (`litellm/interactions/utils.py`) only recognizes `provider == "gemini"`. For `"litellm_proxy"` it returns `None`. 3. Back in `litellm/interactions/main.py`, when `interactions_api_config is None`, the call **silently bridges to `litellm.responses()`** via `LiteLLMResponsesInteractionsHandler` instead of raising or warning. 4. That bridge's request transform, `transform_interactions_request_to_responses_request()` (`litellm/interactions/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py`), maps `system_instruction`, `input`, `tools`, and parts of `generation_config` — but has **no handling for `response_format` at all**. It's dropped entirely, silently. Net effect: a caller who explicitly requested strict JSON-schema output via the Interactions API gets back ordinary free-text (Gemini then wraps its answer in a markdown code fence, as it typically does without an explicit JSON constraint), with no exception and no log line indicating the constraint was dropped. This is especially easy to hit by accident: `USE_LITELLM_PROXY` is a reasonable thing to set globally so that `litellm.responses()`/`litellm.completion()` route through a self-hosted LiteLLM Proxy, but doing so silently breaks the Interactions API for the same process. Confirmed present in every version I checked, `1.82.0` through the current latest `1.96.2` (checked wheel/sdist contents directly) — `litellm/llms/litellm_proxy/interactions/` does not exist in any of them, unlike `litellm/llms/litellm_proxy/{chat,responses,image_generation,image_edit,skills}/` which do. ### Steps to Reproduce ```python import os os.environ["USE_LITELLM_PROXY"] = "true" import litellm response = litellm.interactions.create( model="gemini-3.5-flash", system_instruction="Respond only with JSON matching the schema.", input=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Say hello and give a score of 1."}]}], response_format={ "type": "text", "mime_type": "application/json", "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": {"greeting": {"type": "string"}, "score": {"type": "number"}}, "required": ["greeting", "score"], }, }, generation_config={"max_output_tokens": 512}, api_base="http://localhost:4000", # a real LiteLLM Proxy instance api_key="sk-...", # a valid virtual key for that proxy ) ``` Expected: request reaches the proxy's `/interactions`-equivalent handling (or, if unsupported, the fallback should still honor `response_format`), returning clean JSON. Actual: request is silently rerouted to `/responses` with `response_format` dropped; the returned text is unconstrained free text (often markdown-fenced JSON, not raw JSON), and `json.loads()` on it fails intermittently depending on how the model chooses to format its answer. ### Relevant log output ```shell # No warning/error is logged - the drop is completely silent. Confirmed via the local proxy's # access log: with USE_LITELLM_PROXY=true, an interactions.create() call for a Gemini model never # produces a "/interactions" (or equivalent) hit on the proxy - only "/responses" hits appear, # confirming the silent bridge. ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy / Interactions API ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.0 (also reproduced on v1.96.2; confirmed present via source inspection back through v1.82.0) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(snowflake): transform string tool_choice to object format
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #23284 Snowflake's Cortex LLM API (like Anthropic's Messages API) requires `tool_choice` as an object with a `"type"` field, not as a bare string. Passing `tool_choice="auto"` (or `"required"`/`"none"`) results in Snowflake error 390142 "invalid payload". ### Root cause The `_transform_tool_choice` method in `SnowflakeConfig` was passing string `tool_choice` values through unchanged. However, Snowflake's API follows the Anthropic convention where `tool_choice` must be an object like `{"type": "auto"}`. LiteLLM's own Anthropic handler (`AnthropicConfig._map_tool_choice`) already correctly transforms strings to objects -- the Snowflake handler was missing the same transformation. ### Fix Transform OpenAI string `tool_choice` values to Snowflake's object format: | OpenAI (string) | Snowflake (object) | |---|---| | `"auto"` | `{"type": "auto"}` | | `"required"` | `{"type": "any"}` | | `"none"` | `{"type": "none"}` | The `"required"` -> `"any"` mapping follows the same convention used by Anthropic/Snowflake (the model must use at least one tool). The existing dict-to-dict transformation for specific function tool choices remains unchanged. ### Tests updated Updated `test_transform_request_with_string_tool_choice` to verify the new object format output instead of passthrough. ## Test plan - [ ] Verify `tool_choice="auto"` is transformed to `{"type": "auto"}` - [ ] Verify `tool_choice="required"` is transformed to `{"type": "any"}` - [ ] Verify `tool_choice="none"` is transformed to `{"type": "none"}` - [ ] Verify dict tool_choice (specific function) still works - [ ] Verify requests without tool_choice are unaffected

signal.title: [Bug]: Blocking a model's primary deployment(s) skips the configured `fallbacks` chain entirely, instead of routing to the healthy fallback
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? I have a model alias (`DeepSeek-Flash`) whose primary target is one model group (`DeepSeek-V-Flash-00`), with a `fallbacks` entry configured to escalate to a second model group (`DeepSeek-V-Flash-10`) if the primary fails. `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10` has two deployments: one permanently broken (region/opt-in restricted at the provider), one fully healthy. I blocked the broken deployments through the model-blocking feature: all deployment(s) under `DeepSeek-V-Flash-00` (the alias's primary target), and the one broken deployment under `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10` (leaving its healthy sibling deployment unblocked and unaffected). After doing this, every request for `model=DeepSeek-Flash` fails immediately with a "Model is blocked" permission error, even though the healthy deployment under `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10` — the exact fallback I configured for this situation — is never attempted. **What I expected:** blocking a deployment should only remove that specific deployment (or, if all of a group's deployments are blocked, that specific group) from the routing pool. If a configured fallback chain still has a reachable, unblocked deployment, the request should succeed via that fallback, the same way it would if the primary deployment had failed with a provider-side error instead of being blocked. Instead, blocking the primary target of an alias appears to reject the request before the fallback chain is ever consulted, regardless of whether the fallback chain itself is healthy. ### User Flow ### Before a (hypothetical) fix Calling the gateway's chat completions endpoint for this model fails outright, even though a healthy backend for it is configured and reachable. 1. The operator opens the LiteLLM Admin UI's model management page (`https://<your-proxy-host>/ui/models` — **fill in the exact page URL you used**) and blocks the deployment(s) backing `DeepSeek-V-Flash-00`, plus the one known-broken deployment backing `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10`. The UI/API confirms each block action succeeded. 2. The client application sends: ``` POST https://<your-proxy-host>/v1/chat/completions Authorization: Bearer <virtual-key, redacted> Content-Type: application/json { "model": "DeepSeek-Flash", "messages": [ ... ] } ``` 3. The client receives an HTTP error response with body: ``` litellm.exceptions.PermissionDeniedError: litellm.PermissionDeniedError: Model is blocked ``` (**fill in the exact HTTP status code you observed, e.g. 403**) 4. The client never receives a completion, even though the healthy deployment under `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10` — the model group this alias's `fallbacks` entry points to — was never contacted. ### After a (hypothetical) fix Calling the same endpoint the same way succeeds, because the request is routed to the healthy fallback instead of being rejected outright. 1. The operator opens the LiteLLM Admin UI's model management page (`https://<your-proxy-host>/ui/models`) and blocks the deployment(s) backing `DeepSeek-V-Flash-00`, plus the one known-broken deployment backing `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10`. The UI/API confirms each block action succeeded. 2. The client application sends: ``` POST https://<your-proxy-host>/v1/chat/completions Authorization: Bearer <virtual-key, redacted> Content-Type: application/json { "model": "DeepSeek-Flash", "messages": [ ... ] } ``` 3. The client receives a normal `200 OK` chat completion response, generated by the healthy deployment under `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10`. 4. The client's experience is identical to what it would be if `DeepSeek-V-Flash-00` had failed with an ordinary provider error (e.g. a timeout) instead of being blocked — the fallback is transparent either way. *Not a security/authorization issue — this is purely an availability/reliability regression: a working, authorized path becomes unreachable.* --- ### Proof the bug occurs ### Config used ```yaml model_list: - model_name: DeepSeek-V-Flash-00 - model_name: DeepSeek-V-Flash-10 - model_name: DeepSeek-V-Flash-10 router_settings: model_group_alias: DeepSeek-Flash: DeepSeek-V-Flash-00 litellm_settings: fallbacks: - DeepSeek-Flash: [DeepSeek-V-Flash-00, DeepSeek-V-Flash-10] ``` ### Environment - litellm proxy version: `1.92.2` ### Steps + actual output **1. Block the primary group's deployment (and the broken fallback deployment).** **2. Call the alias and observe the failure:** ```bash curl -X POST https://<your-proxy-host>/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <virtual-key, redacted>" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "DeepSeek-Flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}' ``` Observed server-side log / traceback (captured with `--detailed_debug`): ``` 17:39:14 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: common_request_processing.py:744 - litellm.proxy.proxy_server._handle_llm_api_exception(): Exception occured - litellm.PermissionDeniedError: Model is blocked Traceback (most recent call last): File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py", line 8460, in chat_completion result = await base_llm_response_processor.base_process_llm_request( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ...<16 lines>... ) ^ File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py", line 1414, in base_process_llm_request llm_call = await route_request( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ...<5 lines>... ) ^ File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/route_llm_request.py", line 423, in route_request _raise_if_model_fully_blocked(llm_router=llm_router, model_name=data.get("model"), team_id=team_id) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/route_llm_request.py", line 57, in _raise_if_model_fully_blocked raise litellm.PermissionDeniedError( ...<7 lines>... ) litellm.exceptions.PermissionDeniedError: litellm.PermissionDeniedError: Model is blocked ``` **3. Unblock `DeepSeek-V-Flash-00` (or point the alias at `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10` instead) and repeat step 2** — confirms `DeepSeek-V-Flash-10`'s healthy deployment does serve the request successfully once it's actually reached, which shows the fallback target itself is fine; the only problem is that it's never attempted while the alias's primary target is fully blocked.** ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=vector-stores and click Add Vector Store: the provider dropdown offers Bedrock, S3 Vectors, pgvector, Vertex AI, OpenAI, Azure, and Milvus, but no Valkey 2. signal.title: fix(responses-api): report real usage on guardrail-blocked replies
signal.text: Fixes #36880 ## Problem When a guardrail blocks a request/response through the /v1/responses endpoint, the returned violation message always reports zero usage (`ResponseAPIUsage(input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0, total_tokens=0)`), even for a post-call block where the upstream LLM call already happened and consumed real tokens. Anything reading usage off that response (billing, monitoring, budget checks) sees zero cost for a call that actually cost money. ## Root cause The `except ModifyResponseException as e:` handler in litellm/proxy/response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py hardcodes zero usage instead of reading `e.original_response`, which already carries the real usage when the block happened post-call. The chat completions endpoint already solves this correctly via `_blocked_response_usage()` in proxy_server.py — the Responses API endpoint just never got the equivalent handling. ## Fix Added `_blocked_responses_api_usage()`, mirroring `_blocked_response_usage`'s logic for the Responses API's usage shape: - `original_response is None` (pre-call block, no upstream call happened) → zero usage - `original_response.usage` already Responses-API-shaped (native /v1/responses upstream call) → passed through directly - `original_response.usage` Chat-Completions-shaped (a bridged call under the hood) → field-mapped (prompt_tokens→input_tokens, completion_tokens→output_tokens) ## Testing Added 3 unit tests covering all three branches (None, Responses-shaped, Chat-shaped) directly against the new helper function. I wasn't able to run these through the full pytest suite locally — the proxy test conftest requires a generated `prisma` client, which needs a DB step outside this change's scope — so I verified the exact same assertions via a standalone script against the real function instead; all three pass. Happy to run the full suite if a maintainer can point me to the quickest prisma-generate path, or if CI covers it directly.

signal.title: feat(openrouter): add image edit support for OpenRouter models
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/22305 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Type New Feature ## Changes ### Problem OpenRouter models (e.g., `google/gemini-2.5-flash-image`) support image editing through their chat completions endpoint, but LiteLLM has no image edit configuration for the OpenRouter provider. Calling `litellm.image_edit()` with an OpenRouter model raises `ValueError("image edit is not supported for openrouter")` because `ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_image_edit_config()` returns `None` for OpenRouter. ### Solution Added `OpenRouterImageEditConfig` that implements `BaseImageEditConfig` to route image edit requests through OpenRouter's chat completions endpoint. Unlike providers with dedicated `/images/edits` endpoints, OpenRouter handles image editing via `/api/v1/chat/completions` with the source image sent as a base64 data URL in the message content and `modalities: ["image", "text"]` to signal image output. - Converts source images (bytes, BytesIO, BufferedReader) to base64 data URLs in the messages array - Maps OpenAI parameters: `size` to `image_config.aspect_ratio`, `quality` to `image_config.image_size` - Parses edited images from `choices[].message.images[]` in the response - Tracks usage including input image tokens from `prompt_tokens_details` - Extracts cost and cost details from OpenRouter's usage response - Uses JSON requests (`use_multipart_form_data() = False`), matching the Gemini image edit pattern - Registered in `ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_image_edit_config()` following the existing factory pattern ### Files changed - **`litellm/llms/openrouter/image_edit/__init__.py`** - New module with factory function `get_openrouter_image_edit_config()` - **`litellm/llms/openrouter/image_edit/transformation.py`** - `OpenRouterImageEditConfig` class with request/response transformation, parameter mapping, usage/cost extraction - **`litellm/utils.py`** - Added OpenRouter case to `ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_image_edit_config()` - **`tests/test_litellm/llms/openrouter/image_edit/__init__.py`** - Test module init - **`tests/test_litellm/llms/openrouter/image_edit/test_openrouter_image_edit_transformation.py`** - 33 unit tests ### Testing - 33 new unit tests covering: supported params, multipart mode, parameter mapping (size, quality, n, combined, unknown), size-to-aspect-ratio mapping, quality-to-image-size mapping, URL construction, environment validation, request transformation (basic, BytesIO, multiple images, optional params, base64 encoding, no prompt), response transformation (base64, URL, usage/cost, multiple images, JSON error), error class, and `_read_image_bytes` edge cases - All 33 new tests pass - All 48 existing OpenRouter tests continue to pass (81 total) - Live-tested against the OpenRouter API with `google/gemini-2.5-flash-image`, successfully editing an image and receiving a valid response with correct usage tracking @greptileai @shin-bot-litellm

signal.title: fix(version): switch _version.py to stdlib importlib.metadata, drop importlib-metadata dep
signal.text: ## What changed `litellm/_version.py` imported the third-party `importlib_metadata` backport package, but Python 3.10+ (the project's minimum) ships a fully-featured `importlib.metadata` in the standard library. When `importlib-metadata` is not installed (e.g. in a fresh virtualenv or a minimal Docker image), importing the package raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'importlib_metadata'` before any LiteLLM code runs, breaking every command. This PR replaces the backport import with `from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version` and removes the now-unused `importlib-metadata` entry from `pyproject.toml` dependencies. ## Test plan Run `python -c "from litellm._version import version; print(version)"` in a virtualenv that does not have `importlib-metadata` installed; it should print the version string (or "unknown") instead of crashing. Fixes #36989

signal.title: fix: forward metadata into speech() litellm_params_dict so Gemini TTS spend is tracked
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Gemini TTS (and any TTS provider using the speech-to-completion bridge) is never spend-tracked on the proxy - Virtual key spend stays 0 and no spend-log row is written for these calls How it solves it: - `speech()` takes `metadata` as an explicit named argument, so it never ends up in `**kwargs` - `get_litellm_params(**kwargs)` therefore produced a dict with `metadata: None`, which the bridge spread into the inner `completion()` call, overwriting the logging object's key/user/team context - Pass `metadata=metadata` explicitly to `get_litellm_params` so the inner call carries the real metadata ## User Flow Before: a developer using `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` through the proxy sees no spend logged and key budgets never trip 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts", "input": "hello", "voice": "Kore"}` using a virtual key and receive 200 with `audio/wav` bytes 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "openai/tts-1", "input": "hello", "voice": "alloy"}` using the same key and receive 200 with `audio/mpeg` bytes 3. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs lists only the OpenAI request; the Gemini request is absent 4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows `"spend": 0.00027` (only the OpenAI call), so a budget on the key never trips regardless of Gemini TTS volume After: both calls are logged and billed to the key 1. They send the same POST for `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` and receive 200 with audio 2. They send the same POST for `openai/tts-1` and receive 200 with audio 3. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs lists both requests, the Gemini one with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero spend 4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows the combined spend from both calls, and a max budget on the key applies to Gemini TTS too ## Relevant issues Fixes #37015 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Run the proxy with a Gemini API key and a virtual key, then: ```bash # Before fix: Gemini call logs metadata as None, no spend row appears curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/audio/speech \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <virtual-key>" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts","input":"spend tracking check","voice":"Kore"}' \ --output /tmp/out.wav # After fix: spend row appears with call_type aspeech and non-zero spend curl -s http://localhost:4000/spend/logs -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq '.[] | select(.model | test("gemini"))' ``` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(router): register arbitrary custom pricing thresholds
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem: * Router dropped undeclared `*_above_<N>_tokens` pricing fields. * Threshold discovery depended on input-cost fields, so standalone output and cache thresholds were accepted but silently ignored. Solution: * Preserve declared and regex-matched custom pricing fields during initial and dynamic Router registration. * Select the highest applicable threshold independently for input, output, cache creation, cache creation above 1 hour, and cache read pricing. * Preserve base-rate and service-tier fallback behavior. ## Relevant issues Fixes #34378 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist * [x] I have added meaningful tests * [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks — all 25 GitHub Actions workflows pass on the current head * [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem * [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Verified PR head: ```text b64d0a6eee85da7947ab4901f7ba9b0821fd4edd ``` Standalone output threshold: ```text registered_output_tier=1.8e-05 actual_completion_cost=0.018000000000000002 expected_completion_cost=0.018000000000000002 ``` Standalone cache-read threshold: ```text registered_cache_tier=4e-06 actual_cache_read_rate=4e-06 expected_cache_read_rate=4e-06 ``` An inactive input threshold no longer suppresses an independently active output threshold. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes * Preserve arbitrary `*_above_<N>_tokens` fields accepted by `LiteLLM_Params`. * Apply the registration helper during initial and dynamic deployment registration. * Keep deployment pricing isolated from shared backend entries. * Select thresholds independently for all supported cost categories. * Parse nested keys such as `cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_1hr_above_32k_tokens`. * Add output-only, cache-only, and independent-threshold regression coverage. ## Tests ```text Cost calculation: 105 passed Router isolation: 20 passed, 2 deselected Custom pricing: 16 passed Ruff format/lint: passed GitHub Actions workflows: 25 passed ``` All GitHub Actions workflows, including OSV Scan, pass on the current head. ### Final Attestation * [x] Tests cover standalone output/cache configurations and independent thresholds * [x] The fix exercises real Router registration and cost-calculation paths * [x] No dependency or lockfile changes are included

signal.title: [Bug]: Anthropic /v1/messages: role:"system" messages inside messages[] are silently dropped
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a client sends an Anthropic `/v1/messages` request whose `messages[]` array contains an entry with `role: "system"`, that entry never reaches the backend model. The top-level `system` field is delivered correctly; the in-array one is discarded with no warning and no error. **What I expected:** the in-array system content reaches the model (translated into an OpenAI system message), or failing that, an explicit error. Silent omission is the harmful case, because the request succeeds with HTTP 200 and the response looks completely normal. **Why this shape matters.** Anthropic supports mid-conversation system messages, and Claude Code uses that channel to deliver its skill listing — the catalogue of available Agent Skills that a model needs in order to decide whether to invoke one. Pointing Claude Code at a LiteLLM proxy backed by an OpenAI-compatible model therefore strips the catalogue, and the model behaves as though no skills exist. We lost a 192-cell benchmark run to this. Every cell recorded zero skill invocation, which read as a model-capability finding until we captured request payloads on both sides of the proxy and saw the message count drop from 2 to 1. Anyone benchmarking agent-skill discovery across models through this bridge will silently measure the bridge instead of the model. **Related, but not duplicates:** - #23841 (open) reports five bugs in this same area — `input_text` content blocks being dropped, plus several env-var routing failures. It does not cover `role: "system"` entries inside `messages[]`. - #17904 ("Cannot use claude-code + LiteLLM with openai models") describes symptoms that may share this root cause, but does not identify it. **Workaround** for anyone hitting this now: a small shim in front of the proxy that hoists `role: "system"` messages into the top-level `system` field before the request reaches LiteLLM. Ours is ~150 lines and restored skill invocation from 0/192 cells to the expected rates. ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix** — the model never learns which skills exist, so it never invokes one, and nothing tells me why. 1. I install an Agent Skill into my project so Claude Code can use it, then point Claude Code at my gateway with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4002` and pick an OpenAI-compatible model. 2. I ask it to do the task the skill exists for: "Write the release notes for version 0.2.0." 3. Claude Code sends `POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages`. Its request carries two messages: one with role `"system"` listing the skills available to me, and one with role `"user"` holding my request. 4. I get back HTTP 200 and a perfectly normal answer — the model writes release notes in its own default style. 5. The skill is never invoked. There is no warning, no error, and no hint in the response that anything was missing. From my seat it is indistinguishable from the model deciding the skill was not relevant. 6. I can isolate the invisible part with two requests. I send `POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages` with a codeword inside a role `"system"` message in `messages[]`, asking the model to repeat it — it replies `NONE`. I send the identical request with that codeword in the top-level `"system"` field instead — it replies `PINEAPPLE-7731`. Same gateway, same model, same question, HTTP 200 both times. **After a (hypothetical) fix** — the model receives the listing and invokes the skill. 1. Identical. 2. Identical. 3. Identical. 4. I get back HTTP 200, and the release notes follow the format the skill defines rather than the model's default style. 5. The skill is invoked, because the model actually received the listing describing it. 6. Both requests in step 6 now reply `PINEAPPLE-7731` — whether the codeword arrives inside a role `"system"` message in `messages[]` or in the top-level `"system"` field. ### Proof the bug occurs Live proxy I ran myself, real provider calls, no mocks. **Version** ``` LiteLLM: Current Version = 1.91.4 ``` **config.yaml** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: qwen3.6-35b litellm_params: model: openai/qwen3.6-35b api_base: https://freeinference.org/v1 api_key: os.environ/FREEINFERENCE_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-repro-local ``` **Env vars the proxy ran with** ``` FREEINFERENCE_API_KEY=<redacted> ``` **Started with** ```bash litellm --config config.yaml --port 4002 --host 127.0.0.1 ``` --- ### TEST A — codeword inside `messages[]` as `role: "system"` (the bug) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages \ -H "x-api-key: sk-repro-local" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "messages":[ {"role":"system","content":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731."}, {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `content`: ```json [ { "type": "text", "text": "NONE" } ] ``` The model never received the codeword. --- ### TEST B — identical codeword in the top-level `system` field (control) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/messages \ -H "x-api-key: sk-repro-local" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "system":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731.", "messages":[ {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `content`: ```json [ { "type": "text", "text": "PINEAPPLE-7731" } ] ``` Same gateway, same model, same question — the only difference is where the system content was placed. --- ### TEST C — `/v1/chat/completions` with the same `role: "system"` message (endpoint NOT affected) ```bash curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4002/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-local" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"qwen3.6-35b","max_tokens":200, "messages":[ {"role":"system","content":"You have been given the codeword PINEAPPLE-7731."}, {"role":"user","content":"What codeword were you given? If none, reply exactly: NONE"} ]}' ``` Response `choices[0].message.content`: ``` PINEAPPLE-7731 ``` So the same message shape is honoured on `/v1/chat/completions` and dropped on `/v1/messages`. `/v1/responses` was not tested. [root-cause-analysis.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31067236/root-cause-analysis.md) ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.91.4 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details @pranavh2004 / www.linkedin.com/in/pranav-hemanth

signal.title: [Bug]: Gemini TTS via /v1/audio/speech is never spend-tracked on the proxy (no spend log, key spend stays 0)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Gemini text-to-speech requests sent through the proxy's `POST /v1/audio/speech` return audio (200) but never show up in spend logs, never increment the virtual key's spend, and never count against budgets. OpenAI TTS through the same endpoint, same proxy, and same key is tracked fine, so this is specific to the Gemini path (and, by the same mechanism, any TTS provider that is served by translating the speech request into a chat completion under the hood) Expected: a `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` call priced at $0.30/M in and $2.50/M out shows a spend-log row with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero `spend`, and the key's `spend` moves, exactly like `openai/tts-1` does Root cause, for whoever picks this up: the speech entrypoint takes `metadata` as a named argument, then builds the litellm params it hands to the speech-to-completion bridge from the remaining kwargs, so `metadata` arrives there as `None`. The bridge spreads those params into the inner completion call while reusing the outer request's logging object, and the completion call overwrites that shared object's `metadata` with `None`. By the time the proxy's spend callback runs it finds no key, user, or team on the request and skips the write. Debug logs show it directly: the Gemini call logs `user_api_key None, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None`, the OpenAI call right after it logs the hashed key ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app generates speech with Gemini through the gateway sees every call at $0 and their key budget never moves 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts", "input": "spend tracking check", "voice": "Kore"}` using their virtual key and get 200 with `audio/wav` bytes back 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "openai/tts-1", "input": "spend tracking check", "voice": "alloy"}` using the same key and get 200 with `audio/mpeg` bytes back 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs (or GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs) and only the OpenAI request is listed, at $0.00027; the Gemini request is missing entirely 4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info with their key shows `"spend": 0.00027`, only the OpenAI call, so a max budget on that key never trips no matter how much Gemini audio they generate After a (hypothetical) fix: both TTS calls are logged and billed to the key 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech for `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` and get 200 with `audio/wav` bytes back 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech for `openai/tts-1` and get 200 with `audio/mpeg` bytes back 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs lists both requests, the Gemini one with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero spend computed from its input and audio output tokens 4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows the key's `spend` as the sum of both calls, and a key max budget now trips on Gemini audio too ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `DATABASE_URL` set in the environment, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts litellm_params: model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY - model_name: openai/tts-1 litellm_params: model: openai/tts-1 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Version or commit: `litellm_internal_staging` at 7a5b98e6a9 (v1.98.0), booted with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 41873 --detailed_debug` Commands and their full output (real Gemini and OpenAI calls): ``` $ KEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:41873/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"tts-spend-repro-3"}' | jq -r .key) $ curl -s -o speech.wav -D - -X POST http://localhost:41873/v1/audio/speech -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts","input":"spend tracking check","voice":"Kore"}' | grep -i -E "^HTTP|x-litellm-call-id|content-type" HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-call-id: ab71b16a-e469-437f-8859-562e1c8cb3ef content-type: audio/wav $ ls -la speech.wav | awk '{print $5" bytes"}' 154170 bytes $ curl -s -o speech.mp3 -D - -X POST http://localhost:41873/v1/audio/speech -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"openai/tts-1","input":"spend tracking check","voice":"alloy"}' | grep -i -E "^HTTP|x-litellm-call-id|content-type" HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-call-id: 6dcf0e92-9d26-43c6-9999-ede7aaaecaf1 content-type: audio/mpeg $ sleep 15; curl -s "http://localhost:41873/spend/logs" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq -c '.[] | {request_id, model, call_type, spend}' {"request_id":"6dcf0e92-9d26-43c6-9999-ede7aaaecaf1","model":"openai/tts-1","call_type":"aspeech","spend":0.00027} $ curl -s "http://localhost:41873/key/info" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | jq -c '.info | {key_alias, spend}' {"key_alias":"tts-spend-repro-3","spend":0.00027} $ curl -s "http://localhost:41873/v1/model/info" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq -c '.data[] | {model_name, input_cost_per_token: .model_info.input_cost_per_token, output_cost_per_token: .model_info.output_cost_per_token}' {"model_name":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts","input_cost_per_token":3E-7,"output_cost_per_token":0.0000025} {"model_name":"openai/tts-1","input_cost_per_token":null,"output_cost_per_token":null} ``` So the Gemini model is priced, the call succeeded, and the spend log has only the OpenAI row. The proxy's own debug log for the two calls, in order: ``` 01:56:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_track_cost_callback.py:249 - user_api_key None, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None 01:56:56 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_track_cost_callback.py:249 - user_api_key d628805a57f5b935deab509bb849d9e7761e27681d714c191eee3336135a1f10, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None ``` The same happens with the master key and with the newer `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` (checked at #36788's head 32917b07fc) ### What a fix PR should look like - `litellm/main.py`, `speech()`: pass the named `metadata` (and the other named args the bridge needs) into `get_litellm_params(...)` so the litellm params handed to `speech_to_completion_bridge_handler.speech` carry the request metadata instead of `None`; alternatively have `litellm/endpoints/speech/speech_to_completion_bridge/transformation.py` `transform_request` read `metadata` off the logging object's existing litellm params and forward it, so the inner completion never clobbers what the outer request set - Whichever way, make sure the outer `aspeech` success handler ends up with the request's `metadata` and a non-zero `response_cost` in its kwargs, since the proxy's cost callback reads both from there - Regression test in a new `tests/test_litellm/endpoints/speech/speech_to_completion_bridge/test_handler.py` (no mapped test exists yet for the bridge; `tests/test_litellm/test_main.py` also works for the `speech()` side): call `aspeech` for a `gemini/...-tts` model with `metadata={"user_api_key": "..."}` and a mocked completion, assert the success callback's `kwargs["litellm_params"]["metadata"]` still holds `user_api_key`; a second assertion that the same holds for the OpenAI path keeps the two in lockstep - Out of scope: pricing of TTS models (already correct in `/v1/model/info`), and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header, which is empty for every `/v1/audio/speech` call and can be its own follow-up - Proof for the fix PR: the exact commands above against a live proxy at the fix commit, showing a Gemini row in `/spend/logs` with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero `spend`, and `/key/info` `spend` equal to the sum of both calls ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? litellm_internal_staging @ 7a5b98e6a9 (v1.98.0) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(proxy): preserve repeated multipart form fields in get_form_data
signal.text: Fixes #35937 ## Problem `get_form_data()` in `litellm/proxy/common_utils/http_parsing_utils.py` (used by `/v1/audio/transcriptions`) called `dict(form)` on Starlette's `FormData` object before iterating it. `FormData` is a multidict that can hold multiple values under the same key, but `dict()` collapses repeated keys and silently keeps only the last one. The OpenAI SDK encodes `timestamp_granularities=["word", "segment"]` as two separate `timestamp_granularities[]=...` multipart fields, so the collapse meant only the second value ever reached litellm — matching the exact "last one wins" behavior reported. ## Fix Replaced `dict(form).items()` with `form.multi_items()` in `get_form_data()`, which preserves every repeated key/value pair from the original multidict. ## Testing Updated `tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_http_parsing_utils.py::test_get_form_data` to use a real `starlette.datastructures.FormData` (the previous mock was a plain dict literal, which can't represent a duplicate key and never actually exercised the bug) and assert both `"word"` and `"segment"` survive. Also fixed `TestGetRequestBody::test_form_post_routes_to_form_data`, whose mock likewise needed a real `FormData` object to support `.multi_items()`. Verified as a genuine regression guard: reverting the fix makes `test_get_form_data` fail with `AssertionError: assert ['segment'] == ['word', 'segment']`; restoring the fix passes it again. ``` ============================= 57 passed in 8.24s ============================== ```
