signal.title: fix(router): scan all deployments for weight/rpm/tpm in simple-shuffle
signal.text: ## Problem `simple_shuffle` only consults `healthy_deployments[0]` when deciding whether to do a weighted random pick. A config like: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini # ^ no weight/rpm/tpm declared - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini rpm: 1000 - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini rpm: 500 ``` silently falls back to **uniform random across all three** because the first entry has no `rpm`. Users perceive this as "deployment-level `rpm:` (or `tpm:` / `weight:`) is silently ignored under `simple-shuffle`" — the actual behavior is ordering-sensitive: if the first deployment happens to declare the weight field, everything works; if not, the rest are silently disregarded. This was reported as part of a broader audit of v3 rate limit semantics (sibling to #27913, #27914, #27915). It is the only one of those audit findings that's a pre-existing router bug rather than a v3-limiter or exception-mapper issue. ## Fix Extract `_pick_weight_field(healthy_deployments)` which scans **every** deployment for the precedence-ordered weight fields (`weight` > `rpm` > `tpm`) and returns the first one declared by any of them. Deployments that don't declare the chosen field continue to get weight `0` (preserves the existing semantics for in-list-but-unweighted entries). Also: defensive divide-by-zero guard when `total_weight == 0` (every deployment declared the field as 0 — pathological config). Falls through to uniform random instead of crashing. Docstring updated to be explicit that `rpm` and `tpm` here are **static relative weights**, not cap-enforced limits, and to point users at `router_settings.enable_pre_call_checks` (router-level RPM cap filter, gated on `messages is not None`) or the proxy's key-level v3 TPM/RPM limiter for actual cap enforcement under simple-shuffle. ## Scope notes This PR does **not** change the documented semantics of `rpm`/`tpm` under simple-shuffle (still relative weights). Adding actual cap enforcement to simple-shuffle would change load-balancing behavior for every user on that strategy and is out of scope here — leaving it for a follow-up. ## Tests `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_simple_shuffle.py` — 10 new unit tests: `TestPickWeightField`: - `test_returns_none_when_no_deployment_declares_anything` - `test_returns_weight_when_declared_on_first` - `test_returns_weight_when_declared_only_on_later_deployments` — **the headline regression test** - `test_precedence_weight_over_rpm_over_tpm` — covers two precedence pairs - `test_handles_missing_litellm_params` — defensive `TestSimpleShuffle` (statistical assertions over 6,000 picks): - `test_uniform_random_when_no_weights` - `test_rpm_on_later_deployment_is_respected` — end-to-end regression for silent-fallthrough - `test_zero_total_weight_falls_through_to_uniform_random` — divide-by-zero defense - `test_single_deployment_always_picked` - `test_weight_field_wins_over_rpm` — precedence under simple_shuffle (not just helper) ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_simple_shuffle.py -q 10 passed in 0.17s ``` ## Related Companion PRs from the same audit: - #27913 — fix(rate-limit): stop v3 limiter from leaking internal stash to provider body - #27914 — fix(rate-limit): resolve router model_name aliases to real provider (stacked on #27687) - #27915 — fix(exceptions): don't map upstream 400 to RateLimitError on substring match [Slack Thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/D0AUCPA0MLN/p1778738597799989?thread_ts=1778738597.799989&cid=D0AUCPA0MLN)

signal.title: fix(exceptions): don't map upstream 400 to RateLimitError on substring match
signal.text: ## Problem OpenAI's `Unknown parameter: ''` / `Unrecognized request arguments supplied: , ` 400s, which echo the rejected field name back in the message, get misclassified as 429 `RateLimitError` whenever the field name contains `rate_limit` (or any `rate[\s_\-]*limit` substring) — e.g. `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors`. Concretely: while reproducing the v3 limiter leak (PR #27001 → PR #27913), OpenAI returned ``` { "error": { "message": "Unknown parameter: '_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors'.", "code": "400" } } ``` and LiteLLM surfaced it to the client as ``` HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests { "error": { "message": "litellm.RateLimitError: OpenAIException - Unknown parameter: '_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors'.", "type": "throttling_error", "code": "429" } } ``` That breaks two contracts: 1. **Retry semantics.** Clients see `429 throttling_error` and assume "back off and retry" — but the upstream rejected the body, retrying won't help. Loops forever on a malformed request. 2. **Debuggability.** It's the misclassification that hid the v3 leak: the 429 made it look like rate-limiting working as intended. The bug only surfaced after end-to-end provider testing. ## Root cause In `litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py`: **Cause 1 — unanchored regex:** `ExceptionCheckers.is_error_str_rate_limit` uses `re.search(r"rate[\s_\-]*limit", _error_str_lower)`. No word boundary, so it matches `rate_limit` as a substring of any identifier. Real OpenAI 400 body fields named with `rate_limit` (or LiteLLM-internal field names like `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors` leaked into the body) all trip the heuristic. **Cause 2 — heuristic runs before status code:** Inside the OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible / Mistral branch of `exception_type`, `is_error_str_rate_limit` is called unconditionally — *before* the status-code branch that handles 400 → `BadRequestError`. So an explicit upstream 400 never gets a chance to map correctly when the string matches. Anthropic's branch was already correct: it routes 400/413 to `BadRequestError` via status code, no string heuristic up front. (Companion observation in PR #16482, which tightened `\b429\b` against `429` substrings — same shape of bug, different token.) ## Fix **Anchor the regex** with a leading word boundary: `\brate[\s_\-]*limit`. Embedded identifiers like `_litellm_rate_limit_descriptors` no longer match (the preceding `_` is a word char so `\b` fails). Standalone phrases all still match: `Rate limit exceeded`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `rate-limit-exceeded`, `You hit a rate limit`. **Status-code gate at the mapping site:** when `getattr(original_exception, "status_code", None) == 400`, skip the string heuristic entirely. A 400 is unambiguous per RFC 9110 — the upstream rejected the body, not the rate. Don't second-guess it. Both fixes are independent and complementary: the regex fix protects unknown-status-code paths (some upstream errors don't carry `status_code`), and the gate protects against any future heuristic that could mistake a 400 message for a 429. ## Tests `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py`: - `test_is_error_str_rate_limit_ignores_field_name_substring` — three forms of the OpenAI 400 wire message all return False. - `test_is_error_str_rate_limit_still_matches_standalone_token` — proves the tightening didn't regress legitimate detections. - `TestExceptionTypeStatusCodeGate` — end-to-end mapper tests. Build a real `openai.BadRequestError` with status 400 and the wire messages we saw, run `exception_type`, assert the result is `litellm.BadRequestError` (not `RateLimitError`). - `test_openai_429_still_maps_to_rate_limit` — confirms the genuine 429 path is untouched. ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py -q 43 passed in 0.21s ``` ## Related Companion to #27913 (which fixes the underlying v3 limiter leak that this misclassification was hiding). [Slack Thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/D0AUCPA0MLN/p1778738597799989?thread_ts=1778738597.799989&cid=D0AUCPA0MLN)

signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - LIT012 gates CI but CLAUDE.md never mentions it - Agents keep writing writable TypedDict fields How it solves it: - Document `ReadOnly[...]` on every TypedDict field - Name the `# writable-ok: <reason>` escape hatch ## User Flow Before: an agent writing a new TypedDict has no rule telling it the fields must be read-only 1. It reads CLAUDE.md, which covers LIT001, LIT002, LIT009, LIT010 and LIT011, but says nothing about TypedDict fields 2. It adds a TypedDict with plain `str` / `int` fields 3. signal.title: [Bug]: Managed Bedrock batches cannot be cancelled through /v1/batches/{id}/cancel
signal.text: ## What happened A LiteLLM managed Bedrock batch can be created and reach `InProgress`, but `POST /v1/batches/{managed_id}/cancel` fails before reaching AWS: ```text LiteLLM doesn't support bedrock for `cancel_batch`. Only openai, azure, and vertex_ai are supported. ``` The equivalent provider operation is AWS Bedrock `StopModelInvocationJob`. ## Reproduction 1. Configure a managed Bedrock batch model with `model_info.mode: batch`, an S3 staging bucket, and `aws_batch_role_arn`. 2. `POST /v1/files` with a valid 100-record JSONL file. 3. `POST /v1/batches` using the managed input file and wait for the provider job to reach `InProgress`. 4. `POST /v1/batches/{managed_batch_id}/cancel`. Expected: LiteLLM calls `StopModelInvocationJob` and returns an OpenAI-compatible batch resource with `status=cancelling`, then `cancelled` when Bedrock reports `Stopped`. Actual: LiteLLM returns HTTP 400 without calling Bedrock. ## Root cause `litellm.cancel_batch` / `acancel_batch` only dispatches OpenAI, Azure, and Vertex batch cancellation. Bedrock has a retrieve handler for `GetModelInvocationJob`, but no corresponding cancellation handler for `StopModelInvocationJob`. ## Proposed behavior Add a Bedrock cancellation branch that: - accepts either a full `model-invocation-job` ARN or a bare job identifier; - resolves region and credentials through the same `BedrockBatchesConfig.get_credentials` path as retrieve; - calls `client.stop_model_invocation_job(jobIdentifier=batch_id)`; - follows with `get_model_invocation_job` and maps `Stopping` to `cancelling` and `Stopped` to `cancelled`; - treats the provider's terminal-state `ValidationException` as idempotent cancellation, returning the current terminal status. ## Regression coverage A focused regression should mock the Bedrock control plane and cover: - active cancellation; - full ARN and bare job IDs; - credentials and ARN-region propagation; - `Stopping` / `Stopped` mapping; - repeated cancel after a terminal state; - no credential material in serialized batch responses. ## Environment LiteLLM proxy 1.89.1 with a real AWS Bedrock managed batch, reproduced locally through `/v1/files` and `/v1/batches`.

signal.title: fix: add NotFoundErrorRetries to RetryPolicy
signal.text: Fixes #36896 ## What this does `RetryPolicy` had a retry count field for every exception type except `NotFoundError` (404s). Because of that gap, 404s always fall back to `num_retries`, so the router retries them — and since 404 also triggers an immediate cooldown per deployment, each retry cools down another deployment. After enough retries the whole pool gets cooled and the router raises `RouterRateLimitError("No deployments available")`, which surfaces to the client as a 500. This adds a `NotFoundErrorRetries` field so operators can set it to `0` and have 404s returned to the client immediately instead of being retried across the whole deployment pool. ## Changes - `litellm/types/router.py`: added `NotFoundErrorRetries: int | None = None` to `RetryPolicy`. - `litellm/router_utils/get_retry_from_policy.py`: imported `NotFoundError` and added a check in `get_num_retries_from_retry_policy()` so `NotFoundErrorRetries` is respected. - `tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_helper_utils.py`: added a `NotFoundError` case to the existing `test_get_num_retries_from_retry_policy` parametrized test, using `0` retries to match the motivating case from the issue. ## Testing Ran the existing parametrized test locally — all cases pass including the new `NotFoundError` one. Note: this PR only addresses the missing retry field (the primary fix requested in the issue). The secondary "paradox" behavior mentioned in the issue (an exception that triggers cooldown also being retried by default) is a broader behavioral change and is left out of scope here. @ @

signal.title: feat(spend-logs): opt-in suppression of stack traces in spend-tracking error logs
signal.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2704 ## Summary Spend-tracking error paths log full multi-line stack traces on every 4xx/5xx and transient DB error. Customers running the proxy at log level `INFO` are seeing these tracebacks dominate downstream log volume even though they have no actionable signal — Sentry already receives the exceptions via `proxy_logging_obj.failure_handler`. This PR adds a new opt-in env var, `LITELLM_SUPPRESS_SPEND_LOG_TRACEBACKS`. When it is truthy and the proxy logger is at `INFO` (or higher), spend-tracking error paths emit a single concise `ERROR` line and drop the traceback. At `DEBUG`, the full traceback is still preserved so operators can troubleshoot without unsetting the env var. Sentry / `failure_handler` flow is unchanged. ## Implementation New helper `litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.spend_log_error_logger.spend_log_error(message, *args, exc=None)`: - Reads the env var fresh each call (so dynamic flips work). - Suppresses traceback only when env var is true **and** logger is not at DEBUG. - Otherwise behaves like `verbose_proxy_logger.exception` (active exception's traceback attached). Wired through the spend write hot path: - `litellm/proxy/db/db_spend_update_writer.py` — `update_database`, `_update_key_db`, `_update_user_db`, `_update_team_db`, `_update_org_db`, `_update_agent_db`, `_update_tag_db`, `_update_daily_spend` batch upsert, both `_commit_spend_updates_to_db_with_redis` and `_commit_daily_tag_spend_to_db_with_redis` redis-fallback paths. - `litellm/proxy/hooks/proxy_track_cost_callback.py` — `_PROXY_track_cost_callback` outer except. - `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py` — `get_logging_payload` outer except. - `litellm/proxy/utils.py` — `update_daily_tag_spend` and the spend-logs queue monitor. The pre-existing `verbose_proxy_logger.debug(..., traceback.format_exc())` call sites in `_batch_database_updates` are left as-is — they only emit at `DEBUG`, so `INFO` users were never seeing them. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit` (relevant suites: `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/`, `tests/test_litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/`, `tests/test_litellm/proxy/hooks/test_proxy_track_cost_callback.py`, `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py` — 294 passed) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes - New module `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_log_error_logger.py` exposing `spend_log_error()` and `should_suppress_spend_log_tracebacks()`. - Replaced 14 stack-trace-emitting log sites in the spend-tracking write path with `spend_log_error()`. - New unit test file `tests/test_litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/test_spend_log_error_logger.py` (15 tests) covering env-var gating, log-level interaction, default-on traceback behavior, and `exc=` vs. active-exception attachment. - Updated `tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/test_db_spend_update_writer.py::test_update_daily_spend_logs_detailed_error_on_batch_upsert_failure` to assert against the new ERROR-level emission. ## Configuration ```bash # Opt in (default: off, fully backwards compatible) export LITELLM_SUPPRESS_SPEND_LOG_TRACEBACKS=true ``` When unset or set to `false`, behavior is identical to `main`. Linear Issue: [LIT-2704](https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-2704/suppress-spend-log-stack-traces-when-log-level-is-info)

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): bill Gemini grounding per unique web search query
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Gemini 3 grounding under `web_search_billing_unit: "per_query"` overstates cost. `VertexGeminiConfig._calculate_web_search_requests` summed every non-empty `webSearchQueries` string across grounding metadata items, so when the model runs a deep multi-search loop and repeats a query the count is inflated - Google bills per unique query the model executes, ignoring empty queries. The reporter measured the LiteLLM/Google ratio rising from 1.00 to 1.75 as searches per request grew, with LiteLLM believing single requests issued up to 113 billable searches How it solves it: - Count distinct non-empty queries across all grounding metadata items in a request, matching Google's documented rule - Preserve the existing `int | None` contract (returns `None` when there are no billable queries), so the three call sites are unchanged - Gemini 2.x (`per_prompt`) is unaffected: `cost_per_web_search_request` already clamps `per_prompt` to 1 ## User Flow A proxy or SDK caller uses `vertex_ai/gemini-3-*` with `tools: [{googleSearch: {}}]`. When the model executes several searches in one request and repeats a query string, the returned `usage.prompt_tokens_details.web_search_requests` and the resulting spend now reflect unique queries instead of raw emitted strings. ## Relevant issues Fixes #36377 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is an internal billing-count helper, so the proof is a unit RED to GREEN on the exact function. A live curl proof would require a real Gemini 3 request that non-deterministically repeats search queries, which cannot be forced reliably. RED on `litellm_internal_staging` (before the fix), duplicate queries counted twice: ``` E AssertionError: assert 3 == 2 tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/test_vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py:5568: AssertionError 1 failed in 1.15s ``` GREEN with the fix: ``` tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/test_vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py::test_calculate_web_search_requests_counts_unique_queries PASSED 1 passed in 0.33s ``` Full mapped test file after the fix: `146 passed` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py`: `_calculate_web_search_requests` now returns the count of distinct non-empty queries across grounding metadata items, or `None` when there are none - `tests/test_litellm/.../test_vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py`: regression test covering duplicates within one item, duplicates across items, empty input, and all-empty-strings ## QA runbook Run `make test-unit` (or the scoped file) and confirm `test_calculate_web_search_requests_counts_unique_queries` passes. For a live check, send a `vertex_ai/gemini-3-*` request with `googleSearch` enabled and a prompt that triggers several searches, then confirm `usage.prompt_tokens_details.web_search_requests` equals the number of distinct queries in `groundingMetadata.webSearchQueries` rather than the raw string count. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(scim): refresh / invalidate user cache on PATCH/PUT/DELETE /Users (Fixes #37009)
signal.text: ## Problem The SCIM v2 user endpoints (\`PATCH /scim/v2/Users/{id}\`, \`PUT /scim/v2/Users/{id}\`, \`DELETE /scim/v2/Users/{id}\`) currently only write to \`litellm_usertable\` and do not refresh or invalidate the in-memory user cache used by \`get_user_object\` (which is keyed on the literal \`user_id\` per \`auth_checks.py:1641\`). The very next auth check that hits the cache serves the pre-mutation user, so: - \`PUT\` (full replace, e.g. an email or role change) does not take effect on auth until the management-object TTL expires. - \`PATCH\` (e.g. deactivation via \`active: false\`) does not take effect on auth until the TTL expires. This is especially visible: the same PATCH has already called \`_set_user_keys_blocked\` to block the user's keys, but the cached \`LiteLLM_UserTable\` still reports the user as active. - \`DELETE\` does not invalidate the cached \`user_id\` entry, so a same-user \`POST /user/new\` reusing the same ID would read a stale \`user_email\` / \`metadata\` / \`teams\` snapshot from the cache. SCIM is the standard protocol for IdP-driven user sync (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin, JumpCloud, etc.), so the impact is real for every operator using an IdP-driven deployment: a SCIM-driven deactivation or email rename is silently lost for the cache TTL window on every request. In a multi-pod deployment, the window extends across replicas. This is the same multi-prefix cache Achilles heel pattern already fixed in: - #35565 (cycle 9): \`/team/block\` and \`/team/unblock\` - #36817 (cycle 12): SCIM \`PATCH/PUT/DELETE /Groups/{id}\` The \`/Users\` surface was missed in #36817 because the user cache key shape is different from the team cache key shape. The team cache is dual-keyed (\`team_id:{id}\` + \`team_alias:{alias}\`); the user cache is single-keyed on the literal \`user_id\`. Same defect class, different code path. ## Implementation summary - Add \`_cache_user_object\` and \`_refresh_cached_user\` helpers in \`litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py\` (mirrors the existing \`_cache_team_object\` and \`_refresh_cached_team\`). \`_refresh_cached_user\` accepts either a \`LiteLLM_UserTable\` Pydantic model (the real Prisma return) or a dict (pre-existing test mock contract); production always takes the Pydantic branch. - Add \`_invalidate_cached_user\` helper for the DELETE path. There is no post-mutation row to cache, so refresh is wrong. The helper clears both the local LRU (\`user_api_key_cache.delete_cache\`) and the Redis side of the dual cache (\`proxy_logging_obj.internal_usage_cache.dual_cache.async_delete_cache\`). - \`update_user\` (PUT) and \`patch_user\` (PATCH) call \`_refresh_cached_user\` after the database write. - \`delete_user\` (DELETE) calls \`_invalidate_cached_user\` after the row is deleted. - \`create_user\` (POST) needs no cache work — the user is new, not yet in cache. ## Testing Three regression tests in \`tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/test_scim_v2_endpoints.py\` in a new \`TestScimUserCacheInvalidation\` class (mirrors cycle 12's \`TestScimGroupCacheInvalidation\`: - `test_update_user_refreshes_user_cache` drives `update_user` with mocked Prisma + cache + `_refresh_cached_user`, and asserts the refresh was awaited exactly once with the post-mutation row, the local cache, and the proxy logging handles. - `test_patch_user_refreshes_user_cache` does the same for `patch_user`, mocking `_apply_patch_ops` and `_get_scim_admin_group` to drive the full PATCH flow. - `test_delete_user_invalidates_user_cache` drives `delete_user` and asserts `user_api_key_cache.delete_cache` and `dual_cache.async_delete_cache` were each called with `key=user_id` (the literal `user_id`, not a `user_id:{id}` prefix). All three pins are verified to fail without the source fix and pass with it (self-audit: stashed the source diff, re-ran the 3 tests, observed `AttributeError` on the new helper names — restore, re-run, all 3 pass). Pre-existing test fixtures in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/test_scim_key_deactivation.py` needed a small update: they patched `user_api_key_cache` and `proxy_logging_obj` as plain `MagicMock()`, which failed once the new fix called `await user_api_key_cache.async_set_cache(...)` with `TypeError: object MagicMock can't be used in 'await' expression`. Added `_make_user_api_key_cache_mock` (sync MagicMock with `async_set_cache = AsyncMock()`) and `_make_logging_mock` (sync MagicMock with `internal_usage_cache.dual_cache.async_delete_cache = AsyncMock()`) and switched 6 call sites to the helpers. AsyncMock alone would have made the sync `delete_cache` call a never-awaited coroutine; plain MagicMock fails the await on the async method. The hybrid is the minimal correct shape. ## Files changed - `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py` (+99/-0): new `_cache_user_object`, `_refresh_cached_user`, `_invalidate_cached_user` helpers; one new `Mapping` import for the union type annotation; one cast narrowing for `user_id` - `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/scim_v2.py` (+60/-0): import the new helpers, call `_refresh_cached_user` in `update_user` and `patch_user`, call `_invalidate_cached_user` in `delete_user` - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/test_scim_v2_endpoints.py` (+347/-0): 3 new regression tests in `TestScimUserCacheInvalidation` class - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/test_scim_key_deactivation.py` (+194/-0): new `_make_user_api_key_cache_mock` and `_make_logging_mock` helpers; 6 call sites updated to use them ## Test results - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/`: 155 passed (was 152 before; 3 new tests added) - `scripts/type_discipline_gate.py`: OK - `scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py`: OK - `ruff check`: All checks passed - `ruff format --check`: 4 files already formatted ## Risks - `_refresh_cached_user` is a new helper. If a future SCIM endpoint mutates `litellm_usertable` without calling it, the same defect recurs. Mitigation: cross-reference in the issue body so future contributors see the pattern. - `_invalidate_cached_user` does both `user_api_key_cache.delete_cache` and `dual_cache.async_delete_cache`. If the proxy has no Redis (single-LRU mode), the dual cache is a no-op, so the second call is safe. The cycle 12 /Groups fix used the same pattern. ## Backward compatibility No API surface change. Internal cache-management only. ## Future improvement opportunities - The `_refresh_cached_user` / `_invalidate_cached_user` pair could be deduped into a single `_manage_user_cache(action=refresh|invalidate, ...)` helper, mirroring the pattern of the team endpoint. Skipped for this PR to keep the diff focused on the bug fix. - The dict-or-Pydantic defensive shim in `_refresh_cached_user` is a test-contract concession. If the pre-existing SCIM user tests are migrated to a Pydantic mock contract in a follow-up, the shim can be removed. Fixes #37009. EOF )

signal.title: [Bug]: SCIM PATCH/PUT/DELETE /Users/{id} leave the in-memory user cache stale
signal.text: ## Problem The SCIM v2 user endpoints (`PATCH /scim/v2/Users/{id}`, `PUT /scim/v2/Users/{id}`, `DELETE /scim/v2/Users/{id}`) currently only write to `litellm_usertable` and do not refresh or invalidate the in-memory user cache used by `get_user_object` (which is keyed on the literal `user_id` per `auth_checks.py:1641`). The very next auth check that hits the cache serves the pre-mutation user, so: - `PUT` (full replace, e.g. an email or role change) does not take effect on auth until the management-object TTL expires. - `PATCH` (e.g. deactivation via `active: false`) does not take effect on auth until the TTL expires — even though the same PATCH has already called `_set_user_keys_blocked` to block the user's keys, the cached `LiteLLM_UserTable` still reports the user as active. - `DELETE` does not invalidate the cached `user_id` entry, so a same-user `POST /user/new` reusing the same ID would read a stale `user_email` / `metadata` / `teams` snapshot from the cache. ## Why this matters SCIM is the standard protocol for IdP-driven user sync (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin, JumpCloud, etc.). Operators using an IdP-driven deployment expect a SCIM-driven deactivation or rename to take effect immediately on the proxy. Without cache invalidation, the stale read is silently served on every request for the TTL window — and in a multi-pod deployment, the window extends across replicas. This is the same multi-prefix cache Achilles heel pattern already fixed in: - #35565 (cycle 9): `/team/block` and `/team/unblock` - #36817 (cycle 12): SCIM `PATCH/PUT/DELETE /Groups/{id}` The `/Users` surface was missed in #36817 because the user cache key shape is different from the team cache key shape. The team cache is dual-keyed (`team_id:{id}` + `team_alias:{alias}`); the user cache is single-keyed on the literal `user_id`. Same defect class, different code path. ## Current behavior `PUT /scim/v2/Users/{id}` updates the DB row, returns the new SCIM user shape, and leaves `user_api_key_cache[user_id]` unchanged. ## Expected behavior `PUT` and `PATCH` should call `_refresh_cached_user(updated_user, ...)` after the database write. `DELETE` should invalidate the cache (not refresh, since the user no longer exists) by clearing both halves of the dual cache (local LRU + Redis) for the `user_id` key. `POST /scim/v2/Users` (`create_user`) needs no cache work — the user is new, not yet in cache. ## Proposed solution Add a `_refresh_cached_user` helper in `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py` (mirrors the existing `_refresh_cached_team` at `team_endpoints.py:153`). Import it into `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/scim_v2.py` and call it from the 3 mutating endpoints. Pin with regression tests in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/scim/test_scim_v2_endpoints.py` in a new `TestScimUserCacheInvalidation` class (mirrors cycle 12's `TestScimGroupCacheInvalidation`). ## Alternatives considered 1. Inline the cache write in each endpoint (no helper). Rejected: scatters cache-management knowledge across 3 endpoints, easy to miss on a future SCIM endpoint addition. 2. Reuse `_refresh_cached_team`. Rejected: cache key shape (`user_id` literal vs `team_id:{id}`) and model type (`LiteLLM_UserTable` vs `LiteLLM_TeamTableCachedObj`) differ. ## Scope One source file (`scim_v2.py`, ~25 lines), one helper file (`auth_checks.py`, ~15 lines), one test file (3 tests, ~250 lines). ## Acceptance criteria - `update_user` calls `_refresh_cached_user` exactly once with the post-mutation row. - `patch_user` calls `_refresh_cached_user` exactly once with the post-mutation row. - `delete_user` calls `user_api_key_cache.delete_cache(key=user_id)` AND `proxy_logging_obj.internal_usage_cache.dual_cache.async_delete_cache(key=user_id)` (gated on `proxy_logging_obj is not None`). - 3 new regression tests pass; each is verified to fail without the source fix. - Pre-existing SCIM test suite stays green. ## Backward compatibility No API surface change. Internal cache-management only. ## Risks - `_refresh_cached_user` is a new helper. If a future SCIM endpoint mutates `litellm_usertable` without calling it, the same defect recurs. Mitigation: cross-reference in the new issue body so future contributors see the pattern.

signal.title: Prisma engine watchdog treats ECHILD from waitpid as engine death and forces a reconnect
signal.text: ### The code `litellm/proxy/utils.py`, the thread that waits on the Prisma query engine: ```python def _waitpid_thread_func(self, pid, loop): """Note: uvloop/libuv may reap the child first via waitpid(-1, WNOHANG) in its SIGCHLD handler. In that case our waitpid raises ChildProcessError. we still notify the event loop because the engine is dead either way.""" try: os.waitpid(pid, 0) except ChildProcessError: pass except OSError: pass loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._on_engine_death_from_thread, pid) ``` The comment states the reasoning: *"the engine is dead either way."* We think that is not true. `ChildProcessError` is `ECHILD`, which means **"no such child of mine"** — the child was reaped by someone else, or was never this process's child, or was reparented away. None of those implies the process exited. That distinction is load-bearing here, because this proxy really does have processes that are not its own children. In our container: ``` PID 1 litellm (the application) S PID 559 node-MainThread Z ← never reaped PID 1086 query-engine-de S ← PPID 1, reparented ``` The Node process Prisma spawns to bootstrap the engine exits at startup and stays a zombie for the pod's lifetime; the engine itself has been reparented. A `waitpid` against a PID that is alive but no longer the caller's child is exactly the case that raises `ECHILD`. ### The consequence The notification is unconditional, and the receiver does not re-check liveness: ```python def _on_engine_death_from_thread(self, dead_pid): if self._engine_confirmed_dead: return if dead_pid != self._engine_pid: return if self._consume_expected_death(dead_pid): return # ... engine_process_death + force reconnect ``` Three guards, none of which asks whether the process is running. The class already has `_is_engine_alive()` (`os.kill(pid, 0)`), and this path never calls it. So a spurious `ECHILD` and a real death produce byte-identical behaviour: a forced reconnect that tears down a working connection. ### What we observed, and what we did not establish We saw DB-backed admin endpoints (`/key/list`, `/spend/tags`, `/spend/logs`) intermittently return `500` alongside these log lines: ``` prisma-query-engine PID 4220 exited (waitpid thread); triggering reconnect. Attempting Prisma DB reconnect. reason=engine_process_death prisma-query-engine PID 0 is dead; reconnecting. ``` **We cannot say the incident we saw was a spurious `ECHILD`.** The pod was replaced before we could examine it, and our log retention did not cover that namespace at the time. On the replacement pod the endpoints have been stable and we have not reproduced it. We are reporting the code path rather than the incident: it is reachable, and on that path a live engine and a dead one are indistinguishable. The `PID 0 is dead` line is suggestive — `_is_engine_alive()` treats `_engine_pid <= 0` as alive, so a zeroed PID arriving on a death path looks anomalous — but we cannot tie it to either branch without the pod. ### Suggested fix One line, either way: - Call `_is_engine_alive(pid)` before notifying on the `ECHILD` path, **or** - Do not notify when `waitpid` *raised* — only when it *returned* a status. Related: `_reap_all_zombies()` is only invoked on engine-death paths, never periodically, which is why the startup zombie above survives for the life of the pod. Not a bug on its own, but it is why the process table looks the way it does. ### Version v1.90.0, PostgreSQL backend, container running the app as PID 1 with no init process.
signal.author: b2metric

signal.title: GET /spend/logs has no pagination and OOM-kills the proxy on a large LiteLLM_SpendLogs
signal.text: ### What happens `GET /spend/logs` with no query parameters fetches every row of `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` into memory. On a table of ~110k rows (~371 MB on disk) this exhausts the container and the kernel kills it: ``` reason = OOMKilled exitCode = 137 limit = 4Gi ``` The proxy is unavailable for about a minute while it restarts. In our deployment that proxy fronts all model traffic, so a single admin API call takes every model in the cluster offline. Version: **v1.90.0**, PostgreSQL backend. ### Why it is not avoidable by the caller `view_spend_logs` accepts no pagination parameters at all — there is no `page`, `limit`, or `page_size` in the signature, only filters that all default to `None`: ```python async def view_spend_logs( api_key: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...), user_id: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...), request_id: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...), start_date: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...), end_date: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...), summarize: bool = fastapi.Query(default=True, ...), ... ) ``` and the query is issued with no row cap: ```python data = await SpendLogsRepository(prisma_client).table.find_many( where=filter_query, order={...}, ) ``` `find_many` is called without `take`. A caller who passes no filters therefore cannot bound the result; the only way to stay safe is to know in advance not to call the endpoint. ### The paginated endpoints already exist `/spend/logs/v2` and `/spend/logs/ui` do the right thing: ```python page: int = fastapi.Query(default=1, ge=1) page_size: int = fastapi.Query(default=50, description="Number of items per page", ge=1, le=100) ``` and the admin UI calls those, not the legacy path. So the unbounded behaviour is isolated to the v1 endpoint — which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than a design choice. ### Suggested fix Any of these would close it; the first seems closest to existing behaviour: 1. Add `page` / `page_size` to `view_spend_logs` and pass `take`/`skip` through to `find_many`, mirroring the v2 endpoint. 2. Apply a server-side default cap (e.g. `take=1000`) when no `request_id` is given, and document that the endpoint truncates. 3. Deprecate `/spend/logs` in favour of `/spend/logs/v2` and have it return a `400` when called without filters, pointing at the paginated path. ### Reproducing Populate `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` with a few hundred thousand rows, set a container memory limit in the low gigabytes, then: ``` GET /spend/logs Authorization: Bearer <master key> ``` The request does not return; the connection closes when the process is killed. ### Notes - Retention does not fix this on its own. `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period` bounds growth over time, but a bursty workload can add tens of thousands of rows in a single day, so the table can cross the threshold within any retention window. - We mitigated locally by blocking the exact path at the ingress. That is possible only because the UI uses the `/ui` and `/v2` variants; it is a workaround for an operator, not a fix.

signal.title: fix(responses): return 400 for invalid input types
signal.text: ## Summary - Validate Responses API `input` before iterating over it in prompt management. - Raise `BadRequestError` for non-string, non-list input instead of allowing `TypeError` to propagate as a 500. - Added regression tests covering both `responses()` and `aresponses()`. ### Problem this solves: When `input` is a non-string, non-list value such as an integer, float, boolean, `None`, or dictionary, the Responses API attempts to iterate over it during prompt management. This can raise a `TypeError`, which is subsequently surfaced as a 500 error instead of a client-side 400 validation error. ### How it solves it: Validate the type of `input` before iterating over it. Invalid non-string, non-list values now raise `BadRequestError` with a descriptive message, resulting in a 400-level client error instead of a 500 server error. ## User Flow Before: A client sends an invalid numeric `input` to the Responses API and receives a 500 error instead of a client validation error. 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"input": 12345` and a valid model. 2. The request fails while processing the invalid `input` value. 3. The client receives a 500 response containing a `TypeError` rather than a 400 validation error. After: The same invalid request is rejected as a client error with a descriptive validation message. 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"input": 12345` and a valid model. 2. The request is rejected because `input` must be a string or list of input items. 3. The client receives a 400 response with an error message identifying the invalid `input` type. ## Relevant issues Fixes #36923 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(dashscope): tiered pricing should be all-or-nothing per official docs
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Re-opens the concern raised in [#16150 comment by @togear](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/16150#issuecomment-2806215418) (cites Alibaba's official tiered-billing rules) which never received a follow-up. Related: #14471 (original — correct — implementation), #15423, #16150 (PR that introduced the regression). ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] CLA signed - [x] Added testing in `tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py` (5 existing tests rewritten + 2 new boundary tests) - [x] `make test-unit` passes for the dashscope dir (12/12) - [x] Black, Ruff, MyPy, circular-imports, import-safety all clean - [x] Scope is isolated — only `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` and its test ## Summary This is **not a single-model issue**. It is a systemic mispricing affecting **every Dashscope (Alibaba Bailian) tiered model** — 14 in `model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` today (qwen-flash, qwen-plus, qwen3-coder-plus, qwen3-coder-flash, qwen3-max, qwen-plus-latest and all their dated snapshots), plus any custom user model declaring `tiered_pricing`. It silently breaks `litellm.completion_cost(...)`, spend logs, budgets, team-level quotas, and alerting on every cross-tier request. ## The bug `_calculate_tiered_cost` in `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` currently splits tokens across tiers using **graduated / income-tax-bracket** math. Dashscope's [official billing documentation](https://help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/billing-for-model-studio) explicitly specifies the opposite — **all-or-nothing**: > 百炼部分模型实行阶梯计费。单价取决于单次请求的输入 Token 总量。**该请求的所有 Token 均按对应阶梯的单价结算。** > > 例如，某模型设有两档计费区间：0 < Token ≤ 32K 和 32K < Token ≤ 128K。若输入 100K Token，因数值落在第二区间（32K < 100K ≤ 128K），**所有 Token 均按第二档单价结算**。 (Translation: *The unit price of a request is determined by its total input tokens. ALL tokens in the request are billed at that single tier's rate.*) This regressed in #16150 (2025-11-04), which removed the all-or-nothing logic from the original #14471 implementation and replaced it with graduated brackets. @togear pointed this out in April 2026 on the merged-PR thread, citing the same official source; the comment did not get a maintainer response. There are two related correctness issues, both fixed here: 1. **Tier selection algorithm.** Graduated brackets should be all-or-nothing. 2. **Tier selection input.** `_calculate_prompt_cost` was passing `text_tokens` and `cached_tokens` separately into the tier selector. Per the docs the tier is decided by the *total* request input (text + cache), and that tier's rates apply to every portion (text, cache, and output). The current code can therefore pick a wrong tier even on flat requests when the cache-hit fraction is large. ## Impact (measured against current code + actual Bailian rates for `qwen-plus`) | Request size | Falls in tier | Bailian charge | LiteLLM today | LiteLLM under-bills | |---|---|---|---|---| | 100K | Tier 1 (≤128K) | 0.015 ¥ | 0.015 ¥ | 0% ✓ | | 140K | Tier 2 (128K–256K) | 0.085 ¥ | 0.025 ¥ | **70%** | | 200K | Tier 2 | 0.121 ¥ | 0.061 ¥ | **49%** | | 500K | Tier 3 (256K–1M) | 0.601 ¥ | 0.384 ¥ | **36%** | The closer a request lands to a tier boundary, the worse the under-bill. For users running long-context Qwen workloads (RAG, document analysis, code understanding), a 30–70% gap between LiteLLM's reported spend and the actual Alibaba invoice is large enough to silently blow past team budgets and alert thresholds. This is also a forward-looking concern: any future provider that adopts the `tiered_pricing` array (Moonshot/Kimi, Volcengine/Doubao, GLM, MiniMax — all of which already publish similar input-length-based tiered prices in their public docs) will inherit the same broken semantics unless `tiered_pricing` is defined as all-or-nothing here. ## The fix 1. Replace `_calculate_tiered_cost` (graduated) with a small pair of helpers: - `_select_tier_for_input(total_input_tokens, tiered_pricing) -> Optional[dict]` - `_tier_rate(tier, cost_key, fallback_cost_key=None) -> float` 2. In `_calculate_prompt_cost` and `_calculate_completion_cost`, compute `total_input = text_tokens + cached_tokens` once, select the tier from it, then bill `text_tokens × tier.input_rate + cached_tokens × tier.cache_rate` and `completion_tokens × tier.output_rate + reasoning_tokens × tier.reasoning_rate` against the same tier. 3. Document the semantics + cite the official Bailian source at the top of the module so the next refactor doesn't repeat the regression. Public surface (`cost_per_token`) and helper signatures (`_calculate_prompt_cost`, `_calculate_completion_cost`) are unchanged. Flat-rate fallback path is unchanged. No call sites outside the module use the removed helper (`grep -rn "_calculate_tiered_cost" litellm/ tests/` is empty after the patch). ### Boundary semantics A tier matches when `range_start < total_input <= range_end`, so a request of exactly `range_end` tokens stays in the lower tier — matching the official phrasing `0 < Token ≤ 32K`. Requests exceeding the highest declared range fall back to the last tier's rate. ## Tests `tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py` — 7 tests: | Test | What it locks down | |---|---| | `test_dashscope_flat_pricing_fallback` | Flat-rate models unaffected (qwen-max) | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_within_first_tier` | All-tier-1 request → tier-1 rate | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_crossing_into_higher_tier` | Cross-tier request → entire request at higher tier (the regression case) | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_with_caching` | Tier selected by total input; cache cost billed at input-tier rate | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_exceeding_highest_tier` | Beyond top tier → last-tier rate | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_boundary_at_range_end` | Exactly `range_end` tokens → lower tier | | `test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_output_uses_input_tier` | Output billed at input-selected tier, not by output volume | ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/ -v ====================== 12 passed, 1 warning in 1.15s ======================= ``` ## Lint / type / format ``` $ uv run black --check litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py 2 files would be left unchanged. $ uv run ruff check litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py All checks passed! $ uv run mypy litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py Success: no issues found in 1 source file $ make check-circular-imports check-import-safety No LiteLLM type hints found. [from litellm import *] OK! no issues! ```

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): translate /v1/embeddings batch rows to the Gemini embedding shape
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex batch `/v1/embeddings` rows fail: "no such field: 'contents'" - The OpenAI `input` is dropped entirely on those rows - Embedding result rows come back as raw Vertex jsonl How it solves it: - Route each jsonl line by its own `url` - Embeddings lines emit an `EmbedContentRequest` row - Embedding output rows transform into OpenAI embeddings responses ## User Flow Before: a developer running an embeddings batch job through the gateway sees the batch report success while every row inside it failed and the text they asked to embed was never sent 1. They write `batch_embeddings.jsonl` where every line targets the embeddings endpoint, e.g. `{"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": "hello world from litellm batch"}}` 2. They upload it with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (`purpose=batch`, `model=gemini-embedding-001`) and get back a `file-...` id 3. They create the job with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches passing that `input_file_id` and `"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"`, and a batch id comes back 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reports `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null`, which looks like success 5. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and every row is an error, `{"custom_id": "req-1", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": "... EmbedContentRequest ... no such field: 'contents'"}}`, with not one embedding in the file After: the same job returns one OpenAI embeddings response per input line 1. They write the same `batch_embeddings.jsonl` with `"url": "/v1/embeddings"` lines 2. They upload it with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (`purpose=batch`, `model=gemini-embedding-001`) and get back a `file-...` id 3. They create the job with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches passing that `input_file_id` and `"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"`, and a batch id comes back 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it reports `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null` 5. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and get one row per input line, e.g. `{"custom_id": "req-1", "response": {"status_code": 200, "body": {"object": "list", "data": [{"embedding": [...], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 7}}}, "error": null}` 6. A line whose `input` was an array of N texts comes back as one row whose `data` holds N embeddings, index-aligned with the input array ## Relevant issues Fixes #35638 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4920 Resolves LIT-5123 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live Vertex AI batch runs against a real project in `us-central1`, staging through a real GCS bucket; no mocks anywhere. Latest re-verification after the staging merge: before on `litellm_internal_staging` at `f03df1bb42`, after at the PR tip `de77711cf9`. The earlier full-coverage runs at `627d2755da` and `bf723fa9c1` are kept below <details open><summary>Re-verification: the same 2-entry batch before at f03df1bb42 and after at de77711cf9</summary> Input file: `req-1` with a single string input, `req-2` with an array of 2 texts, both lines `"url": "/v1/embeddings"`. Identical commands both times: upload `curl -X POST http://localhost:<port>/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -F purpose=batch -F 'model=gemini-embedding-001' -F file=@batch_embeddings.jsonl`, create via `POST /v1/batches` with the returned `input_file_id` and `"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"`, poll `GET /v1/batches/<id>` to `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null` (~4 min), then fetch `GET /v1/files/<output_file_id>/content` Before at `f03df1bb42`, what LiteLLM staged to GCS is chat-shaped with the customer texts replaced by a single space and req-2's 2-text array collapsed into one row ```json {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-1"}}} {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-2"}}} ``` and the content fetch returned 2 rows with zero embeddings ```json {"id": "batch_req_7ec23587-6414-415d-a686-4b4399251fec", "custom_id": "req-2", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": "{\"code\":3,\"space\":\"generic\",\"message\":\"Failed to 'contents'\"}"}} {"id": "batch_req_2c1a60ce-b35a-40e5-b50a-d5899bf25c34", "custom_id": "req-1", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": texts intact ```json {"key": "req-1", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "hello world from litellm batch"}]}}} {"key": "req-2#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "first text"}]}}} {"key": "req-2#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "second text"}]}}} ``` and the content fetch returned one OpenAI row per entry, embedding arrays trimmed here ```json {"id": "batch_req_0bf52833-0663-45b3-ac9a-cfda7f4bb030", "custom_id": "req-2", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id": "", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "data": [{"embedding": [-0.029436894, 0.024541076, "...3072 floats"], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}, {"embedding": [0.01739435, 0.002744379, "...3072 floats"], "index": 1, "object": "embedding"}], "object": "list", "usage": {"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 4, "total_tokens": 4}}}, "error": null} {"id": "batch_req_eedcbbb6-19bc-42f9-acd3-7c13522f146e", "custom_id": "req-1", "response": {"status_code": 200, "request_id": "", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "data": [{"embedding": [-0.020151937, 0.020540899, "...3072 floats"], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}], "object": "list", "usage": {"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 7}}}, "error": null} ``` cosine between a live online `/v1/embeddings` call for `"first text"` and the batch `req-2` `data[0]` vector is 1.000000, against `data[1]` it is 0.806420, so `data[0]` aligns with `input[0]` specifically </details> <details><summary>After: one real batch job over a mixed single / array / nested-combined input</summary> Input file, uploaded with `curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -F purpose=batch -F 'model=gemini-embedding-001' -F file=@batch_embeddings.jsonl` ```json {"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": "hello world from litellm batch"}} {"custom_id": "req-4", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": ["ALPHA: photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy", "BETA: the Baroque period followed the Renaissance in music"], "dimensions": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"custom_id": "req-5", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": ["ONE: submarines navigate using sonar", "TWO: sourdough bread needs a starter culture", "THREE: the Voyager probes left the solar system"]}} {"custom_id": "req-6", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": [["a caption about mountains", "and a second combined part about rivers"]]}} ``` what LiteLLM actually wrote to GCS, 7 Vertex rows for 4 entries ```json {"key": "req-1", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "hello world from litellm batch"}]}}} {"key": "req-4#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "ALPHA: photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"key": "req-4#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "BETA: the Baroque period followed the Renaissance in music"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"key": "req-5#0/3", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "ONE: submarines navigate using sonar"}]}}} {"key": "req-5#1/3", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "TWO: sourdough bread needs a starter culture"}]}}} {"key": "req-5#2/3", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "THREE: the Voyager probes left the solar system"}]}}} {"key": "req-6", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "a caption about mountains"}, {"text": "and a second combined part about rivers"}]}}} ``` Vertex job 50095132740943872 reached `JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED` and `GET /v1/batches/<id>` went validating -> in_progress -> `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null`. Vertex accepted `#` and `/` in `key` and echoed both back verbatim, and it happened to return the rows scrambled (`req-5#1`, `req-5#2`, `req-6`, `req-4#1`, `req-5#0`, `req-1`, `req-4#0`), so the reassembly was genuinely exercised `GET /v1/files/<output_file_id>/content` returned four rows, one per input entry, custom_ids bare ```json {"id": "batch_req_...", "custom_id": "req-4", "response": {"status_code": 200, "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "object": "list", "data": [{"embedding": ["...768 floats..."], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}, {"embedding": ["...768 floats..."], "index": 1, "object": "embedding"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 18, "total_tokens": 18}}}, "error": null} ``` ``` req-5 status_code=200 error=null data=3 indexes=[0,1,2] dims=[3072,3072,3072] usage.prompt_tokens=23 req-6 status_code=200 error=null data=1 indexes=[0] dims=[3072] usage.prompt_tokens=11 req-4 status_code=200 error=null data=2 indexes=[0,1] dims=[768,768] usage.prompt_tokens=18 req-1 status_code=200 error=null data=1 indexes=[0] dims=[3072] usage.prompt_tokens=7 ``` Cosine check of each position against a live online `/v1/embeddings` call for that exact text and params confirms the order follows the input array rather than the order Vertex wrote the rows in ``` req-4 data[0] cos=1.0 vs ALPHA (0.6653 vs BETA) data[1] cos=1.0 vs BETA (0.6653 vs ALPHA) req-5 data[0] cos=1.0 vs ONE data[1] cos=1.0 vs TWO data[2] cos=1.0 vs THREE ``` </details> <details><summary>After, second run at bf723fa9c1: custom_ids that collide with the fan-out key format</summary> Same setup, one batch job over a plain scalar entry `req-a`, a lookalike scalar entry whose custom_id literally is `req-a#0/2`, an array entry whose custom_id literally is `req-b#1/1` (with `dimensions: 768`), and a plain array entry `req-c` what LiteLLM wrote to GCS ```json {"key": "req-a", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "PLAIN: koalas sleep up to twenty hours a day"}]}}} {"key": "req-a%230%2F2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "LOOKALIKE: the Rosetta Stone was found in 1799"}]}}} {"key": "req-b%231%2F1#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "GAMMA: tectonic plates drift a few centimetres a year"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"key": "req-b%231%2F1#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "DELTA: the tuba is the lowest brass instrument"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"}} {"key": "req-c#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "EPSILON: honey never spoils in a sealed jar"}]}}} {"key": "req-c#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "ZETA: Mercury has no atmosphere to speak of"}]}}} ``` Vertex job 6020509242262290432 reached `JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED` with `error: null`, the batch reached `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null`, and Vertex echoed every key back byte for byte including the escapes. It returned the rows scrambled again (`req-c#1/2`, `req-b%231%2F1#0/2`, `req-b%231%2F1#1/2`, `req-a`, `req-a%230%2F2`, `req-c#0/2`) ``` req-c status_code=200 error=null data=2 indexes=[0,1] dims=[3072,3072] usage.prompt_tokens=20 req-b#1/1 status_code=200 error=null data=2 indexes=[0,1] dims=[768,768] usage.prompt_tokens=20 req-a status_code=200 error=null data=1 indexes=[0] dims=[3072] usage.prompt_tokens=11 req-a#0/2 status_code=200 error=null data=1 indexes=[0] dims=[3072] usage.prompt_tokens=15 ``` custom_ids come back byte for byte, and the lookalike stays its own row rather than folding into `req-a`: the two carry different vectors (cosine 0.5318 between them) and their own usage, 11 and 15, matching the `promptTokenCount` Vertex reported for each. Cosine per array position against online `/v1/embeddings` for the same text and params is 1.0 (0.7192 and 0.5953 against the siblings), so ordering again came from the key rather than the file </details> <details><summary>Why the per-row config sits inside request rather than in the documented embed_content_config sibling</summary> An earlier revision of this PR emitted the shape from the docs and Vertex failed the entire job, not the row: `The column or property "embed_content_config" in the specified input data is of unsupported type. Supported types for this column are: [STRING, INTEGER, FLOAT, BOOLEAN, TIMESTAMP, DATE, DATETIME, NUMERIC].` A hand-written file copied from the docs example, submitted straight to the Vertex REST API with no LiteLLM in the loop, fails identically, so that shape simply does not work against the live API today. The same fields inside the `EmbedContentRequest` succeed, and the 768-length vectors for req-4 above show the dimensionality is honored The live runs also showed usage arriving as `response.usageMetadata.promptTokenCount` rather than the documented `response.tokenCount`, which is why the transform reads the former and keeps the latter as a fallback </details> ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Legacy `text-embedding-*` predict-shape batches stay unsupported, untouched - Per-row config rides inside `request`; live Vertex rejects documented `embed_content_config` ## Changes `VertexAIFilesConfig` only ever implemented the Gemini chat batch translation. Every jsonl line of an uploaded batch file went through `_transform_request_body`, which reads `body["messages"]`, so an `/v1/embeddings` line was rewritten as ```jsonc {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-1"}}} ``` Two independent bugs there: `EmbedContentRequest` has no `contents` field (that is the `generateContent` shape), which is the 400 the customer saw on every row, and the actual embedding `input` was never read, so even the shape-correct rows would have embedded a placeholder space. `labels` is not a field on `EmbedContentRequest` either, so the `custom_id` smuggling would have been the next 400 after fixing `contents` Lines are now routed by the `url` that OpenAI puts on each one, and embeddings lines are translated into the batch shape Vertex documents for `gemini-embedding-*` at https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/embeddings/batch-prediction-genai-embeddings ```jsonc { "key": "req-1", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "hello world"}]}, "output_dimensionality": 768, "task_type": "RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT"} } ``` `content` is singular, and the `custom_id` round-trips through the top-level `key` that Vertex echoes back, so embedding rows no longer need the label trick. The docs put the per-row config in an `embed_content_config` sibling of `request`; the live API rejects that key and fails the whole job, so it goes inside the `EmbedContentRequest` instead, which is what actually works (see the proof section). The OpenAI to `EmbedContentRequest` mapping itself is the one already used by the online `embedContent` path (`transform_openai_input_gemini_embed_content`), so `dimensions`, `task_type`, `title`, and `gs://` multimodal inputs come along for free. Chat lines are untouched and keep going through `_transform_request_body` with their labels An `EmbedContentRequest` returns exactly one vector, while an OpenAI entry with an array `input` expects one embedding per element, so array entries fan out into one Vertex row per element and the element position rides along in the key as `<custom_id>#<i>/<n>` ```jsonc {"key": "req-4#0/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "first"}]}}} {"key": "req-4#1/2", "request": {"content": {"parts": [{"text": "second"}]}}} ``` The custom_id half of the key is percent-encoded so that a customer one which itself ends in `#<i>/<n>` cannot be read back as the tag and merged into a different entry; ordinary ids are unreserved characters and so are unchanged on the wire Scalars and single-element arrays keep a bare key, and a nested array (OpenAI's combined-parts shape) stays one row with several `parts`, since that is genuinely one embedding. On the way back the rows are grouped by the custom_id in front of the `#` and ordered by the index behind it, so one OpenAI row comes out per original entry with `data[i]` matching `input[i]` and the prompt tokens summed; Vertex returns predictions in arbitrary order, so the key is the only thing that can carry the position. If any element of an entry failed, the whole entry's row is the error row, because a partial `data` array would silently misalign every index after the gap. A missing or duplicated fan-out row errors the entry the same way: the group size rides in the key, and a group that does not come back as exactly the indexes `0..n-1` is refused rather than silently renumbered onto the wrong input positions On the way back, `_try_transform_vertex_batch_output_to_openai` gated batch detection on `candidates` / `promptFeedback` / `processed_time`, so embedding result rows failed detection and the caller got raw Vertex jsonl. They are now detected on `response.embedding` and turned into a normal OpenAI batch row whose body is an `EmbeddingResponse`, with `usageMetadata.promptTokenCount` as the usage (the documented `tokenCount` is kept as a fallback) and the model recovered from the managed GCS path since embedding rows carry no `modelVersion` Scope is the modern Gemini embedding models. The legacy `text-embedding-*` `predict` format, which has no `request` wrapper at all, stays unsupported and is left untouched rather than half-translated; happy to do it in a follow-up if we want those models on batch ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7c5c3f3f492f4bde87289f9f46caec9e Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d389d721419d486e83067a4fb76f683f <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit f2a10f6331ef99881c5529f362c154c402c58a52. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: [Bug]: Vertex AI batch /v1/embeddings rows drop `input` and emit the chat `contents` shape
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? > Searched `is:issue` for `vertex batch embeddings`, `EmbedContentRequest`, `"no such field"`, and > `_openai_batch_jsonl_entries_to_vertex_wrapped_requests`. No existing **issue** covers this. > > There is, however, an open **PR** that fixes exactly this: > **[#35092 — fix(vertex_ai): translate /v1/embeddings batch rows to the Gemini embedding shape](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/35092)** > (opened 2026-07-29, still open/unmerged as of filing, `Resolves LIT-4920`). I'm filing this anyway > so the bug has a public issue to reference — PR #35092's "Relevant issues" section is empty, and > anyone hitting this on a released version currently finds nothing when they search. Happy to close > as soon as #35092 lands. --- ### Setup that triggers it Submitting an embeddings batch job through the managed-files flow with a Vertex AI / Gemini embedding model: - `POST /v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and a JSONL file whose rows are `"url": "/v1/embeddings"` - `POST /v1/batches` referencing that file - Model configured as `vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001` (any `gemini-embedding-*`) ### Expected Each `/v1/embeddings` JSONL row should be translated into the Vertex AI embeddings batch-prediction shape, carrying the row's `body.input` text through to Vertex. ### Actual Every row — regardless of its `url` — is translated as if it were a **chat completions** request. `_openai_batch_jsonl_entries_to_vertex_wrapped_requests()` reads `body["messages"]`, which does not exist on an embeddings row, so it gets `[]`. The empty-messages defensive fallback then substitutes a single blank content block, and **the actual `input` text is discarded entirely.** Given this input row: ```json {"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}} ``` LiteLLM emits, verbatim: ```json {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-1", "litellm_custom_id_raw": "b32_ojsxcljr"}}} ``` `PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT` appears nowhere in the output. It has been replaced by `" "`. There are two independent defects visible in that one line: 1. **`input` is dropped.** The text to be embedded never reaches Vertex. 2. **The shape is wrong.** `contents`/`parts` is the `generateContent` (chat) shape. Vertex's embeddings batch request is `EmbedContentRequest`, which has **no `contents` field** — and no `labels` field either, so the `custom_id` smuggling would be the next failure even after fixing `contents`. The only runtime signal on LiteLLM's side is a `WARNING`-level log line (full text in §4), which explicitly says it is masking the problem rather than surfacing it: > `Setting an empty content to prevent an 400 error.` ### Downstream effect, and how the failure is masked Per the live Vertex AI runs documented in PR #35092 (real project in `us-central1`, real GCS bucket, no mocks), the malformed row is **rejected** by Vertex per-row: ```json {"custom_id": "req-1", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": "... EmbedContentRequest ... no such field: 'contents'"}} ``` The masking is at the **job** level: the enclosing batch still reports `"status": "completed"` with `"errors": null` even though every single row failed. So a caller polling `GET /v1/batches/<id>` and checking job status sees a clean success, and only discovers the total failure if they parse the output file row by row. ### Scope notes — what was and wasn't tested **Tested by me (reproduced, v1.89.1):** the transformation-level `input` drop, via a direct call into the vendored transformer. This needs no GCP credentials and is the repro in §3. I also confirmed the equivalent chat-completions row round-trips correctly, isolating the defect to the embeddings path rather than a general transformation failure. **Not tested by me:** I did **not** run this against live Vertex AI. The per-row `no such field: 'contents'` rejection and the `completed`/`errors: null` job-level masking described above are from PR #35092's live runs, not my own observation. I'm citing them rather than claiming them. **Confirmed unaffected — live/synchronous embeddings.** This is isolated to the managed-files batch path. Ordinary `/v1/embeddings` calls are fine, because they run through structurally separate code that never touches the batch-files transformer: - `vertex_ai/*` models → `vertex_embeddings/embedding_handler.py::VertexEmbedding.embedding()`, which calls `transform_openai_request_to_vertex_embedding_request(input=input, ...)` and POSTs directly to `:predict`. `input` flows straight through. - `gemini/*` models, and `vertex_ai/*` models flagged `uses_embed_content=True` → `gemini_embeddings/batch_embed_content_handler.py::GoogleBatchEmbeddings.batch_embeddings()`. (Despite the name this is synchronous `:batchEmbedContents` — batching several texts into one HTTP call — not the async `/v1/batches` job API.) `input` flows straight through here too. `grep -rn "GoogleBatchEmbeddings\|batch_embed_content_handler\|VertexEmbedding\b" litellm/proxy/ litellm/batches/ litellm/files/` returns zero matches, i.e. the batch/files route handlers never delegate to either live handler. This is consistent with the bug going unnoticed: people are using live embeddings successfully, and that says nothing about the batch path. ### Steps to Reproduce The defect is in a pure transformation function, so it reproduces with no proxy, no GCP project, and no credentials. **1. Install the affected version** ```bash pip install litellm==1.89.1 ``` **2. Run the embeddings row through the Vertex batch-files transformer** ```python import json from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.files.transformation import VertexAIJsonlFilesTransformation t = VertexAIJsonlFilesTransformation() row = { "custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}, } out = t._transform_openai_jsonl_content_to_vertex_ai_jsonl_content([row]) print("OUTPUT:", json.dumps(out[0])) print("SENTINEL PRESENT:", "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT" in json.dumps(out[0])) ``` **3. Observe** — a `WARNING` is logged, the output carries the chat `contents`/`parts` shape instead of an `EmbedContentRequest`, and the input text is gone: ``` OUTPUT: {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-1", "litellm_custom_id_raw": "b32_ojsxcljr"}}} SENTINEL PRESENT: False ``` - **Expected:** an `EmbedContentRequest`-shaped row containing `PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT`. - **Observed:** a `generateContent`-shaped row containing `" "`. `SENTINEL PRESENT: False`. **4. Control step — change only the row's `url` and `body` to the chat shape and repeat.** This isolates the cause to the embeddings path: ```python row = { "custom_id": "req-2", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": "gemini-2.0-flash-001", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}]}, } out = t._transform_openai_jsonl_content_to_vertex_ai_jsonl_content([row]) print("OUTPUT:", json.dumps(out[0])) print("SENTINEL PRESENT:", "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT" in json.dumps(out[0])) ``` Result — no warning, and the text survives: ``` OUTPUT: {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-2", "litellm_custom_id_raw": "b32_pe"}}} SENTINEL PRESENT: True ``` So the transformer is not broken in general — it silently mishandles exactly the rows whose `url` is `/v1/embeddings`. **5. (Optional) End-to-end through the proxy**, if you have a Vertex project. Config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gemini-embedding-001 litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-001 vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEX_PROJECT vertex_location: us-central1 ``` `batch_embeddings.jsonl`: ```json {"custom_id": "req-1", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": {"model": "gemini-embedding-001", "input": "hello world from litellm batch"}} ``` ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/files \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -F purpose=batch -F 'model=gemini-embedding-001' \ -F file=@batch_embeddings.jsonl # then POST /v1/batches with the returned file id ``` Per PR #35092's live runs the job reports `"status": "completed"` / `"errors": null` while every row in the output file carries the `no such field: 'contents'` error. --- ### Relevant log output ```shell # Step 2 above — the embeddings row. The warning is the ONLY runtime signal, and it # states outright that it is masking the problem instead of raising. 12:59:59 - LiteLLM:WARNING: transformation.py:1088 - No contents in messages. Contents are required. See https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.publishers.models/generateContent#request-body. If the original request did not comply to OpenAI API requirements it should have failed by now, but LiteLLM does not check for missing messages. Setting an empty content to prevent an 400 error. Relevant Issue - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/9733 # The emitted Vertex row. Note: shape is `contents`/`parts` (generateContent), NOT an # EmbedContentRequest; and the input text has become " ". EMBEDDINGS_ROW_OUTPUT: {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": " "}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-1", "litellm_custom_id_raw": "b32_ojsxcljr"}}} SENTINEL_PRESENT: False # Control: the same transformer on a /v1/chat/completions row. No warning, text preserved. CHAT_ROW_OUTPUT: {"request": {"contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}]}], "labels": {"litellm_custom_id": "req-2", "litellm_custom_id_raw": "b32_pe"}}} SENTINEL_PRESENT: True # Downstream, from PR #35092's live Vertex AI runs (NOT observed by me): the malformed # row is rejected per-row, while the enclosing batch still reports success. {"custom_id": "req-1", "response": null, "error": {"code": "vertex_ai_error", "message": "... EmbedContentRequest ... no such field: 'contents'"}} # ...yet: GET /v1/batches/<id> -> "status": "completed", "errors": null ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.89.1 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
