signal.title: fix(cost): tiered pricing supports cache creation cost and is all-or-nothing
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Pricing schema rejected `cache_creation_input_token_cost` inside tiers - Cache-creation tokens were never billed at tier rates - Dashscope tiers were billed graduated, not all-or-nothing - Tiered-only models (volcengine) were billed at $0 - `tiered_pricing` under a router deployment's `litellm_params` was silently ignored - Reasoning tokens ignored the tier's reasoning rate on the generic path - With tiers now effective, a PTU deployment carrying `tiered_pricing` would bill per token on top of its reserved-capacity flat cost - Tier tables that publish only input-side rates billed completion tokens at $0, both cost-map entries and proxy deployments whose custom tiers omit output rates How it solves it: - Schema generator and committed schema accept the tier field - Tier selection now happens once, from total input tokens - Selected tier prices text, cached, cache-creation, output, reasoning - Generic cost path resolves tiered rates for any provider - Deployment mirror copies `tiered_pricing` onto model_info so custom-pricing detection fires - Generic path and cost breakdown bill reasoning tokens at the selected tier's `output_cost_per_reasoning_token` - PTU deployments refuse supplied `tiered_pricing` with the same 400 as flat rates and store tiers already on the row as an empty list, so the cost map's tier table cannot back-fill them - A tier without an output rate bills completions at the model's own output rate (reasoning tokens at the model's own reasoning rate), and a deployment entry whose tiers omit one inherits that rate from its backend model at registration; an explicit zero rate in a tier or on a model is honored as free, and a backend rate that get_model_info synthesizes as zero is never inherited ## User Flow Before: someone running a Qwen deployment with prompt caching gets undercharged and inconsistently charged, and the pricing entry they need cannot even be loaded 1. They add a model entry whose `tiered_pricing` tier carries `cache_creation_input_token_cost` and the entry fails schema validation, so the rate cannot be expressed at all 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Dashscope model with a 300K-token prompt 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows spend computed by slicing the prompt across two tiers, first 256K at the cheap rate and the rest at the expensive one, which is below what the provider invoices 4. They send the same request with a cache write and the cache-creation tokens are billed at the plain input rate, so the log again understates spend 5. They point a key at a volcengine doubao-seed-2.0 deployment, which only publishes tiered rates, and every request logs at $0 spend 6. They set `tiered_pricing` under a deployment's `litellm_params` in the proxy config and every request on it still logs at the base model-map rate, ignoring their tiers entirely 7. They send a reasoning request to a Qwen model whose tier publishes a separate `output_cost_per_reasoning_token` and the log bills those tokens at the tier's plain output rate 8. An admin whose deployment carries `tiered_pricing` adds PTU config via PATCH https://litellm-domain/model/{model_id}/update, and with tiers now effective every request would keep logging per-token tier spend on top of the flat PTU cost 9. They send a request to a model whose cost-map tier table publishes only input-side rates and every completion token bills at $0; a proxy deployment whose custom `tiered_pricing` declares only input rates serves completions free the same way After: the same requests log the amount the provider actually invoices 1. The same model entry with `cache_creation_input_token_cost` inside a tier loads successfully 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Dashscope model with a 300K-token prompt 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the whole request billed at the 256K-1M tier rate, matching the published all-or-nothing table 4. The same request with a cache write bills those tokens at that tier's cache-creation rate, falling back to the tier's input rate when the tier does not publish one 5. The volcengine doubao-seed-2.0 request now logs non-zero spend at the tier its input size lands in 6. The deployment with `tiered_pricing` under `litellm_params` bills every request at the configured tier rates on /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, and /v1/responses 7. The reasoning request bills reasoning tokens at the tier's `output_cost_per_reasoning_token` and the rest of the completion at the tier's output rate 8. That update stores the tiers as an empty list so requests on the PTU deployment log $0 per-token spend (removing the PTU config restores tier billing), and sending `tiered_pricing` together with PTU config is refused with a 400 like any other rate 9. Those completion tokens bill at the model's own output rate while the tier keeps pricing the input side, and the input-only-tier deployment bills completions at its backend model's public rate ## Relevant issues Fixes #28844 Supersedes the approach in #28047 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4375 Resolves LIT-4376 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, real Anthropic spend, same config on both legs: a `qwen-tiered-sim` deployment (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`) with two-tier `tiered_pricing` under `litellm_params`, exercising the same generic cost path dashscope map entries ride, plus a `qwen-tiered-noout` deployment whose tiers publish only input rates ```yaml model_list: - model_name: qwen-tiered-sim litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY tiered_pricing: - range: [0, 3000] input_cost_per_token: 3.25e-7 output_cost_per_token: 1.95e-6 cache_creation_input_token_cost: 4.063e-7 cache_read_input_token_cost: 3.25e-8 - range: [3000, 128000] input_cost_per_token: 6.5e-7 output_cost_per_token: 3.9e-6 cache_creation_input_token_cost: 8.125e-7 cache_read_input_token_cost: 6.5e-8 - model_name: qwen-tiered-noout litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY tiered_pricing: - range: [0, 3000] input_cost_per_token: 3.25e-7 - range: [3000, 128000] input_cost_per_token: 8.125e-7 general_settings: master_key: sk-qa-tiered-1234 ``` Cache-write request used on both legs (cache-read leg repeats it, small-prompt leg sends a 21-token user message): ```bash BIG=$(python3 -c 'print(" ".join(f"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog number {i}." for i in range(400)))') curl -sD - http://localhost:<port>/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-tiered-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"qwen-tiered-sim\",\"max_tokens\":20,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"$BIG\",\"cache_control\":{\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}}]},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Reply with the single word: ok\"}]}" ``` **Before, merge base `3b5317c40d`**: every request billed at the base model-map rates, tiers ignored entirely | Scenario | Usage | Observed header | Tier-correct value | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---| | chat cache write | text 13, creation 6502, out 4 | 0.0081605 | 0.005306925 | FAIL | | chat cache read | text 13, cached 6502, out 4 | 0.0006832 | 0.00044668 | FAIL | | /v1/messages cache read | text 13, cached 6502, out 4 | 0.0006832 | 0.00044668 | FAIL | | /v1/responses 5415 in | input 5415, out 4 | 0.005435 | 0.00353535 | FAIL | | chat small prompt | input 21, out 20 | 0.000121 | 0.000045825 | FAIL | The before numbers reconstruct exactly from claude-haiku-4-5 base rates (e.g. cache write: 13\*1e-6 + 6502\*1.25e-6 + 4\*5e-6 = 0.0081605), proving `tiered_pricing` was dead config **After, head `18752c860c`**: every `x-litellm-response-cost` header matches the tier math computed from that response's own usage to within 1e-9. The zero-rate row's deployment was created via `POST /model/new` with an explicit `"cache_creation_input_token_cost": 0` in its tier | Scenario | Tier | Observed header | Expected | Spend log | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | chat cache write (creation 5601) | 2 | 0.0045748625 | 0.0045748625 | matches (rerun: 0.00458055) | PASS | | chat cache read (cached 5601) | 2 | 0.000388115 | 0.000388115 | n/a | PASS | | /v1/messages cache read | 2 | 0.000388115 | 0.000388115 | n/a | PASS | | /v1/responses 5265 in | 2 | 0.00343785 | 0.00343785 | n/a | PASS | | chat small prompt (21 in) | 1 | 1.4625e-05 | 1.4625e-05 | 1.4625e-05 | PASS | | qwen-tiered-noout (21 in, 4 out) | 1 | 2.6825e-05 | 2.6825e-05 | 2.6825e-05 | PASS | | zero-rate cache write (creation 5616) | 1 | 1.2025e-05 | 1.2025e-05 | 1.2025e-05 | PASS | Key proofs from the after leg - Cache-creation rate: 13\*6.5e-7 + 5601\*8.125e-7 + 4\*3.9e-6 = 0.0045748625 observed; billing creation tokens at the tier's input rate would give 0.0036647, so the dedicated `cache_creation_input_token_cost` is what's applied - All-or-nothing: the 5265-token /v1/responses request bills entirely at tier 2 (a graduated split would give 0.001718925), and the 21-token request bills entirely at tier 1 (tier 2 would give 2.925e-05) - Input-only tiers: the qwen-tiered-noout request bills 21\*3.25e-7 + 4\*5e-6 = 2.6825e-05, the tier input rate plus the backend model's public output rate; at pre-fix commit `c3e38a0b52` the same request billed 6.825e-06, input only, completions free - Explicit zero rate: the zero-rate deployment bills 13\*3.25e-7 + 4\*1.95e-6 + 5616\*0 = 1.2025e-05, honoring the tier's `cache_creation_input_token_cost: 0` instead of the input-rate fallback, which would have billed 0.001837225 - `GET /spend/logs?request_id=<response id>` equals the header to the digit for the cache-write, small-prompt, and input-only-tier scenarios, so the persisted spend matches what the client saw **PTU interplay, head `18752c860c`**: DB-backed proxy with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=true`, driven through the management API | Scenario | Check | Result | Verdict | |---|---|---|---| | POST /model/new, tiers + PTU | HTTP status | 400 naming tiered_pricing | PASS | | tiered deployment, no PTU yet | cost header | 1.4625e-05 (tier 1) | PASS | | PATCH /model/{id}/update adds PTU | stored blobs | tiered_pricing [], rates 0.0 | PASS | | same completion after PTU | header, spend log | 0.0, 0.0 (fresh process) | PASS | | PATCH releases PTU | stored blobs | tiers and zeroed rates dropped | PASS | | same completion after release | cost header | 4.1e-05, public map rates (fresh process) | PASS | ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Tiered rates now apply on the generic path for all providers - Volcengine doubao-seed-2.0 spend changes from $0 to real - Tier boundaries are exclusive at the start, inclusive at the end - `tiered_pricing` works in a deployment's `litellm_params` or `model_info`; passing it as a raw SDK completion kwarg is still unsupported - Legacy POST /model/update still ignores model_info patches; untouched here - register_model's additive merge keeps stale tiers until restart; untouched here - Toggling PTU on then off drops the operator's tier table; billing falls back to the cost-map rates until tiers are re-added - An explicit zero rate inside a tier or on a model entry bills that token type free instead of falling back to another rate ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/61c1a67073dd4a10973334cdfb1224c2 Requested by: @mateo-berri

signal.title: chore(release): backport 11 staging PRs onto patch-1.92.0rc2 for the 1.92.0 stable cut
signal.text: ## Relevant issues This backports eleven already-merged `litellm_internal_staging` PRs onto `patch-1.92.0rc2` (the branch cut at the `v1.92.0-rc.2` tag) so they ride the pending `1.92.0` stable release. Seven were requested for the release; the other four are prerequisites those seven need to compile and pass their own tests on this older line, without which the requested picks would be dead on arrival. No version bump: the branch's `pyproject.toml` already holds the final `1.92.0`, and `v1.92.0` has not shipped anywhere yet (no DockerHub/GHCR image, no git tag, no `release/v1.92.0` branch), so the picks ride the pending version rather than bumping it. This matches the rc1 -> rc2 backport, which was also bump-less. ## Linear ticket ## What is included (staging merge order) Requested for the release - #32542 fix(guardrails): walk Responses-API text taxonomy in shared content helpers - #32578 fix(bedrock): keep mid-conversation system messages in place for Claude Invoke - #32655 feat(otel): emit the gen_ai.client.operation.exception event on failed LLM calls - #32831 fix(bedrock): gate in-place system role messages on model support for Claude Invoke - #32882 fix(bedrock): flag mapped Claude 4.8+ entries with supports_mid_conversation_system - #32873 refactor(fallback-generalizations): split rules into routing and provider-neutral capability kinds - #32874 fix(anthropic): thread real provider through capability probes instead of pinning anthropic Prerequisites (required for the above to work on this line; each is itself a merged staging PR) - #32389 fix(utils): resolve bedrock regional inference profiles to regional pricing in get_model_info; #32873's cost-ladder test fails without it (regional ids fall back to bare pricing) - #32701 feat: add Meta Model API provider and muse-spark-1.1; #32874 patches a class this PR introduces (JSONProviderAnthropicMessagesConfig) - #32867 fix(anthropic): translate adaptive thinking/effort to pre-4.6 model support; #32874 modifies a method this PR introduces (_translate_adaptive_effort_for_non_adaptive_model) - #32739 test: add /v1/messages to supported_endpoints schema enum; follow-up of #32701 that keeps the model-cost JSON schema canary green once muse-spark advertises /v1/messages Every commit is a `git cherry-pick -x` of the corresponding staging squash/merge; there is no hand-written code and no version-bump, lock, or UI-artifact commit (no production `.tsx` is touched). ## Adaptation notes Four picks diverge from their staging source; the rest are byte-for-byte (patch-id verbatim). - #32701: the new `test_meta_provider.py` shipped without a local-cost-map fixture, so its four muse-spark model-info tests passed only when an earlier test happened to leave the bundled cost map in `litellm.model_cost`; run in isolation they failed because `muse-spark-1.1` is a day-0 model not yet on the remote `main` map. Added the same `local_model_cost_map` fixture that sibling day-0 model tests use, pinning the bundled map for those four tests. This is a determinism fix, not a behavior change; the provider code itself is unchanged and correct. - #32882: the staging diff flags eleven Claude 4.8+ cost-map entries; this line does not carry `jp.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` (added to staging by a PR outside this set), so that one entry is skipped and the other ten are flagged. Behavior is preserved because #32831's `bedrock-anthropic-claude-mid-conversation-system` fallback rule still flags unmapped Claude 4.8+ ids, including the jp variant. Its parametrized tests that name `jp.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` resolve through that rule and pass. - #32873: the `basedpyright-code-budget.json` / `type-discipline-budget.json` ratchets from the staging diff are dropped; this line keeps its own ceilings. Staging's lowered limits were computed against staging's full tree, not this subset, so importing them could produce a too-tight gate. The functional refactor (utils.py, fallback_generalizations.py, model-cost JSON) is applied verbatim. - #32874: the two touched test files had diverged far enough on this line that the three-way merge swept in neighbor tests belonging to unrelated staging PRs (`TestDefaultSuffixAdaptiveThinking`, the LIT-3393 beta-headers fixture). Those were excluded; only #32874's own additions were kept (`TestCapabilityProbeUsesCallerProvider`, `test_bedrock_messages_thinking_shape_follows_exact_bedrock_entry_flag`) plus the required `_is_adaptive_thinking_model(model)` -> `(model, "anthropic")` signature migration on the seven existing call sites this line does have. Every source caller of the changed signatures is updated, so no existing caller breaks. ## Known noise on this line - `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/credential_migration.py` is not formatted to the line's `ruff format` gate on `patch-1.92.0rc2` itself; no pick touches it, so a red `format-check` on that file is pre-existing and not introduced here. - The default `proxy_config.yaml` points caching at a placeholder `redis.example.com`, so the proxy log shows a Redis connection error at boot. Unrelated to these changes. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests (carried by the picks; validated as a delta against a clean pre-pick baseline) - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on the picked code (per-worktree proxy at `localhost:4001`), real Anthropic API call, no mocks: ``` $ curl -s "http://localhost:4001/health/liveliness" "I'm alive!" $ curl -s "http://localhost:4001/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly the word: backported"}],"max_tokens":20}' content: backported model: claude-haiku-4-5 usage: {'completion_tokens': 5, 'prompt_tokens': 15, 'total_tokens': 20, ...} ``` The proxy boots on the picked code (40 models registered, including the #32701 provider path and #32874's rewritten anthropic transformation), then serves a real completion end to end. Targeted-test delta: the pre-pick baseline was clean (591 passed, 0 failures across the pre-existing touched test files); after the picks the full targeted set is green at 1163 passed, 0 failures. Each pick's own tests pass, so each delivers its claim on this line, and there are zero new failures versus the baseline. Behavioral gauntlet (universal, standard depth): the two regression-relevant sub-claims held, symbol closure (every identifier the picks reference resolves) SURVIVED and no-existing-caller-broken SURVIVED. The run flagged that #32701's day-0 muse-spark tests passed only with the bundled cost map in place; the strongest dissent confirmed the provider code is correct and the gap was a missing test fixture. That fixture was added (see adaptation notes), after which every touched test file passes in isolation with no env var forced, a full per-file fragility sweep run to confirm nothing else was order-dependent. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Eleven cherry-picks onto `patch-1.92.0rc2` in staging merge order, no version bump, three picks adapted as noted above, everything else verbatim.

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): convert messages to contents in gemini count_tokens
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `litellm.acount_tokens()` returns `total_tokens=0` with `error=False` for any `vertex_ai/gemini-*` model when called with `messages` - The Gemini branch of `VertexAITokenCounter.count_tokens` never converts `messages` to Gemini `contents`, so the request body is `{"contents": null}` - Vertex accepts that with HTTP 200 and no `totalTokens` field, and the old code read `result.get("totalTokens", 0)` as a valid zero How it solves it: - Converts `messages` to Gemini `contents` via the existing `_gemini_convert_messages_with_history` helper when `contents` is `None` - Treats a response without `totalTokens` as a failure (returns `None`) so the caller falls back to local token counting ## User Flow Before: a developer calling `acount_tokens` with `messages` on a Vertex Gemini model gets a silent zero, so their pre-flight context-window guard always passes and overflows surface later as a provider 400 1. They call `await litellm.acount_tokens(model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])` 2. The SDK returns `TokenCountResponse(total_tokens=0, tokenizer_type="", error=False)` 3. Their guard checks `total_tokens < max_tokens`, passes, and sends the real request 4. Vertex rejects the real request with a 400 because the context window is actually exceeded After: the same call returns the real token count from Vertex, or falls back to local counting 1. They call `await litellm.acount_tokens(model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}])` 2. The SDK converts `messages` to Gemini `contents` format and sends `{"contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "Hello"}]}]}` to Vertex 3. Vertex returns `{"totalTokens": 3}` and the SDK returns `TokenCountResponse(total_tokens=3, tokenizer_type="gemini")` 4. Their guard correctly compares the real count against the context window ## Relevant issues Fixes #36921 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Will add curl-based proof against a live Vertex AI endpoint shortly. Unit tests verify the message-to-contents conversion and the no-totalTokens failure path: ``` python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py -k "count_tokens or token_counter" -v tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_converts_messages_to_contents_for_gemini PASSED tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_returns_none_when_api_omits_total_tokens PASSED tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_routes_gemini_models PASSED tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_routes_partner_models PASSED tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/test_vertex_ai_common_utils.py::test_vertex_ai_token_counter_uses_count_tokens_location PASSED 5 passed ``` ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `system` and `tools` parameters are still dropped on the Vertex Gemini count_tokens path. The issue mentions this as lower priority. Follow-up PR can address it - The local tiktoken fallback has no Gemini tokenizer, so the fallback is approximate for Gemini. Also noted in the issue as lower priority ## QA runbook

signal.title: fix(proxy): requeue spend logs when the DB write fails with a transport error
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A DB outage silently loses every queued spend log - Prisma's P1001 masquerade escaped the retry clause entirely - Failed batches were dropped, never put back on the queue How it solves it: - Classify failures with the existing transport-error helper - Requeue the batch at the head after retries exhaust - Route every enqueue and dequeue, producer appends included, through one pair that holds the queue under a byte budget so a long outage cannot OOM the pod ## User Flow Before: an admin whose primary database goes down keeps serving traffic, then finds no usage recorded for the outage window 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions repeatedly while the primary database is unreachable 2. Every request returns 200 with a normal completion, so the app is unaffected 3. The proxy logs `Error in spend logs queue monitor: Can't reach database server ... :5432 (P1001)` 4. The database comes back and they open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs filtered to the outage window 5. Nothing is there, and GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs returns no entries for those requests, so that spend is billed to nobody After: the same outage delays the records instead of losing them 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions repeatedly while the primary database is unreachable 2. Every request returns 200 with a normal completion, so the app is unaffected 3. The proxy logs the connection failure once per retry, saying how many logs are held back 4. The database comes back and they open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs filtered to the outage window 5. Every request from the outage is there with its real spend, and GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs returns all of them ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5475 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on localhost:4000 with a real Postgres and real Anthropic calls (`anthropic-haiku-4-5`, real spend). The outage is a `service postgresql stop` while traffic keeps flowing, exactly the controlled validation the customer ran. Same script for both runs, tagging the six requests with a unique `user` so the rows can be counted afterwards: ```bash PROBE="outage-probe-$(date +%s)" sudo service postgresql stop for i in $(seq 1 6); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "request $i -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" -m 60 http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"anthropic-haiku-4-5\",\"max_tokens\":8,\"user\":\"$PROBE\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"say hi $i\"}]}" done sleep 90 # flush job runs against the dead DB sudo service postgresql start sleep 90 # next flush after recovery PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h localhost -U postgres -d litellm -c \ "select count(*) from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" where end_user = '$PROBE';" ``` Before, at 3b5317c40d (this branch's merge base): ``` request 1 -> HTTP 200 request 2 -> HTTP 200 request 3 -> HTTP 200 request 4 -> HTTP 200 request 5 -> HTTP 200 request 6 -> HTTP 200 count ------- 0 (1 row) ``` After, at ebaaeaba0c (fix commit; later commits only change how the queue is bounded and a stale test import): ``` request 1 -> HTTP 200 request 2 -> HTTP 200 request 3 -> HTTP 200 request 4 -> HTTP 200 request 5 -> HTTP 200 request 6 -> HTTP 200 count ------- 6 (1 row) ``` Proxy log from the after run showing the batch surviving the outage and being retried rather than dropped: ``` 00:21:38 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: utils.py:5583 - Spend tracking - DB connection error writing spend logs, retry 1/3. logs_count=6, error=All connection attempts failed 00:21:45 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: utils.py:5583 - Spend tracking - DB connection error writing spend logs, retry 4/3. logs_count=6, error=All connection attempts failed ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Requeued rows flush out of chronological order - Queue is bounded at a fixed 64 MB, not a row count - Guardrail usage tracking still skips a failed batch Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5a90b9cf2ca84ee4ac762ffeaa0fe93f

signal.title: fix(anthropic): populate inference_geo from the request so regional pricing applies
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streamed Anthropic usage loses the region it was served from - Regional traffic then gets billed at global rates How it solves it: - Streaming reassembly carries `inference_geo` through - Requested region is the fallback when the response omits it ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming Anthropic traffic out of a US region sees the gateway log no region at all, so regional pricing never applies to any streamed request 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true` 2. The response streams back fine, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at the global price with no region recorded 3. They repeat it on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages with `"stream": true`, and both log the same way 4. Dropping `"stream": true` on any of the three routes does record `us`, so their spend is only correct for non-streaming traffic After: the same streamed requests record the region, so streamed and non-streamed traffic price the same way 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true` 2. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows the request served from `us` 3. The same holds on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and POST https://litellm-domain/anthropic/v1/messages with `"stream": true` 4. A request that asks for no region, or that Anthropic serves globally, still records `global` and prices as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4867 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Screen recording of the before and after run, in one video, is in [this Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1786414063855749?thread_ts=1786408619.329699&cid=C0BE49SAUE6). It captured the before at `1d3b64c66f` (current `litellm_internal_staging`) and the after at `82a64de9a2`, and reproduced the runs below Live proxy against the real Anthropic API, real spend, `claude-opus-4-8`, one request per route with `"inference_geo": "us"` and `"stream": true`. Region and cost were read off the standard logging payload ```bash H=(-H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01') curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions "${H[@]}" -d @chat_geo_stream.json curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d @msg_geo_stream.json curl -sS localhost:4000/anthropic/v1/messages "${H[@]}" -d @pt_geo_stream.json ``` Before, at `1d3b64c66f`, every streamed route drops the region: ``` route=acompletion geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 route=anthropic_messages geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 route=pass_through_endpoint geo=None cost=0.14798499999999998 ``` After, at `82a64de9a2`, all three keep it: ``` route=acompletion geo=us cost=0.14788949999999998 route=anthropic_messages geo=us cost=0.14788949999999998 route=pass_through_endpoint geo=us cost=0.14799949999999998 ``` The cost barely moves because the uplift itself is #34850, and the point here is that without the region reaching cost calculation that PR can never fire on streamed traffic. The same three routes without `"stream": true` already recorded `us` before this change, on this branch they still do ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Merged with `litellm_internal_staging`, absorbing the #36447 speed plumbing - Cache tokens still miss the geo uplift until #34850 lands ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/13d7b3dbf5a641f0a24aa0b48893d315 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit d88193eea52b0095df6bb61d83179608497c9350. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(bedrock): forward provider response headers on chat completions
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock responses dropped `x-amzn-requestid` on `/chat/completions` - Broke request correlation with AWS when debugging - Affected converse (both modes) and invoke streaming How it solves it: - Converse non-streaming now surfaces the provider's headers - Converse and invoke streaming carry them to the caller - Generic HTTP streaming path forwards them too ## User Flow Before: a developer debugging a slow Bedrock deployment can't get the AWS request id back out of the gateway, so AWS support has nothing to look up 1. The proxy admin sets `return_response_headers: true` and points a model at `bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model and reads the response headers 3. The response is 200 with a normal completion, but carries no `llm_provider-*` headers at all, so there is no AWS request id to hand to support 4. Same thing with `"stream": true`, and same thing again for a `bedrock/invoke/...` model with `"stream": true` After: the same requests come back with the AWS request id in the response headers 1. The proxy admin sets `return_response_headers: true` and points a model at `bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model and reads the response headers 3. The response now includes `llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: 836b894b-b89a-40e2-8522-532c4e71f882`, which they can quote verbatim to AWS support 4. Same for `"stream": true`, and for `bedrock/invoke/...` in both streaming and non-streaming, which also exposes the `x-amzn-bedrock-*` token and latency headers ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5145 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy against real bedrock-runtime us-east-1 and real Anthropic (claude-haiku-4-5, real spend), `litellm_settings: return_response_headers: true` ```bash # for each of: bedrock-converse-haiku-4-5 (bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0), # bedrock-invoke-haiku-4-5 (bedrock/invoke/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0), # anthropic-haiku-4-5 (anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) # and for each of stream=false, stream=true: curl -s -D /tmp/h.txt -o /tmp/b.txt -X POST localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"MODEL","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"max_tokens":16,"stream":STREAM}' grep -i "^llm_provider" /tmp/h.txt || echo " (NONE)" ``` Before, at `1a183efaa1` (base): ```text == BEDROCK CONVERSE non-streaming (NONE) == BEDROCK CONVERSE streaming (NONE) == BEDROCK INVOKE non-streaming llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: 198e5fda-7d53-45f8-ac22-88e42d9f4a5c == BEDROCK INVOKE streaming (NONE) == ANTHROPIC baseline non-stream llm_provider-request-id: req_011Ce3m... == ANTHROPIC baseline streaming llm_provider-request-id: req_011Ce3m... ``` After, at `9c922f4aa4`: ```text == BEDROCK CONVERSE non-streaming llm_provider-date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 02:48:57 GMT llm_provider-content-type: application/json llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: 836b894b-b89a-40e2-8522-532c4e71f882 == BEDROCK CONVERSE streaming llm_provider-content-type: application/vnd.amazon.eventstream llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: 73fcf3fe-13d0-41cf-9368-e120c4d741a4 == BEDROCK INVOKE non-streaming llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: f2d37bbb-7413-4927-9105-86eef40587e5 llm_provider-x-amzn-bedrock-invocation-latency: 717 llm_provider-x-amzn-bedrock-output-token-count: 16 llm_provider-x-amzn-bedrock-input-token-count: 9 == BEDROCK INVOKE streaming llm_provider-content-type: application/vnd.amazon.eventstream llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: d424e810-9c73-4f22-b2df-4d4306694eda llm_provider-x-amzn-bedrock-content-type: application/json == ANTHROPIC baseline non-stream llm_provider-request-id: req_011Ce3mkgiRLu5WtvZdoM3PM llm_provider-anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining: 9999 == ANTHROPIC baseline streaming llm_provider-request-id: req_011Ce3mkjmiskvQcvh2fUmYa llm_provider-anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining: 9999 ``` Regression tests kill the mutation: reverting only the `litellm/` changes fails all three new tests, and they pass with the fix ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Invoke streaming now builds its stream eagerly, not lazily ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/698b5dfc69ee439e810c80a77a5e35d7

signal.title: [Bug]: /v1/responses guardrail-blocked replies report zero token usage despite real upstream consumption
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a post-call guardrail blocks a response on `/v1/responses`, the proxy returns a 200 with the violation message and a usage object that is hardcoded to all zeros, even though the upstream LLM call completed and consumed real tokens. The same guardrail block on `/v1/chat/completions` (and `/v1/messages`) reports the real token usage the blocked upstream call consumed This matters because a guardrail-blocked call still costs real money upstream, and the response body is the only place the caller can learn that: the blocked request is logged on the failure path with 0 tokens and $0 spend, so any client-side token accounting built on response bodies silently undercounts every blocked `/v1/responses` call. Callers who reconcile their own per-request token counts against provider bills see an unexplained gap that grows with guardrail activity Expected: the `/v1/responses` blocked reply carries the real `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, and `total_tokens` the upstream call consumed, exactly like the `/v1/chat/completions` blocked reply already does (zeros remain correct for pre-call blocks, where no upstream call ever happened) ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app tracks per-request token spend from response bodies gets zeros for every guardrail-blocked Responses API call, so their accounting drifts under what the provider bills 1. Their platform team runs a LiteLLM proxy with a post-call guardrail (content policy) enabled by default 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "..."}` and the reply trips the guardrail 3. They get a 200 whose output text is the violation message and whose usage reads `"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0`, so their app records zero consumption for a call the provider billed 4. A teammate sends the same prompt as POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions, gets the same violation message with `finish_reason: "content_filter"`, but their usage shows the real counts, so the two apps' dashboards disagree about identical traffic 5. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs the blocked request shows 0 tokens and $0 spend, so nothing in the gateway lets the developer recover the real number After a (hypothetical) fix: the same blocked call reports the tokens it really consumed, so body-based accounting matches across endpoints 1. Their platform team runs a LiteLLM proxy with a post-call guardrail (content policy) enabled by default 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "..."}` and the reply trips the guardrail 3. They get a 200 whose output text is the violation message and whose usage carries the real counts, e.g. `"input_tokens": 14, "output_tokens": 20, "total_tokens": 34` 4. The teammate's POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions shows the same real counts for the same prompt, so both dashboards agree 5. Pre-call blocks (prompt never reached the provider) still report zero usage on both endpoints ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (`c17_repro_config.yaml`), using a minimal post-call guardrail that blocks every response the way any content policy guardrail would: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY guardrails: - guardrail_name: zero-usage-repro litellm_params: guardrail: c17_zero_usage_guardrail.ZeroUsageReproGuardrail mode: post_call default_on: true general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 litellm_settings: drop_params: true ``` `c17_zero_usage_guardrail.py`, mirroring how in-tree post-call guardrails (e.g. Straiker) raise their block with the original response attached: ```python from litellm.exceptions import ModifyResponseException from litellm.integrations.custom_guardrail import CustomGuardrail from litellm.proxy._types import UserAPIKeyAuth class ZeroUsageReproGuardrail(CustomGuardrail): async def async_post_call_success_hook( self, data: dict, user_api_key_dict: UserAPIKeyAuth, response, ): raise ModifyResponseException( message="Content flagged by policy, response withheld", model=data.get("model", "unknown") or "unknown", request_data=data, guardrail_name=self.guardrail_name or "zero-usage-repro", original_response=response, ) ``` Version: commit 9d069f21dc on litellm_internal_staging, proxy booted with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config c17_repro_config.yaml --port 41893 --detailed_debug`, real OpenAI API key, real provider calls Same prompt through both endpoints: ``` $ curl -sS http://localhost:41893/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a haiku about token accounting"}]}' ``` returns the block with the real usage the upstream call consumed: ```json { "id": "chatcmpl-66663aed-a8c6-4c2d-97cd-9eff02f7e001", "choices": [{"message": {"content": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld"}, "finish_reason": "content_filter"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 14, "completion_tokens": 18, "total_tokens": 32} } ``` ``` $ curl -sS http://localhost:41893/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"Write a haiku about token accounting"}' ``` returns the block with usage zeroed: ```json { "id": "resp_a87a5e6a-60ae-47c3-8602-59347a4b9ca2", "output": [{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld"}]}], "status": "completed", "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_details": null, "output_tokens": 0, "output_tokens_details": null, "total_tokens": 0} } ``` The proxy's own `--detailed_debug` log proves the blocked `/v1/responses` upstream call really consumed tokens. The RAW RESPONSE for it (upstream id `resp_00b30e92cd26f454006a7e8dc088d08198b9f384df52662262`) ends with: ```json "usage": { "input_tokens": 14, "input_tokens_details": {"cache_write_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": 20, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": 34 } ``` And the spend log rows for both blocked requests (GET /spend/logs/ui) show `prompt_tokens: 0, completion_tokens: 0, spend: 0.0` with an empty usage object, confirming the response body was the caller's only chance to see the real consumption ### What a fix PR should look like `litellm/proxy/response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py` catches `ModifyResponseException` and builds the synthetic blocked reply with `usage=ResponseAPIUsage(input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0, total_tokens=0)`, never reading `e.original_response`. That field exists exactly for this: the chat completions handler in `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` passes it through `_blocked_response_usage`, whose docstring spells out the contract (report the real usage the upstream call consumed, zero only for pre-call blocks), and `litellm/proxy/anthropic_endpoints/endpoints.py` does the same for `/v1/messages` The fix is to derive the `ResponseAPIUsage` from `e.original_response` in that handler: when the original response is a `ResponsesAPIResponse` its usage can be lifted directly, and when it is a chat `ModelResponse` (bridged calls) the `Usage` fields map as prompt_tokens -> input_tokens and completion_tokens -> output_tokens, falling back to zeros when `original_response` is `None` (pre-call block). Worth extracting a shared helper next to `_blocked_response_usage` rather than a third hand-rolled mapping Two adjacent gaps worth closing in the same PR so the fix actually reaches all guardrails: `raise_passthrough_exception` in `litellm/integrations/custom_guardrail.py` and the guardrail pipeline raiser in `litellm/proxy/utils.py` both raise `ModifyResponseException` without attaching `original_response`, so blocks raised through them zero out usage on every endpoint even where the handler is correct Regression test: extend the mapped test file for `response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py` with a post-call guardrail block carrying a known usage on `original_response` and assert the returned body's usage matches it, plus a pre-call block asserting zeros ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? commit 9d069f21dc (litellm_internal_staging) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix: report real token usage on guardrail-blocked /v1/responses replies
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Guardrail-blocked /v1/responses replies always reported zero token usage - The upstream LLM call had already consumed real tokens - /v1/chat/completions and /v1/messages already report real counts on blocks How it solves it: - Shared blocked-usage helper now builds the /v1/responses usage object - Lives next to the existing /v1/messages helper in guardrail_translation utils - Maps bridged chat prompt/completion tokens to input/output tokens - Post-call guardrails can attach the blocked response via raise_passthrough_exception - Pre-call blocks still report zeros since no upstream call was made ## User Flow Before: a developer whose app tracks per-request token spend from response bodies gets zeros for every guardrail-blocked Responses API call 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "..."}` and the reply trips a post-call guardrail 2. They receive a 200 whose `usage` reads `"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0` 3. Their cost dashboard records that request at zero spend despite a real upstream call After: the same blocked call reports the real token counts 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses and the reply trips the same post-call guardrail 2. They receive a 200 whose `usage` now carries the real counts, e.g. `"input_tokens": 12, "output_tokens": 8, "total_tokens": 20` 3. Their cost dashboard records the request at its real token consumption ## Relevant issues Fixes #36880 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5615 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, real OpenAI and Anthropic calls, no mocks. Both legs boot the same config: a `post_call` custom guardrail that is `default_on` and raises `ModifyResponseException` with the blocked response attached, one native model (openai/gpt-4o-mini) and one chat-bridged model (anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5). Before runs at the merge base `2d3c3e3098`, after at this PR's head `e06e2e6c12`. Every call returns 200 carrying the guardrail's blocked message instead of a model reply; only the reported usage differs | Route | Model | Before `2d3c3e3098` | After `e06e2e6c12` | |---|---|---|---| | /v1/responses | gpt-4o-mini | 0 / 0 / 0 | 12 / 8 / 20 | | /v1/responses | claude-haiku-4-5 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 12 / 10 / 22 | | /v1/messages | claude-haiku-4-5 | 12 in, 10 out | 12 in, 10 out | | /v1/chat/completions | gpt-4o-mini | 12 / 7 / 19 | 12 / 7 / 19 | <details> <summary>Repro setup (config.yaml and the guardrail module)</summary> ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY guardrails: - guardrail_name: zero-usage-repro litellm_params: guardrail: c17_zero_usage_guardrail.ZeroUsageReproGuardrail mode: post_call default_on: true general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 litellm_settings: drop_params: true ``` ```python from litellm.exceptions import ModifyResponseException from litellm.integrations.custom_guardrail import CustomGuardrail from litellm.proxy._types import UserAPIKeyAuth class ZeroUsageReproGuardrail(CustomGuardrail): async def async_post_call_success_hook( self, data: dict, user_api_key_dict: UserAPIKeyAuth, response, ): raise ModifyResponseException( message="Content flagged by policy, response withheld", model=data.get("model", "unknown") or "unknown", request_data=data, guardrail_name=self.guardrail_name or "zero-usage-repro", original_response=response, ) ``` </details> <details> <summary>Before at 2d3c3e3098: /v1/responses reports zeros, control endpoints report real usage</summary> ``` curl -sS http://localhost:47913/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "Say hello in five words"}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ```json { "id": "resp_2fe68d15-194c-4129-ada8-8fe5b75adb0e", "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "object": "response", "output": [ { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld" } ] } ], "status": "completed", "usage": { "input_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_details": null, "output_tokens": 0, "output_tokens_details": null, "total_tokens": 0, "cost": null } } ``` ``` curl -sS http://localhost:47913/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "input": "Say hello in five words"}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ```json { "id": "resp_2d97f82d-b77e-44a8-a945-894a7cf3b996", "model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "object": "response", "output": [ { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld" } ] } ], "status": "completed", "usage": { "input_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_details": null, "output_tokens": 0, "output_tokens_details": null, "total_tokens": 0, "cost": null } } ``` ``` curl -sS http://localhost:47913/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "max_tokens": 64, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words"}]}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ```json { "id": "msg_28dd94f4-8df5-497c-9e1d-441b31cab61d", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld" } ], "model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "stop_reason": "end_turn", "usage": { "input_tokens": 12, "output_tokens": 10 } } ``` ``` curl -sS http://localhost:47913/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words"}]}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ```json { "id": "chatcmpl-b4f56270-ae32-49ac-a178-ad36c2910279", "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "object": "chat.completion", "choices": [ { "finish_reason": "content_filter", "index": 0, "message": { "content": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld", "role": "assistant" } } ], "usage": { "completion_tokens": 7, "prompt_tokens": 12, "total_tokens": 19 } } ``` </details> <details> <summary>After at e06e2e6c12: /v1/responses reports real usage for native and bridged models, control endpoints unchanged</summary> ``` curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:52741/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "Say hello in five words"}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ```json { "id": "resp_830b71b5-2aa2-4d48-bbf5-cd5913cc3f24", "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "object": "response", "output": [ { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld" } ] } ], "status": "completed", "usage": { "input_tokens": 12, "input_tokens_details": { "audio_tokens": null, "cached_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": null, "cache_write_tokens": 0 }, "output_tokens": 8, "output_tokens_details": { "reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": null }, "total_tokens": 20, "cost": null } } ``` ``` curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:52741/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "input": "Say hello in five words"}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ```json { "id": "resp_9d500821-ad5b-4b88-9afc-fbf0f7ccd788", "model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "object": "response", "output": [ { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld" } ] } ], "status": "completed", "usage": { "input_tokens": 12, "input_tokens_details": { "audio_tokens": null, "cached_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 12, "cache_write_tokens": 0 }, "output_tokens": 10, "output_tokens_details": { "reasoning_tokens": 0, "text_tokens": 10 }, "total_tokens": 22, "cost": null } } ``` ``` curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:52741/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "max_tokens": 64, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words"}]}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ```json { "id": "msg_cf458d37-a442-4fdd-aff4-c0eb0ca838a8", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld" } ], "model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "stop_reason": "end_turn", "usage": { "input_tokens": 12, "output_tokens": 10 } } ``` ``` curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:52741/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words"}]}' | python3 -m json.tool ``` ```json { "id": "chatcmpl-c8946773-1cc4-41ad-9403-89559d582194", "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "object": "chat.completion", "choices": [ { "finish_reason": "content_filter", "index": 0, "message": { "content": "Content flagged by policy, response withheld", "role": "assistant" } } ], "usage": { "completion_tokens": 7, "prompt_tokens": 12, "total_tokens": 19 } } ``` </details> Observations from the QA run, all pre-existing behaviors this PR leaves alone: - Blocked /v1/responses replies report usage.cost null - Blocked /v1/responses output items lack type, role, id, status - Blocked replies say status completed, not a refusal signal - Only /v1/chat/completions flags blocks via finish_reason content_filter ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(proxy): allow custom budget exceeded messages
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Budget errors expose exact spend and limits - Every client must replace the message independently How it solves it: - Adds a configurable client-facing budget error message - Preserves detailed values for logs and callbacks - Applies consistently across proxy budget enforcement paths ## User Flow Before: a developer receives internal financial limits when their assigned budget is exhausted 1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with their virtual key and chat messages 2. Below budget, they receive HTTP 200 with a `chatcmpl-...` ID and an answer 3. Once exhausted, the same request returns HTTP 429 with exact current spend and maximum budget 4. Their application must detect `error.type: budget_exceeded` and replace the message After: the same developer receives the administrator-defined message from every compatible client 1. The proxy admin sets `budget_exceeded_error_message` under `litellm_settings` 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with the same virtual key and chat messages 3. Below budget, they receive the same HTTP 200 response 4. Once exhausted, the request returns HTTP 429 with the configured message and `error.type: budget_exceeded` ## Relevant issues Fixes #36729 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Not captured locally because this checkout has no configured proxy runtime or provider credentials ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Full test suite was unavailable in the local Python environment ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the custom and default message behavior while preserving the budget error type and status
